# FIRST DEGREES

->C<-

**GOD**; virtue; the <term>Philosopher's Stone</term> <note>original: "Lapidem Philm."; the legendary substance capable of transmuting base metals into gold and granting eternal life</note> is most aptly designated philosophically through **Jasper** (on account of its greenness and blood-red color), not lacking in mystery; **Gold; EVERYTHING**; all these are granted in the <term>Oratory</term> <note>The place of prayer</note> and <term>Laboratory</term> <note>The place of chemical/alchemical work</note> by the **WISDOM OF GOD**. See verse 45: *All good things came to me together with her*, verse 291. Therefore, seek **WISDOM**, as much as it is better than Gold; and **PRUDENCE**, as much as it is more precious than Silver; seek them all the more ardently. Pecuniary riches (which are mere shadows and fleeting things like smoke) will profit the impious nothing; the treasures of iniquity will profit nothing on the day of vengeance: **WISDOM** is the tree of life: and Justice (which **ETERNAL WISDOM** incarnate—whose treasures are infinite and therefore inexhaustible—gives to us as a gift) alone delivers from death. Proverbs 10:2, 11:4. Psalm 49. Ecclesiastes 5:10. Zephaniah 1:13. Zechariah 9.

*Now.*] Having been warned so many times, invited by rewards, and enticed as if by charms. Just as the acquisition of Wisdom brings Glory, Life, and joy: so the contempt of Wisdom brings ignominy, death, and a perpetual mourning and roaring.

We are taught, moreover, by the Spirit of **WISDOM**, as much through living Masters, wise and experienced, granted to us by God; and through the silent ones, which are the books of the Wise, when the key of the Holy Spirit opens them; as by naked and solitary inspiration; or by secret revelation. A <term>Theosopher</term> <note>One who seeks direct knowledge of the divine</note> can thus learn the good Sciences, the secret Arts, the **Philosopher's Stone** and its proper name by which it is called among the common people, as well as the method of preparation—which two secrets of the Art are **EVERYTHING**. 

Therefore, whether Prince or Noble, lest you be a fool and called stupid in the sight of God and those truly Wise, and someday you repent of this foolishness, obey him who advises you well; (for *even a division of this is good*, <note>original Greek: "ἀγαθὴ γὰρ καὶ δαίρεσίς ἐστι ταύτης"</note> as Homer says in the *Iliad*, book 1.) Listen to the Teacher who strives to correct you **Theosophically**, and to regenerate you, as it were, from vices and errors. Juvenal, Satire 7.

# INTERPRETATIONS

->The gods willed that the Teacher hold the place of a holy Parent.<-
<note>original: "Dii Præceptorem sancti voluêre Parentis Esse loco."</note>

Alexander the Great is worthy of praise for saying, quite excellently, that he owed no less to his Teacher, Aristotle, than to his Father: for from his Father he had received the beginning of living, but from his Teacher the beginning of living well. Yet all of this depends upon the will of GOD. For it is not of the human who wills, nor of the one who runs by himself, but of GOD showing mercy (and going before us). "To will," says Paul in Romans 9:16 and 7:18, "is present with me; but how to perform that which is good I find not" (therefore, there is a need for GOD as a Co-worker). And a little later in verse 22: "For I delight in the Law of GOD according to the inward man: But I see another law in my members, warring against the Law of my Mind, and bringing me into captivity to the Law of sin which is in my members" (therefore, there is a need for GOD as the Perfecter). Thus GOD has co-operated from the beginning of the world, as in Ecclesiasticus 51:11. Thus Christ co-operated with the Apostles when they were sent into the whole world to preach the Gospel to every creature, and he confirmed their word with the signs that followed. Mark 16, last verse. Therefore, so that GOD may have mercy on you, implore the MERCY of the Merciful One with a faithful soul.

# INTERPRETATIONS

WISDOM calls all without discrimination, in verse 1. In the sight of GOD, the peasant is equal to the Noble: the reason is that both were redeemed from the power of the devil at one and the same price. This one is worth as much as that one. Indeed, not even by a <note>original: "μηδὲ γρῦ" (mēde gry), a Greek idiom meaning 'not even a syllable' or 'not the slightest bit'</note> grunt—that is, not in the slightest—is a Noble by birth alone better than a commoner who is upright and honest; even in this life, *Humility and virtue ennoble*. Do you know what true Nobility is? Hear Juvenal in his Satires, book 7: *Virtue is the sole and only nobility. It is fitting to rely on virtue, not on blood. Man is a contemptible thing unless he cares for virtue.* On account of lineage, riches, offices, and honors, a man is indeed superior or "greater," as he is called; but he is "better" only because of virtue. Even the lowest of the common people can be endowed with this; while the highest in Noble lineage may lack it. Regarding those who are Noble in name only, a certain Italian said not un-cleverly: *A nobleman is a beast, sitting upon a beast <note>a horse</note>, having a beast <note>a hawk or falcon</note> upon his hand; with beasts <note>hunting dogs</note> running all around him; chasing and pursuing a beast <note>the prey</note>.* O, what a fit description of those nobles! And of an unlearned King, King Alphonso said he was *a crowned ass*. And another, writing against the boasting that comes from riches, lineage, nobility, and offspring, sang thus:

-> *Though you be freeborn, and descended from famous parents,* <-
-> *Even so, you can still be a great beast.* <-
-> *Add the honor of a father, take for yourself famous relatives,* <-
-> *Even so, you can still be a great beast.* <-
-> *Let riches be yours; let your household goods be many and clean,* <-
-> *Even so, you can still be a great beast.* <-
-> *Finally, whatever you shall be, unless prudence is with you,* <-
-> *A great beast, I say, you will always be.* <-

Hear now whom GOD, the parent and author of nobility, wishes to ennoble, in 1 Samuel 2:30. *Therefore says the LORD GOD of Israel: I said indeed that your house and the house of your father should minister in my sight forever. But now the Lord says: Far be it from me; for whoever honors me, I will glorify him, but those who despise me shall be ignoble.*

You err, you err; the third and fourth figures of this *Amphitheater* will remind you of the higher things of WISDOM, through the practical fruits of <term>Cabala</term> <note>mystical interpretation of scripture</note>, <term>Magic</term>, and <term>Physico-Chemistry</term>.

The Philosopher rightly said: If GOD found a faithful heart, He would surely reveal the Science and the Art to it.

*Now]* After you have heard who, of what kind, and how great **I, WISDOM,** am. *Those who guard my ways.]* That is, those who keep or perform my commandments. You, says Christ, who is **WISDOM** incarnate in *John 15:14*, are my friends if **YOU DO** those things which I command you. And in the same book, *chapter 13:17*, **You will be blessed if YOU DO them.** *Luke 8:21:* **My mother and my brothers are these who hear the word of GOD and DO it.** To do what the **WISDOM OF GOD** has commanded is to walk in her ways. Therefore, let him who wants to acquire life amend his life, so that he may be clothed in life. Christ is the Archetype <note>the original model or perfect pattern of humanity</note>; he who knows Him, puts Him on, and imitates Him is Wise, Blessed, and truly Christian. It must be noted: although we must exist and live in the World while we remain in this skin <note>the physical body</note>, we must nevertheless flee and leave the "unclean world" daily. How is this done? If, I say, we do not cling to worldly impurities in our heart, words, or deeds—that is, if we do not live in a worldly way with the unclean world—then we are clothed in Christ and we imitate the Archetype through a <term>Theosophical life</term> <note>a life lived according to Divine Wisdom, from the Greek "theos" (god) and "sophia" (wisdom)</note>. This is to draw near to **GOD**. He who has drawn near is illuminated, joined, and united. It is necessary for one to become spiritual, good, and sublime in mind within the Spirit of the Best and Greatest [God], if he desires the company of good spirits, more sublime contemplations, and <term>deific union</term> <note>a mystical union where the soul becomes "God-like"</note>. For the conjunction and union happen between like things, not unlike things. To lose oneself in this way in the worldly "circumference" <note>the outer, material distractions</note> is to find oneself in the Center—that is, in **GOD**—and to find **GOD** within oneself. See verse 132. By this path of **WISDOM**, you withdraw from the world with Christ, even though you live and converse daily in the World, even in the midst of those living worldlily. You live not in a worldly way, but Theosophically in and with Christ. Christ conversed and ate with sinners, tax collectors, Pharisees, and heretics; you will be able to as well, provided it is not as an enormous sinner, tax collector, Pharisee, or heretic. Stay in the center: this is what that <term>Cabalistic</term> <note>referring to Jewish mystical tradition, though often used broadly in this era for "hidden spiritual truth"</note> saying means: *It is never so good to go out, that staying within is not better.* **O JEHOVAH**, stay in me, so that I may stay in You; and establish me as a <term>Christ-bearer</term> <note>original Latin: "Christophorum," meaning one who carries Christ within their soul</note>, so that I may emerge from the shallows of this unclean world, and having passed the rocks, I may stand with a joyful and firm foot in the harbor of salvation, safe, guarding Your ways. Amen.

63 ☞ **Better is WISDOM than strength: and a prudent man is better than a strong one.**

*Better is WISDOM, etc.* For it is the fountain of all Good, just as we are taught everywhere in this prologue by the Wise Man. See verses 45 and 327. And certainly Divine WISDOM excels all physical power: for by a single serious and pious prayer, great power is often broken. Thus Moses, with hands lifted high, broke the power of Amalek, Exodus 14:11 <note>The text cites Exodus 14:11, though the battle with Amalek is traditionally in Exodus 17.</note>. Jehoshaphat, with a single hymn, broke the strength of the sons of Ammon and Moab, and scattered their army, 2 Chronicles 20:22. How often did David break the ferocity of Saul and other enemies with his hymns? Those who understand the hidden <term>Nature of things</term> <note>Referring to "Physica" or natural philosophy, the study of the underlying laws of the universe.</note> can produce many such proofs, which the common people regard as miracles. History also testifies that many heroes were aided by natural strengths. But how often is victory or a cause won, or a people saved, through remarkable prudence? Was not Egypt saved by the Wisdom of Joseph? Persia by that of Daniel? The Israelite people by that of Moses? Here, certainly, Wisdom was better than strength.

[*You who hold authority, etc.*] <note>original: "Qui continetis, &c." Referring to those who hold sway over others.</note> As much in the Ecclesiastical and Scholastic state as in the Political. You, who rejoice to be called the interpreters and possessors of true WISDOM, and of her goods and gifts, in Universities, Academies, etc. You, I say, who hold authority—that is, who rule and govern—multitudes of youth; you (I say, and you yourselves say it, your titles of office bearing witness) are also Kings, that is, Rectors of peoples: and you, says the Wise Man, learn and teach WISDOM: not only from the fanatic ravings of certain unhealthy Heathens (among whom that trickster Aristotle is the prince and leader); but rather from the fountains of the books of Holy Scripture and of Nature, and from GOD himself, speaking within yourselves, you who are theosophically <note>Theosophy: "God-wisdom"; a mystical understanding of the divine through direct experience and spiritual illumination.</note> purified and divinely illuminated. Let not, therefore, the authority of a lying man reign in the Schools, but only the TRUTH of the Divine will, according to Holy Scripture, Nature, and your own upright consciences. *Multitudes*] One must not boast of a multitude of people, but of prudent administration, which is achieved by the help of wise men, who are able to bend the minds of men, win them over to you, and keep them in their duty; who can foresee useful things, anticipate damages, and drive away adversity through piety, virtue, prayer, and prudence.

<term>Ministers of His Kingdom</term>] From this it is clearly evident that Kingdoms belong to **GOD**, and are granted to princely persons for a time only. Since, therefore, O all you Kings and Princes, you are only ministers of **GOD** and of His Kingdoms; do not administer the Kingdom according to your own will, but according to the will of **GOD**, your **LORD**. The Justice of **GOD** is the will of **GOD**, which He searches out through the Spirit of **WISDOM**: if it is otherwise, you have not yet learned to judge rightly. 

<term>You have not judged rightly</term>] You have not taught rightly, you who are the slaves of certain Greek lies <note>A dismissive reference to the reliance on ancient Greek philosophers like Aristotle instead of biblical or mystical truth.</note>: you were and are the seducers and corrupters of tender youth. Oh, pestilential audacity! Therefore, having been warned by our Wise Man and by so many and such faithful, beloved interpreters of **WISDOM**, and having abandoned the falsehoods of certain unilluminated Heathens—leaving them behind the Caspian Mountains <note>A metaphorical "exile" for pagan ideas, suggesting they should be banished to the furthest edges of the known world.</note>—be converted at last to the truth. 

Pant for the Fountain of super-celestial **WISDOM** in a Theosophic, Christian-Cabalistic, Divine-Magical, and Physico-Chemical manner. According to the Laws and Doctrine of this **Amphitheater** <note>Referring to the author’s own work, "The Amphitheater of Eternal Wisdom."</note>, by **Praying and Working**, hasten to the universal [catholicon], the triune truth; hasten, I say, to the books of **Holy Scripture, Nature, and yourselves**, being regenerated by the method of repentance and illuminated by the ray of Theosophy. There, draw the ethereal liquid and drink to the full satisfaction of your minds. Search the veins of this fountain not in a Sophistical <note>Refers here to "Sophistry," or empty, deceptive logical wordplay.</note> way, but Theosophically: you will find there the Ore of **WISDOM**; and from this, living waters leaping up into Physical, Physico-Medical, Physico-Chemical, Physico-Magical, Hyperphysico-Magical, Ethical, Political, Cabalistic, and Theosophical truth; indeed, **ALL** truth. The *Christian Physics and Ethics* of Lambert Danæus <note>A prominent 16th-century Protestant theologian who attempted to create a system of science based on the Bible.</note> (to say nothing of the labors and writings of others on this subject) shall put the antagonists of Truth to shame. 

<term>The Law of Justice</term>] Divine Justice: placed within **Holy Scripture, Nature, and your Consciences** by God, being **triune**.

*O Tyrants*] He calls Kings and Princes "Tyrants" in a positive sense. <term>Tyrannos</term> <note>original Greek: Τύραννος</note>, Lord, or King: For as Trogus <note>Gnaeus Pompeius Trogus, a Roman historian.</note> says, *Kings, having been advanced to such a height of majesty by their moderation observed among good men, were called Tyrants on account of their strength.* <term>tyranneo</term> <note>original Greek: τυραννέω</note>, I rule. *Health of the whole world*] Many ask, why is the whole world steeped in wickedness? I respond, warned by the teaching of this passage: Because all places are full of fools; otherwise, the world would not be "un-world" <note>original: "mundus non esset immundus." A Latin wordplay: *Mundus* means both "the world" and "clean/ordered," while *immundus* means "unclean."</note>. For a multitude of the Wise is the health of the world. They chose it; let them have it. *A wise King, etc.*] Woe to the people, cries out Solomon (Ecclesiastes 10:16). Blessed is the Land whose King is Noble (in virtue), and whose Princes eat in their proper time, for refreshment and not for luxury. For the firm state of a people consists in the Wisdom and Prudence of the King; a weak state consists in the luxury of gluttons, whom excess destroys. Certainly, <term>a dry soul is most prudent</term> <note>original: "anima sicca, prudentissima." A philosophical maxim suggesting that a mind free from the "moisture" of sensory passions and drunkenness is most capable of wisdom.</note>. Take note of this, you who are mere jars of Bacchus <note>Followers of the god of wine; i.e., habitual drunkards.</note>; and correct this perverse way of living and drinking: **Otherwise you will drink yourselves into being fools, sick, and poor, and finally drink yourselves to the devil in the very depths of Hell.** <note>original German: "Sonsten sauffet ihr euch zu Narren/ kranck/ arm/ vnd endlich zum teuffel gar in die Helle."</note> (Verse 305).

# II.
## THE SECOND
### PROLOGETIC LEVEL
### EXPLAINED.

<margin>The Wise Man <note>Likely referring to Solomon, the traditional author of the Book of Proverbs.</note> teaches and warns that Wisdom and its fruit and its way must be sought, and that one must persevere constantly in it.</margin>

| 82 | **Hear, O sons, the Instruction of a Father: and attend, that you may know Understanding.** | Prov. 4 Verse 1. | ✍️ *Hear, O sons, the* **INSTRUCTION** *of a father, and attend, so that you may know* **PRUDENCE**. | 82 |

<gloss>Hear, O sons</gloss> The Wise Man shows here the legitimate way to happily attain **WISDOM** and its fruit, namely to hear the instruction of the Father, by which vicious desires are first corrected so that they may become capable of receiving divine light. For the more the flesh is tamed, the more the Spirit is enlightened. To hear the doctrine, and by hearing to obey, and by obeying to seek guidance from **GOD**, is the beginning of true **ILLUMINATION**.

**Sow in the morning, etc.**] Just as the sky of the Macro-Cosm <term>Macro-Cosmos: The "great world" or the universe as a whole</term> fertilizes the earth with morning and evening dew, and also refreshes the Micro-Cosm <term>Micro-Cosmos: The "little world," referring to man as a reflection of the universe</term>: so you, in the *morning*, should scatter the seed of pious prayers, and in the *evening*, the seed of Divine Praises. And just as the ancients said that the dawn <note>original: "auroram"</note> is a friend to the Muses; so you should establish the dawn as a friend to the good Angels. Prayer to GOD is a most fertile seed: liberality, beneficence, and alms are a most fruitful seed: works of charity are the most joyful seeds: the amendment of one's entire life is the best seed. You shall sow this seed-crop in the flower of youth, even unto the evening of old age, until the harvest of eternal life follows.

| Go to the ant, sluggard, see its ways, and be wise: | Proverbs 6 Verse 6. | ☞ *Go to the ant, O sluggard, and consider its ways, and learn WISDOM.* |

**Go to the ant**] Not to the ant alone, but also to any animal: for in each of these you will experience a spark of Wisdom or Prudence reflecting. Aventinus, in the *Annals of the Bavarians* <note>Johannes Aventinus (1477–1534), a Renaissance humanist historian</note>, proves with a lengthy story that the STORK is most devoted to marital chastity, so much so that if it happens to catch its own mate in adultery (which it can smell), it tears her and the chicks conceived in adultery by the mother into pieces. On the fidelity of DOGS, there exists a quite elegant poem in Phalaecian meter by Jacob Micyllus <note>A German Renaissance humanist and neo-Latin poet</note>, the beginning of which is:

> *Among the four-legged, the faithful dog,*
> *Among the four-legged, the dog is a pleasure,*
> *Among the four-legged, the dog knows,*
> *Venerates, and protects its Master, etc.*

See many excellent examples of the fidelity of dogs in Plutarch’s book *On the Industry of Animals*. The idea of faith, constancy, ferocity, beauty, and mildness...

<meta>This page continues the exploration of Divine Wisdom as reflected in the natural world, specifically focusing on the intelligence and "rational" behaviors observed in animals as evidence of the Creator's hand, following the previous discussion on light and the macrocosm.</meta>

# SECOND STAGE.

...in Adamantius, the most charming little dog of Julius Caesar Scaliger <note>A famous Italian scholar and physician (1484–1558)</note>, as his tomb shows, found in the first part of his master's poems. Nor is there a lack of examples of others, found almost everywhere. The ELEPHANT, the largest of land animals, is docile, mild, prudent, and possesses a strong memory; it is a <term>lover of humanity</term> <note>original Greek: "φιλάνθρωπον"</note> according to Pliny in Book 8 of his *Natural History*, and *Justus Lipsius* <note>A renowned Flemish humanist and philosopher</note> in his Letters, as contemporary experience also testifies. Indeed, trustworthy eyewitnesses know what proofs of greatness of spirit elephants have displayed in Antwerp, Lisbon, and Vienna in our time. The LARK <note>original: "Alauda"</note> takes its name among the learned from "praise" <note>original: "à laude"</note>, because it marvelously praises GOD and gives Him thanks for His gifts and good things. It has even been observed seven times that the bird flies on high and descends before taking a single grain from the earth for its food. Is this not a rational act, to praise GOD and give Him thanks? In this matter, they are far wiser than many inhumane men. Who taught the swallow to build such an artful home for itself? "Four things," says Agur, son of Jakeh (Proverbs 30:24, etc.), "are the smallest on earth, and they are wiser than the wise: the Ants, a weak people, who prepare their food in the harvest; the little rabbit <note>The Latin "lepusculus" refers here to the rock hyrax or coney mentioned in the Bible</note>, a powerless folk, who place their bed in the rock; the locust has no king, yet the whole swarm goes out in its ranks; the lizard <note>original: "stellio"</note> uses its hands to climb and stays in the palaces of kings." A great field is opened here for discussing the traces of Wisdom and Prudence in animals; however, for the present, these few examples shall suffice in place of many. I will add this: Plutarch felt that these things called <term>irrational animals</term> <note>original Greek: "ζῶα ἄλογα"</note> are actually <term>rational</term> <note>original Greek: "λογικά"</note>, that is, endowed with reason—he could have said that if they do not have it in full, they at least have certain sparks or atoms of reason and virtue. Lactantius <note>An early Christian author (c. 250 – c. 325)</note> also established this, and in our time William d’Oncieu <note>A French jurist and author known for his work on the mystery of numbers</note>, writing particularly on the mysteries of numbers, defends it. And all these men (in my judgment as well) felt correctly: for while a spark of Divine Wisdom shines in all animals—whether of the land, water, or air—they are not entirely irrational, but only lower than humans in their degree of prudence. For in humans, a far more abundant Wisdom reflects. I fear that if the gift of speech were granted by the Creator to certain animals (for not all humans are wise or prudent in equal degree), they might in some way satisfy those who cry out against them. The lack of vocal speech is made up for by the speech of their works and deeds. Let the judgment rest with the experienced. "The creature groans" in Romans 8:22; it does not do so for nothing. You object with that line from the Psalmist: *To whom there is no understanding* <note>Psalm 32:9</note>. That is certainly a weak point. Is not the same usually said of violent, angry, and fierce men, who are otherwise not lacking in reason? God is wonderful in His works; the whole universe speaks, confesses, and professes His Goodness, Omnipotence, and Wisdom (both specifically and universally), if only there were those who would observe God speaking through the <term>macrocosm</term> <note>The universe viewed as a complex, ordered whole</note> and understand Him.

| Nevertheless, it prepares its food in summer, and gathers its sustenance in the harvest. | It prepares food for itself in summer, and gathers what it might eat in the harvest. |

**It prepares in summer, etc.]** We are wisely taught, even by the ant, that one must work. Theosophically, it is **to Pray and to Labor wisely** <note>original: "Orandum & sapienter Laborandum"</note> for each of us. Therefore, Paul in Ephesians 4:28 commands that everyone should work with their hands at what is good, so that they may have something to give to those in need. This is the will of **GOD**, who detests idleness: *because idleness breeds vice. Idleness is the pillow of Satan.* In Ezekiel, among the sins of Sodom, idleness is also numbered, where in chapter 16:49 it reads: *This was the iniquity of Sodom: pride, fullness of bread, and abundance, and the idleness of her and her daughters: and they did not reach out their hand to the needy and poor. And they were haughty, and committed abominations: and I took them away, as you saw.* Idleness in this context is understood as a shameful cessation and vacancy; it is a pleasant evil, a decay of life, and a wasting sickness of all good things—not to be confused with that honorable and liberal leisure mentioned below at verse 170. Venerable Antiquity rightly teaches that "the hand must be moved along with Minerva" <note>A Greek proverb meaning one should act and work while also seeking divine help</note>: and indeed in summer, which is to say, at the opportune time. See verse 170. Therefore, do not delay the study and labors of true **WISDOM** until tomorrow, or for long: today, today Pray, learn, observe, and note down whatever the Spirit of Truth suggests to you theosophically. Today, today Work, and prepare the food of **WISDOM** for the body, Spirit, and Soul, you who are a student of <term>Christian Kabbalah</term> <note>The study of Jewish mystical traditions through a Christian theological lens</note>, <term>Physico-Magic</term> <note>The study of the hidden or "magical" powers within the natural, physical world</note>, and <term>Physico-Chemistry</term> <note>An early form of alchemical study focusing on the chemical properties of nature</note>. Weigh these things carefully in the balance of reason; from one task another is sown, until a labyrinth is born from which you may never be extricated. Therefore, follow good counsel, and do not delay good labors (both mental and manual) from day to day. *Whatever good you wish to do and labor at, do it quickly.* <note>original German: "Was du gutes thun und laboriren wilt/ das thue balde."</note> For *life is short, art is long.*

**Want and poverty]** This refers not only to a lack of bread, but even more to a lack of **WISDOM**, Prudence, and Understanding, as much in natural, artistic, and mechanical matters as in metaphysical and divine ones. # INTERPRETATIONS

This foolish harlot, painted with makeup and dressed in purple robes, ensnares many with her frauds and allurements. She cloaks her foolishness with grand titles and leads her followers through every degree of folly, right up to the final mask. <note>The "final mask" likely refers to the ultimate stage of deception or the point where the true, ugly nature of folly is revealed.</note> Regarding this, see more in verses 107 and 117.

*At the doors, etc.*] Just as the door of <term>Wisdom</term> <note>original: "Sapientia"</note> is truly the fear of **GOD** and constant prayer, so the door of the house of folly is ignorance of **GOD** and one's own imagination, which gets stuck in playful word-games and boastfully shows itself off. And just as the entrance halls of a house are usually beautiful and splendid, so the door of folly is decorated with grand, puffed-up words. *In a high place, etc.*] Even though worldly <term>wisdom</term> has nothing besides makeup and the charms of empty words, it has nevertheless built itself a seat in a high place of the city; that is, it wins for itself the reputation of <term>Wisdom</term>, carries people away into admiration of itself, and is worshipped by all as if it were some divinity, while true <term>Wisdom</term> is oppressed and hissed off the stage. This is just as the Scribes, Pharisees, and High Priests sat in a high place—that is, they held great authority—while Christ our Savior, who is the true <term>Wisdom</term>, was driven out.

*Stolen water, etc.*] All sciences that are not acquired through divine means—or through <term>Christian-Cabalistic</term> <note>original: "Christiano-Cabalicè"; refers to a Renaissance tradition that sought to find Christian truths within Jewish mystical traditions</note> and divine-magical ways through prayers and tears—are "stolen waters," not given by God. They are "sweet" because they are acquired without the mortification of the flesh, without true repentance, and without the true fear of **GOD**; thus they are sweet to the flesh. *Hidden bread*] That which is acquired by theft is not the bread of Wisdom and life by which the soul is nourished, but is the bread of worldly pleasure, and of trivial riches and honors; thus it is pleasant to the flesh, but lethal to the soul.

CHRIST, the God-Man <note>Greek original: *Theanthrōpos*</note> ☞, (the WISDOM OF GOD, made flesh for our sake) is a sure, and indeed most sweet brother, who is perceived in times of uncertainty. Is he not a great friend, who dies out of love for an enemy? In him, by faithfully imitating the Archetype <note>the original divine pattern</note>, we understand, are able to act, and obtain ALL THINGS, in a Christian-Cabalistic <note>relating to a mystical interpretation of scripture</note>, Physico-magical, Physico-Chemical, and Theosophical <note>referring to divine wisdom or hidden knowledge of God</note> manner. By WISDOM all were preserved who pleased the LORD from the beginning, verse 270. See the whole of chapter 10 of the Book of Wisdom. Furthermore: You have spoken excellently, brother, [in] Matthew 8:20: *The foxes have holes, and the birds of the air have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.* In me, I beseech you, lay your head: I am completely open to you: I am entirely yours: not so that you alone might rest, but that for me—in Body, Spirit, and Soul—there may be eternal rest through you (WHO ARE). Saint Augustine agrees with these thoughts of ours in his *Meditations*, chapters 7 and 8, saying: *I love you, my GOD, with a great love, and I desire to love you more; grant that I may love you always as much as I wish and as much as I ought, so that you alone are my entire focus and all my meditation. May I meditate on you through the days without ceasing, sense you in my sleep at night, may my Spirit speak with you, and my Mind converse with you. May my heart be illuminated by the light of your holy vision, so that with you as my leader and guide, I may walk from virtue to virtue, and finally see you, the GOD of Gods in Zion—now indeed through a glass darkly <note>original: "per Speculum in ænigmate"</note>, but then face to face, Amen. Bring forth, son of Learning, what I desire.*

# INTERPRETATIONS

*She has cast down many wounded* ] Many who have slept with this harlot—men of a character that was otherwise not at all wicked—were gravely infected by her subtle poison, as if by an epidemic plague. Only at the very end, in the agony of death, did they feel any relief. Many of the "strongest"—that is, those considered learned and most wise by their peers (though they were actually most foolish)—fell while lying in the darkness of such unwise "Wisdom." Having been lethally wounded, they expired miserably (innumerable examples are ready at hand). They perished in their vanities, and they remain lying buried in the abyss of darkness. Therefore, my son, learn from the example of another. *For happy is he whom the dangers of others make cautious.* <note>original: "Nam felix, quem faciunt aliena pericula cautum." A common Latin proverb derived from various classical sources.</note>

*The ways of hell, etc.* ] These lead back to the place from which they came. The ways of Divine Wisdom are straight, leading to heavenly and eternal things, penetrating the inner reaches of life. But the ways of hell are the ways of impiety, leading to the inner bitterness of death. The end of true and Divine Wisdom is life; the end of false and worldly wisdom is death. For that serpentine cunning <note>a reference to the serpent in the Garden of Eden</note> introduced death into the world, but Divine Wisdom (incarnated as the Son of GOD) gave life to the world.

*See to it that no one deceives you through Philosophy and empty deceit, according to the tradition of men, according to the elements of the world, and not according to Christ.* <note>Colossians 2:8</note> That is, through a Philosophy which lacks the breath of GOD and Divine illumination: one that leans upon its own fantastic and worldly prudence, rather than the light of truth found in the Books of Holy Scripture, Nature, and the Conscience—all written, handed down, and manifested by God. <insert>Those who speak perverse things</insert> in whatever field of knowledge. Whether he be a <term>Diabologian: a speaker for the devil, a play on the word "Theologian"</term>, or a <term>Perverter-of-Law: a pun on "Jurisperitus," one skilled in law</term>, a <term>Bad-Physician: a pun on the Greek "kakos" (bad) and the Latin for medical practice</term>, a Pseudo-Physicist, a Sophist, or anyone else substituting false things for right ones under a stained appearance of truth. 

Indeed, in every kind of status (about which every lover of Justice complains), such men hold the rudders of affairs everywhere today. It is such that among the Wise, in this age, it is hardly safe to purely profess the Doctrine of WISDOM. So much has the smoke of malice prevailed! For if there are any (born of the Gods) <note>original: "Diis geniti," a classical idiom for those of noble or divinely inspired nature</note> who dedicate themselves entirely to TRUTH, they are called insane, ignorant, irreligious, and sometimes even heretics. They are held in hatred; they face capital danger; they are afflicted with insults, and often deprived of the very use of this light [their lives]. These are the rewards for lovers of WISDOM in this filthy world. Since WISDOM incarnate—our head—was injuriously treated in this way, let us, the members, bear similar things patiently. For it is the highest happiness to suffer from the worst people for the sake of the Best. O times! O customs! <note>original: "O tempora! o mores!" a famous exclamation by Cicero</note> May GOD give these people enough rope and a final end. <note>original: "funem & finem." A play on words; "funis" is a rope or noose, suggesting they hang themselves with their own errors.</note> Amen, let every lover of <term>Theo-Sophia: "Divine Wisdom," from the Greek theos (god) and sophia (wisdom)</term> say so.

| <margin>114</margin> | Who leave the right path, and walk through dark ways. | <gloss>Verse 13.</gloss> | *Who abandon the straight paths and walk through dark ways.* | <margin>114</margin> |

*Who abandon, etc.*] Namely, they leave the true paths of WISDOM. Because of this, WISDOM in turn leaves them, and by the highest right delivers them over (as in Romans 1:28 and following) to a reprobate mind, so that they walk through dark ways and do those things which are not fitting. They are filled with all injustice (weigh these things, I pray, you who judge the Earth in the Ecclesiastical, Political, and Scholastic spheres), with fornication, craftiness, greed, and malice. They are full of envy, murder, strife, and deceit; they are endowed with bad character—whisperers, detractors, haters of GOD, insolent, proud, boastful, inventors of evil, and disobedient to parents. They are devoid of understanding, not at all tenacious of their covenants, far from the affection of charity, ignorant of any holy treaty, and merciless. 

Let every person (of whatever order, status, or faculty) rub his Conscience against this <term>Lydian Stone: a touchstone used since antiquity to test the purity of gold</term>. Let him examine his own acts and deeds, if he wishes and rejoices to be called a son of true WISDOM. These <term>SIGNATURES: outward marks or characteristics that reveal the inner spiritual reality</term> demonstrate more certainly than certainty itself that those who live this way know nothing firm, solid, or right; they only have "opinions." While they hold opinions, they are always learning and disputing, yet never arriving at the goal of truth. *For by too much wrangling—according to the proverb of Clodius and Varro—the truth is lost.*

*When they have done evil* <note>original: "Cum male fecerint"</note> ] When they have craftily substituted and defended the false for the true, the unjust for the equitable, the wicked for the lawful, and the fraudulent for the honest. For such people, Law and Justice, Truth and Conscience are nothing but public commodities and empty pursuit of glory among the unlearned and common crowd—those who value few things by the standard of truth, but many by the standard of opinion. Let those perish who turn white into black. *In the worst matters* <note>original: "In rebus pessimis"</note> ] Woe to them: for they commit a sin against the Conscience, which is not easily forgiven.

| Whose ☞ ways are perverse, and their steps are infamous. | Verse 15. | *Whose paths are perverse, and they are crooked in their ways.* | <margin>116</margin> |

*Perverse ways*] Ah, why not perverse? For they maliciously hold up the most ruinous masks of pride, <term>sophisms: clever but false arguments used to deceive</term>, lies, litigious reasoning or petty conclusions, deceptions, and falsehoods before the beautiful face of truth with a haughty brow. Because of this, their steps are truly infamous.

<margin>
The prostitution of both reason and mind, as well as the body, is to be avoided.
</margin>
<margin>117</margin>
| That you may be rescued ☞ from the foreign woman, and ☞ from the stranger, ☞ who softens her words. | Verse 16. | *That it may rescue you, I say, from the strange woman, from the foreigner, who smooths over her speech,* | <margin>117</margin> |
|----------|----------|----------|----------|

*From the foreign woman* <note>original: "A muliere aliena"</note> ] Here, the Wise Man does not simply treat of carnal <term>fornication: the author uses "scortatio" to mean both physical immorality and the "prostitution" of the intellect to false ideas</term>, but also that of the senses, of reason, and of the mind, as appears in verse 108. For just as wicked conversations corrupt good morals, so do false doctrines corrupt good minds. 

Worldly wisdom—which is fox-like, swollen, proud, litigious in dispute, bombastic, blathering sounds without meaning through a chatter of empty words, and through <term>logical trickery: the text uses "dialecticis præstigiis" to warn against the abuse of logic</term> (I distinguish, dear Reader, the true use from the abuse)—stretching out nets of seduction through the winding paths of sophisms, is that seductive, flattering, alien, and "foreign woman" (Proverbs 7). She is foolish and clamorous, and under a most lying title, she diabolically sells herself to fools as true **WISDOM**. Yet, according to Paul, there is no truer foolishness before **GOD** than earthly wisdom; it must be unlearned by him who truly desires to be wise. 

In matters of Philosophy, listen to the philosopher <note>Joannes Ludovicus Vives (1493–1540), a Spanish humanist and critic of traditional scholasticism.</note> Ludovicus Vives (who, as a master of his art, is to be believed), a man strong in age, learning, and experience. He says: "Those things which I thought were treasures in Philosophy during my youth with a haughty brow, now that I am changed and old, I see are scarcely better than dung, and were merely hindrances to a pious life and necessary studies." Thus he spoke. Even the Holy Fathers—Jerome, Ambrose, Augustine, Cyprian, Hilary, Basil, Cyril, Tertullian, Bernard, Prudentius, Isidore, and many other pious and learned men (of whom I could provide a lengthy catalog if time and place allowed, as their writings abundantly testify)—regretted not a little the labor they spent in handling secular philosophy, which is always litigious, heathen, and earthly. All of them, after many labors exhausted in that field, finally agree on this: that it is a plague to the truth, to solid knowledge, to the Law of **GOD**, and to the Religion of Christ. 

Flee, therefore, flee, O young men, from the harlot: and, following the example of the Emperor Maximilian I...

# ->THE THIRD LEVEL<-

Those who philosophize in a pagan or profane manner: listen to them as you would listen to frogs, not as you would listen to nightingales. Let him who can understand (if the devil does not hinder him) understand and amend his ways. *From the foreign woman* <note>original: "Ab extranea"</note> ] Meaning a stranger, a Greek <note>In this period, "Greek" was often shorthand for pagan philosophy, specifically that which relied on human reason rather than divine revelation.</note>, a liar, who is not proven by the internal testimony of the Holy Spirit. The reason is that Wisdom is not acquired through the false and decked-out words of Rhetoric, nor by the twists and turns of <term>syllogisms: logical arguments where a conclusion is drawn from two premises</term>, with which this Foreigner lures the small and the unwary into her love (alas, a shameful and harlot-like love!). Instead, Wisdom is acquired by the Light of a mind divinely illuminated—inspired by God <note>original: "Enthusiasticè"</note>—falling upon the intellect and moving the free will to belief. This is the most noble way of knowing all things. *Who softens her words* <note>original: "Quæ mollit sermones suos"</note> ] Through Logic and Rhetoric. Seneca says: *A honeyed poison is a flattering speech. He who believes easily is easily deceived.* Therefore, Cicero rightly said: *The strength and sinews of Wisdom consist in not being easy to believe.* And Euripides: *Nothing is better or more useful to men than a prudent distrust.* Learn now, therefore, O mortals, by the warnings of so many great men, to beware of this woman; do not imitate the error of those wandering in the heat of youthful ignorance, but rather follow the repentance of those who grew wiser with age.

Even today, He invites and calls. *The covenant of her GOD, etc.* ] Following the example of her Father, that is, the devil, who did not remain in the truth (John 8:44), of whom she is a most obedient daughter. All who join and unite themselves with her in marriage desperately forget the covenant of their GOD; they become the sons-in-law of the devil and have as their mother-in-law the enemy of GOD, of the Creature, of Nature, and of the entire human race. which you may see in the second Figure of this Amphitheater <note>The "Amphitheater" refers to Khunrath's famous engraved plates, which were designed to be meditated upon alongside the text.</note>. He who walks clothed <term>Theosophically: through the knowledge of God and divine things</term> <note>original: "Theosophicè"</note> in the ten garments of Regeneration is UNITED WITH GOD: these garments lead the Magi of the Cabalists <note>original: "Cabalistarum"</note> coming from the East (as in verse 170) successfully to the fountain of life and the ocean of WISDOM, guided by the shining star of WISDOM that has risen in both the Microcosm and the Macrocosm <note>The "Microcosm" is the human being, seen as a miniature universe; the "Macrocosm" is the great universe itself.</note>.

*That you may walk in the good way]* The good way is the way of wisdom, justice, sanctification, redemption, truth, and life, as noted in 1 Corinthians 1:30. And all the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth, according to Psalm 25:10. The good way is the path of humility, gentleness, constancy, silence, faith, charity, hope, and patience. In John 8:31, Incarnate WISDOM said to those Jews who believed in him, *If you remain in my word, you will truly be my disciples, and you will know the truth; and the truth will set you free.* Therefore, I advise you to remain in the word of WISDOM, so that you may be a disciple of WISDOM—the most faithful teacher who knows not how to deceive. May you know ALL TRUTH, in both the Physical and the hyper-physical <note>metaphysical or spiritual realms</note>, just as you walk in divine things, O Cabalist, Magus <note>a seeker of natural and divine mysteries</note>, and <term>Physico-Chemist: one who studies both the physical properties of nature and the spiritual art of alchemy</term>, in the good way: and may you be freed from error and wandering by the teaching of truth. *The paths of the just]* These are the examples of virtues and piety, and especially the imitation of the life of Christ our Savior. Whence the Apostle says in 1 Corinthians 11:1, *Be imitators of me, as I am of Christ.* One must walk this path in the <term>Oratory and Laboratory: the dual workspace of the alchemist, combining prayer (oratory) with physical experiment (laboratory)</term>. Indeed, this very path is shown to you synoptically in this Amphitheater, and in the Prologue through those seven steps which lead us to the innermost chambers of the only true, eternal Wisdom.

See how intimately the Wisdom of GOD has joined itself to you, and prepared for itself a dwelling place out of human nature, in which the whole fullness of the Godhead might dwell. Ah, why do you throw yourself into the bosom of a harlot (the unclean, worldly wisdom), when the heavenly virgin has long since begun to love you to distraction—she who is pure, chaste, unstained, and full of graces, gifts, and immortal benefits. # OF THE SECOND STEP.

*The ways of man, etc.* <note>Reference to Proverbs 5:21: "For the ways of man are before the eyes of the Lord, and he considers all his paths."</note>] When your mind hungers for worldly things—honors, pleasures, wealth—your ways are perverse, and you stray from the **HIGHEST GOOD** <note>original: "SUMMO BONO," a philosophical term referring to the ultimate state of happiness or God.</note>. *He considers his steps*] Your pursuits, counsels, schemes, snares, cunning, and foolish desires are your "steps," which the Lord considers; the Angels watch them; your conscience accuses and observes them; and the devils count them. **GOD**, who searches the hearts and kidneys <note>In biblical language, the "kidneys" or "reins" represent the seat of the most secret emotions and hidden thoughts.</note> of all, and understands every thought of the mind (1 Chronicles 28:9), loathes the depravity of the heart and hands it over to be punished (unless you repent) by avenging creatures, which execute vengeance upon all whom **GOD** loathes. Moreover, the greatest misery—indeed, Hell itself—is to be abandoned by **GOD**.

<margin>124</margin>
| | | |
|:---|:---:|:---|
| His own iniquities will seize the wicked man himself, and he will be held by the cords of his sin. | Verse 22. | *His own iniquities will seize the wicked, and he is bound by the ropes of his sins.* |

*Iniquities*] Every iniquity inflicts punishments and lashes upon itself: there is no vice that does not give birth to its own peculiar disease. For just as virtue itself is its own most beautiful reward, so every vice is its own worst reward. For every seed produces its own fruit. The fruit of mercy is mercy; the reward of kindness is kindness; and conversely, the fruit of unmercifulness is unmercifulness and cruelty. *He is bound by the cords of sins*] Sin is certainly the greatest slavery and captivity, binding the wicked man so tightly that he cannot escape punishment. Divine Wisdom is a noble freedom, which liberates the mind of man from the chains of folly, from the errors of darkness, from the lashes of vice, and from the snares of despair.

<margin>125</margin>
| | | |
|:---|:---:|:---|
| He himself shall die, because he did not have **DISCIPLINE**, and in the multitude of his folly he will be deceived. | Verse 23. | *He himself shall die, because he did not hear instruction: and because of the multitude of his folly he will go astray.* |

*He will go astray*] The human mind, when not illuminated by the light of Divine Wisdom, is so full of errors that not even its smallest actions are free from mistake. If it looks toward **GOD**, it errs; if it looks at Nature, it raves; if at itself, it is mistaken; if at its neighbor, it is deceived. In short: it cannot look upon the smallest star in the Heaven, nor a tiny herb of the earth, without error; because all its thoughts are errors. This is truly the "multitude of folly," which can bring nothing other than death and destruction with it. For man has fallen from the fountain of Light into the abyss of darkness, from which he can by no means struggle out, unless he has divinely obtained the Spirit of Wisdom.

**Your HEART]** Wisdom has its seat in the Heart: therefore, beware lest foolish wisdom <note>original: "fatua sapientia," referring to worldly or deceptive cleverness as opposed to divine truth.</note> occupy and fill this seat. For that ancient serpent blinds the mind and instills his poison through many traps: he pollutes the heart with lust, puffs it up with pride, inflames it with anger, and ravages it with hatred—all of which are the works of the devil. See to it that you guard your **HEART** from this poison: preserve it, however, and open it to Heavenly Wisdom, the fear of **GOD**, uncorrupted faith (which purifies the heart), unfeigned charity, unshaken hope, unbroken patience, and the most lovely humility. Let your **HEART** be a workshop of prayer and petitions, an instrument of most holy groans, and a dwelling place of piety.

And because they cast aside true **WISDOM**, and its beginning, the **FEAR OF THE LORD**, they cannot **Pray Theosophically** <note>original: "Theosophicè Orare." Khunrath's term for prayer that combines divine study with spiritual labor.</note>, nor **Work** wisely and with fruit. Note this, you who seek the **Philosophers' Stone** <note>original: "Lapidem Philm.," an abbreviation for Lapidem Philosophorum.</note>, and who aspire to understand, know, possess, and perform those things **Caballistically, Magically, Chemically, Theosophically, etc.**, which are wisely noted in the fourth figure of this **Amphitheater**: Learn first, I say, to treat yourselves **Theosophically** in such a way that (with **GOD** showing mercy, giving, and working) you may be untangled, drawn out from the filth of sins, and freed from the excesses of impurities—dissolved, separated, purified, joined (O abyss of the mystery of **GOD**! In this point of Divine union, it is not of him who wills or runs by himself, but of **GOD** who shows mercy. **The Infinite! The Infinite!** <note>original: "En-soph! En-soph!" A Hebrew term from the Kabbalah referring to the Divine origin or the Infinite God before His self-manifestation.</note>)—to a degree of more-than-perfection (by the **Divine** artifice of the **Divine** fire) may you be sublimated, that is, exalted, and be mentally fermented with **GOD** himself in Spirit and Truth; before, I say, you attempt to dig out the **Philosophers' Stone** and the other treasures of **WISDOM** from the Mine of **WISDOM**, which is the true Universal **MAGNESIA** <note>term: Magnesia. In alchemy, this is not the chemical magnesium, but the "Prima Materia" or the primordial substance from which the Stone is made.</note> of the **Theosophers**. Otherwise (believe one who speaks the truth) **you will be washing an Ethiopian and a brick** <note>original: "Æthyopem & laterem lauabitis," a classical idiom for attempting an impossible or futile task.</note>. These are, were, and always shall be the **Goods and Gifts of GOD**, which this **Amphitheater** of ours deals with, depending on **GOD** alone: who, being sublime, glorious, and filled with all Justice and Goodness, bestows or withdraws from whom he wills. Note: **MAN** is the **Brick** to be whitened, and the **Body** which stands; **GOD** is the **Soul** which gives life; the **HOLY SPIRIT** is the bond, by whose power the **UNION** is made; who tints and gives entry to the perpetual **Kingdom**. O wonderful **Regenerative** harmony of the **Macro- and Micro-Cosm**! No one unless they are a student of regeneration, and indeed by the singular guidance of **GOD**, will understand these **Regenerations**: to all others they are like the Bohemian forests <note>Bohemian forests: At the time, these were famously dense, dark, and easy to get lost in; a metaphor for impenetrable confusion.</note>, wandering and dark.

## OF THE THIRD STEP.

Because it conquers every subtle thing and shall penetrate every solid thing. <note>This is a famous phrase from the Emerald Tablet of Hermes Trismegistus, describing the power of the Philosopher's Stone.</note> It animates ALL things, gives them life, moves them wisely, and preserves them powerfully. If you knew NATURE theosophically—which all the ancients and orthodox Fathers most truly and piously affirmed to be "through Paul" <note>original: "διὰ Παύλω"; Khunrath likely refers to the Apostle Paul’s teachings that God is revealed through his creation (Romans 1:20).</note>, that is, the voice of GOD—both in the abstract and the concrete, universally and particularly; then you would know (believe one who speaks the truth) the PERPETUAL MOTION of the Wise. I refer you to verse 154 and 178, and to the definition and explanation of the third figure of this Amphitheater, the Philosopher's Stone. Remember to study there: praying to GOD that, as a theosophic co-worker, He may inspire and show the truth to you. I have known many in the courts of rulers seeking a perpetual motion of wood or steel, etc., mechanically (alas, in vain). If they had investigated the MOST HOLY SCRIPTURE, NATURE, and THEMSELVES theosophically, physically, and physico-medically, etc. (as shown in the 2nd and 3rd figures of this Amphitheater), they would indeed have found a MOTION not only perpetual, but also Eternal, Divine, and Natural, in both Worlds of the Wise. <note>The "two worlds" refer to the Macrocosm (the universe) and the Microcosm (man).</note> The vain common folk do not perceive this UNIVERSAL REMEDY <term>Catholicon: a universal medicine or elixir sought by alchemists to cure all diseases and perfect all matter.</term>, the only true one, being hindered by a spirit of seduction. The blind lead the blind, wherefore their labors are in vain. The Sophists <note>Here, false or superficial philosophers.</note> show a motion that must be moved, not one that is itself the mover.

### INTERPRETATIONS

<margin>98</margin>
Our mind is in the heavens: it is not (believe me) the work of a single day. We must migrate step-by-step from evil to Good; from the corporeal to the Spiritual; from the things of the senses to the things of the Mind; from the earthly to the Divine, if we wish to be capable of receiving those things which are Good, Spiritual, and Divine. There are steps to these ascents. See verse 218. **She herself goes about, etc.**] This means she searches everywhere, wherever on earth, in every time and place, to see if anyone can be found who truly takes true **WISDOM** to heart, so that she may signify and declare her concern and benevolence toward her faithful, beloved lovers in reality—that is, by communicating her infinite treasures to them. See verses 142, 144, 160. If you seek **WISDOM**, you will be sought and magnetically attracted by her in turn: you will find and you will be found. <note>original German: "Wie man sich gegen sie erzeigt und verhält / also sie auch hinwiderumb."</note> *As one behaves and conducts oneself toward her, so she does in return.* **In the ways.**] What are these ways? They are none other than the Books of Holy Scripture, of Nature, and of our own Mind when it has been <term>Christianly purified</term> <note>Referring to the process of repentance and spiritual refinement (verse 61).</note>. In these ways of **WISDOM**, I say, while we are walking wisely—if we pray <term>Theosophically</term> <note>Seeking direct divine knowledge through prayer and meditation on nature.</note>, and if we work wisely—**DIVINE WISDOM** shows herself to us in a wonderful and miraculous manner. See verse 48. **In every thought, etc.**] That is, in their opinions, their feelings, and their concepts of the mind, which are kindly grasped and informed. For the word used here is *to imagine* <note>Greek: φαντάζεσθαι (*phantazesthai*), meaning to form a mental image or representation.</note>, which means *to imagine, and to give form to something within the thought and mind*. Thus, **WISDOM** says that she dwells within their minds and thoughts in such a way that she may show and communicate herself to them in a friendly manner. The person who sees **GOD** is the one to whom **GOD** appears; to whom He offers Himself to be seen; to whom the **WISDOM OF GOD** represents herself. This does not happen in a common way, but through the Holy Scripture, Nature, and the mirror of the Mind when it has been theosophically washed and cleansed. Verse 336. The Divinity that flourishes in man is immense and cannot be valued enough; for man, being superior in reason, rules over the Creatures (by the will and command of **GOD**) in such a way that he does not merely use what is present for his needs, but also wanders through remote and secret things, using and enjoying his Spirit and genius <note>The guiding spirit or natural talent</note> under the guidance of **GOD**. And indeed, it is worthy of wonder what an experienced and learned age can bring forth! Indeed, what that Reason and <term>the Word</term> <note>Greek: ὁ λόγος (*ho logos*), referring to both human reason and the Divine Reason/Christ.</note> may build within this mortal little worm! To whom He has given all eternity and the ability to know the breadth, height, and depth of the entire worldly machine: so that by knowing the created things, he may observe the Creator, and may hear and understand this <term>Metaphysical peak</term>, the living principle of the rational mind. Let him grasp this whole self through reason; let him cultivate it with the mind, and let him breathe that very thing with sensible vigor: let whatever he is, be for this. And finally, having left behind a merely shrewd human philosophy, let him strive to <term>return to the Father's home</term> <note>Latin: *patrizare*, meaning to take after one's father or return to the fatherland.</note>. For all things which He had made were very good. May **GOD** grant it, and let every lover of **WISDOM** say, Amen.

# THE THIRD STEP

or <term>Sophistry</term> <note>The use of clever but false arguments, which Khunrath contrasts with true spiritual wisdom.</note> (verse 118), the genuine daughter of the devil; I love **WISDOM** (by the command of the Wise Man in verse 106, and by the invitation of **WISDOM** herself), and so do I: and so that **SHE** may love me in return, and that I may never fail in my love for her, grant this to me graciously, O **JEHOVAH**, Amen. Oh, the wondrous Art of Divine Love, unknown to the impure world! Happy is he who tastes the cup of the lovers of **WISDOM**; most happy is he who is intoxicated by it. *And I sought her, etc.*] In the morning; in the Summer; from my earliest age; from my youth, in which the love of **WISDOM** and the study of her took fire in my soul. But how? <term>Theosophically</term> <note>In the tradition of Theosophy, seeking direct, divine knowledge through the union of the soul with God and the study of nature.</note>, according to the Laws and Doctrine of this <term>Amphitheater</term> <note>Khunrath refers here to his own book, "The Amphitheater of Eternal Wisdom."</note>. Proverbs 28:5. Begin, I beseech you, you mystical bedfellow <term>Abishag the Shunammite</term> <note>In the Bible, Abishag was the young woman brought to keep the aging King David warm; here, she represents the spiritual warmth Wisdom brings to the soul.</note>, to lie in my bosom: may you warm my mind with holy fervor, and cherish my cold limbs with your embraces, my little Soul! Divine **WISDOM** embraces the forms of all things, which vie with one another in beauty. For who, I ask, can sufficiently contemplate the beauty of God the Father? Who can sufficiently marvel at that one who is "beautiful in form above the sons of men"? Who can sufficiently love the joyful little flame of the Holy Spirit, which gives life to all things?

The beauty of Wisdom is splendor in the Angels, brightness in the Stars, whiteness in the Heavens, light in the Air, greenness on the Earth, clarity in the Water, color in the Flowers, proportion in Animals, grace and figure in Man, reason in the Soul, and faith in the Faithful. Who, then, would not choose her for a bride, unless they were the most foolish of all? Who would not be captured by her beauty? Wherever you turn, she shows her face to you, whether you contemplate heavenly or earthly things. But to gaze upon the internal beauty and form of things: this, at last, is the bedchamber of Wisdom; this is the intimate kiss of this Bride. Open to me, therefore, my sister, my beautiful one; show me your genuine face, not merely the external form and beauty of things, but the internal and most intimate; for you do not truly love me unless you open your heart to me.

# THE THIRD STAGE.
### I

...fixed or placed. <term>I was brought forth <note>original Latin: Parturiebar</note></term>] Conceived as a Divine Conception, so also brought forth or born in a birth that is imperceptible to us, and therefore inexpressible; Divinely begotten. <term>En Sof <note>original: Ensoph. Experts and craftsmen believe anyone skilled in their own art: the Pythagoreans rested upon their *he himself said it* <note>original Greek: αὐτὸς ἔφα (autos epha)</note>; the <term>Kabbalists <note>original Hebrew: Meckablim</note></term>, in their saying *the Sages have said* <note>original Hebrew: emoru Hachamim</note>; so you, who profess yourself a Christian, follow the Christians' command to *believe* <note>original Greek: πίστευσον (pisteuson)</note>: believe in whom? <meta>This page continues the commentary on the "autobiography of Wisdom" from Proverbs 8, specifically focusing on verse 28 regarding the "establishment of the clouds/aether." -># INTERPRETATIONS<-

<page-num>66</page-num>

*[When] he established the aether above]* <note>original Latin: Æthera firmabat sursum, from Proverbs 8:28.</note>] When he established the aetherial Spirit—that is, the Heaven (Genesis 1:1)—and constituted the <term>Firmament <note>The "expanse" or solid dome mentioned in Genesis, believed to separate the waters of the sky from the waters of the earth.</note></term> by solidifying it through his Word (Genesis 1:6). Regarding the nature of Heaven, consult the third part of this *Amphitheater* <note>Referring to Heinrich Khunrath's *Amphitheatrum Sapientiae Aeternae* (Amphitheater of Eternal Wisdom), the work this manuscript likely accompanies.</note>, Question 5 and verse 261. 

Therefore, let the vanities of certain "know-it-alls" vanish; those who fabricate stories that the entire **NATURE** of the whole Worldly machine is not so vigorous, healthy, unharmed, and strong in our times as it was in the age of our ancestors or fathers. [They claim] that the Heaven, by falling, has lowered itself by 8,000 miles; that the Sun, Moon, and Stars have lost much of their original light; that herbs, flowers, fruits, etc., and the animals of land, water, and air are not of such power, efficacy, or operation today as they were a hundred or a thousand years ago. Indeed, [they claim] that Nature is still being totally weakened by old age from day to day, and that its strength is being broken because of our sins. A grand statement, if only it were true! 

If you understood, my Lords, the **NATURE OF NATURE** <note>original: NATVRÆ NATVRAM. A philosophical concept referring to the underlying creative principle or the essence of the natural world.</note>—that is, what it is, what its Being is, and the greatness and quality of its Law, by whom it was implanted in the Creature and for what use—you would speak differently. As far as the Heaven is concerned, tell me, I pray: have you ever observed a circumference, firmed in a circle, fall toward the center? Do you not read: *By the word of the Lord the heavens were made firm, and all their power by the spirit of his mouth* (Psalm 33:6)? And, *Let there be a Firmament:* and *God called the firmament Heaven* (Genesis 1:8). If it had fallen, what kind of "firmament" would it be? A remarkable one, surely! This is such a distinguished firming of the heavens by the Word of the Lord! Oh, you know-it-alls! 

God said, moreover: *Let there be lights in the firmament of the Heaven, and let them divide the day and the night: and let them be for signs and seasons, and days and years: that they may shine and illuminate the earth.* And it was done so. And God made two great lights: the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night, and the stars (Genesis 1:14 ff.). Is this not the power of the Heavens, firmed by the Spirit of the mouth of **JEHOVAH**? Who of sound mind will deny that the Sun, Moon, and Stars divide the day and night, serve as signs and seasons, days and years, shine and illuminate the earth, and rule the day and night just as well today as they did a thousand years ago? Where the fact itself speaks, what need is there for further proof? 

The **VOICE OF GOD** [said]: *Let the earth bring forth green grass, and the seed-bearing herb, and the fruit-bearing tree making fruit according to its kind, whose seed is in itself upon the earth.* [And]: *Let the waters bring forth the creeping thing of a living soul, and the winged creature above the Earth under the firmament of Heaven.* [And]: *Let the Earth bring forth the living soul in its kind, cattle and creeping things, and the beasts of the Earth according to their species.* This Voice of God, I say, in Genesis 1, was fulfilled. Produced by the Divine Blessing, **INCREASE AND MULTIPLY**, and being animated and strengthened, they have grown and multiplied from the beginning of the World. They grow and multiply today; they will grow (by the vigor of the Law implanted by God once and for all) and multiply until the renewal of the whole World through **FIRE**. **THE WORD OF THE LORD** remains forever (Isaiah 40:8). *So shall my word be*, says **JEHOVAH** (Isaiah 55:11), *which goes out from my mouth: it shall not return to me void, but it shall do whatever I have willed, and it shall prosper in those things for which I sent it.* Therefore, grass still grows today just as well as it did a thousand years ago. <note>original German: Wächst derentwegen heutiges Tages noch gleich also gut Graß / als vor tausendt Jahren.</note> Tell me, I pray, what is this? *Heaven is my throne, but the Earth is my footstool* (Isaiah 66:1).

# INTERPRETATIONS

**[HE] WAS, AND [HE] WHO WILL BE.** So also in the Lord’s Prayer: **Our Father, WHO ART in the heavens.** <note>original Latin: *Pater noster, QVIES in cælis*. The author likely uses "QVIES" as a variant or pun on "qui es" (who art), suggesting a divine "rest" or "stillness" in the heavens.</note> So elsewhere incarnate **WISDOM**, **JESUS CHRIST, I AM,** *the Way, the Truth, and the Life.* And, *Before Abraham,* **I WAS.**

This Cabalistic <term>Cabalistic <note>Referring to Christian Kabbalah, a Renaissance tradition that sought to uncover divine mysteries in the Hebrew Bible and the names of God.</note></term> point, by no means to be despised, will be treated more fully in its own place (God willing) in the **Amphitheater of Eternal WISDOM**, the only true [Wisdom], etc., explained in the exposition of the name of **GOD, EHIEH**, <note>The Hebrew name of God meaning "I AM."</note> in the first figure.

Cease now, you slanderer, from your most destructive delusions, denying both the Divinity and the eternity of **WISDOM** (who was incarnated in time).

**I WAS, EHIEH**, that is, **GOD, THE WISDOM OF GOD**, composing all things.

Note: What our wise man <note>Referring to Solomon, the traditional author of Proverbs.</note> says here about **WISDOM**, the same is said in **John chapter 1** regarding the **WORD. The WORD**, therefore, made flesh, and the **WISDOM OF GOD** incarnated in the world, are **THE SAME: GOD, THE SON OF GOD, WAS, IS, WILL BE**, from eternity to eternity. What, O impious one, do you say to this? Whatever exists before the World was created is **GOD**: **WISDOM** exists before the World was created, therefore **WISDOM** is **GOD**.

Hence **John the Evangelist**, having learned from the Wise Man that the **WORD** was already there in the Beginning, immediately infers that He was with **GOD**, who alone exists before the Beginning. And because whatever exists before the Beginning is necessarily **GOD**, he rightly infers also that the **WORD** is **GOD** Himself: lest anyone suspect there are two **GODS**. The Start or Beginning of creation excludes everything created before it. For it is the Beginning of the created.

However, **GOD**, to whom the **WORD** belongs, did not create his own **WORD** (through which He created all things in the Beginning); otherwise, it would not have been before the Beginning.

What then? From Himself **GOD** begat **GOD from GOD**, eternal from eternal: for nothing else can now be imagined. Let it vanish now and return into nothingness—that which existed before nothingness—this fanatical, heretical, blasphemous, and most pestilential voice of the **Arians** <note>Arians followed the teachings of Arius, who argued that Jesus Christ was a created being and not co-eternal with God the Father.</note>: *There was once* (namely a time, or eternity, or whatever Arius wished or was able to imply) *when (the Son of GOD) was not yet.*

This adamantine <term>adamantine <note>Unbreakable or diamond-like; used to describe an argument that cannot be shattered.</note></term> argument against all **Antitrinitarians**, drawn from the Book of Nature, **Macro- and Micro-Cosmically**, <note>The "Macrocosm" is the great world (the universe) and the "Microcosm" is the little world (the human being).</note> is shown to you by the doctrine of the most invincible physical **Professor of GOD** in this world; explaining the great Book of Nature **Physico-Chemically**; <note>Combining the study of physical nature with spiritual and laboratory alchemy.</note> so that you may perceive the triune **CREATURE** universally and particularly to confess, represent, and teach the **TRIUNE ELOHIM** <note>ELOHIM is a plural Hebrew name for God, used here to support the doctrine of the Trinity.</note> (who in the Beginning created the Heaven and the Earth, etc. **Genesis 1**).

Furthermore: **BODY, SPIRIT, SOUL**, from which **MAN** consists, sufficiently express the Divine triune likeness, according to which triune Man was made. I distinguish between Likeness and Image.

**THE SUM: ALL THINGS ARE TRIUNE**; because they were made by the **TRIUNE**.

This is the wondrous voice of **GOD** in Nature through the Creature. See the third figure of this Amphitheater, proposition 1, distinction 7.

**I was delighted]** **JEHOVAH HEA** <note>A mystical name for God combining the Tetragrammaton with a feminine or pronoun-based ending.</note> was delighted and is delighted in turn, that is, in the Son; in whom **HE** (**HU**, <note>Hebrew for "He" or "He-ness."</note> that is, **THE SAME, HE**; which **Capnio** <note>The pseudonym of Johann Reuchlin (1455–1522), a famous scholar of the Hebrew language and Kabbalah.</note> numbers among the names of **GOD** in **book 2 of *The Mirific Word*, chapter 16**) has delight from eternity to eternity.

Concerning this [Wisdom] incarnate there stands the testimony of the Father, **Matthew 17:5: THIS IS my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear him.**

Let us therefore hear the **Son of GOD**, what he says of himself (by the will and mandate of the Father, who sent him for our sake) in his word written Biblically, **Macro- and Micro-Cosmically**; not Arius, nor the Fanatics <note>original: *Swermeros* (German: *Schwärmer*), a derogatory term for radical reformers or "enthusiasts" who claimed direct spiritual revelation outside of church or reason.</note>...

# INTERPRETATIONS #

**THE FEAR OF THE LORD** hates evil, etc. <note>original: "TIMOR DOMINI odit malum," quoting Proverbs 8:13</note>] Why? Because the **LORD**, whom one fears (as **LORD**), is **GOOD**: he hates arrogance and pride; because he fears the Greatest, the Eternal, the Terrible, and the Strong: he hates the crooked way; because he fears the All-seeing, the Jealous, and the Just: he detests the double-tongued mouth; because he fears the Best, the only Wise, and the Truthful: and so **THE FEAR OF THE LORD IS THE BEGINNING OF WISDOM**, which is to enjoy **JEHOVAH**, the Long-suffering, the Merciful, and the one of great Kindness. It is well for the man who fears the **LORD**. For to this believer nothing is impossible, because the **LORD** fulfills the will of those who fear him (Psalm 145:19).

## INTERPRETATIONS

...then, of the Eternal and Infernal things, the most profound, most hidden, most secret, inscrutable and ineffable CAUSE, Origin, Seat, Source, and Recess, producing wonderful effects, which cannot be comprehended by any sharpness of human reason. It is, moreover, the **Abyss of Creation**, of which Moses speaks in Genesis 1:2: *And darkness was upon the face of the deep <note>original: "Abyssi"</note>.* It is the **Abyss of Holy Scripture**, of which Ezekiel speaks in chapter 47, and Ecclesiasticus <note>Also known as the Wisdom of Sirach.</note> 1:2 and 24:8. It is the **Abyss of Providence**, of which the entirety of Psalm 139 speaks. It is the **Abyss of Divine Omnipotence and Wisdom**, of which Isaiah speaks in chapter 40. It is the **Abyss of Predestination**, of which Saint Paul speaks in Ephesians 1:4 and Romans 9. It is the **Abyss of Love, Redemption, and the merit of Christ**, of which John 3 and Romans 5 speak. It is the **Abyss of the judgments of GOD**, of which Psalm 36:7 says: *your judgments are a great deep <note>original: "abyssus multa"</note>.* Ecclesiasticus 38: *His counsel is in the deep.* It is the **Abyss of human misery and sin**, and of the wicked heart, Jeremiah 17:9 and Ezekiel 26:19. It is the **Abyss of Hell**, Revelation 9:1 and 2. It is, finally, the **Abyss of eternal life and joy**, where all things lack end or limit. Ezekiel 31:4: *The deep set him up on high <note>original: "Exaltauit illum abyssus"</note>*, that is, infinite blessedness and prosperity.

From these, as far as pertains to our present purpose, we shall explain only the **Abyss of Creation and of Providence**. The Abyss of Creation and of Natural things consists of the Sources, Origins, Treasuries, and invisible Spring-heads—most pure, perpetual, and most deeply hidden—within the Centers of the purest and simplest Elements: namely, of Earth, Water, Air, and the Firmament. In these most secret treasuries, the **seminal reasons** <note>original: "seminariæ rerum Rationes," a philosophical concept referring to the "seed-blueprints" or divine potentials implanted in nature that allow species to reproduce and grow.</note> of things, which preserve the species, shall be kept perpetually until the Dissolution of the World: such as the forms, proportions, and conditions of Animals, Vegetables, Minerals, rivers, winds, storms, clear skies, times, ages, and of all things, by which they come forth onto this visible stage of the World at appointed times, destined to serve the Commonwealth of the whole of human life and the course, ebb, and flow of all Nature. This natural Abyss is called by Orpheus *Night, Darkness, Mist, and the unseen Diana*, seen by no mortal—naked, that is—in the hymn which begins thus: *Night, the source of all things* <note>original Greek: "Νύξ γένεσις πάντων" (Nyx genesis pantōn).</note>. The **Abyss of Providence** is the most hidden order of Divine Counsels, the administrator of all Nature and human life, which is the author, moderator, and dispenser of times, ages, changes, years, months, days, hours, and minutes; of Natural things and human actions, duties, vocations, studies, dangers, calamities, afflictions, Deliverances, and of Human Life and Death. The Abyss of Wisdom is described in the book of Wisdom, chapter 7.

# THE THIRD STEP

**WHAT IS HIS NAME, etc.) THE WISE MAN** <note>referring to Solomon in Proverbs 30:4</note> prophesies concerning **WISDOM** incarnate, and concerning the ineffable and admirable **NAME**, **J E H O V A H**. The Psalmist teaches us how we ought to wisely use the Names of **G O D** in the Oratory <note>A private room or chapel for prayer and study.</note>, in *Psalm 18:2 and 3: The Lord is my strength, my rock, my fortress, my deliverer, my G O D, my stone, my protector, the horn of my salvation, my refuge.* And, Moses in *Exodus 34:6: L O R D, our G O D, Good, Gracious, Merciful, Kind, Patient, of much Mercy and Goodness.* But the Name **J E S V S** <note>original: "I H E S V S"</note> is the name above every name, at which every knee bows, of those in heaven, on earth, and under the earth. **T H I S  N A M E** is the effective cause of all divine miracles, if the Mind is rightly prepared in a Theo-Saphic <note>Divine-Wisdom; "Theo-Sophia" refers to knowledge of divine things.</note> and Mystical way through faith and invocation. To this faith, which has joined, coupled, and rightly **U N I T E D** itself with the Name **J H S V H** <note>A mystical "Pentagrammaton" version of the name of Jesus, often used in Christian Kabbalah to represent the Word made flesh.</note>, all the virtues of the Heavens, all earthly powers, all diabolical strength, and all things from the kingdom of sin and the devil that infest the bodies and souls of men, must yield.
