| Eat, my son, honey, because it is good: and the honeycomb, which is sweet to your palate: | | *Eat (therefore) my son H O N E Y, because it is good, and the honeycomb most sweet to your throat:* |

**Honey**] Athenaeus writes that the ailing Democritus <note>An ancient Greek philosopher.</note> lived for several days on honey alone, and when he lacked it, he died; Diogenes Laërtius <note>A biographer of Greek philosophers.</note> writes that when he was near death, he drew out his life for three days by the scent of warm bread. The honeyed doctrine of Eternal **W I S D O M** (which is the bread of life, *John 6:35*), if piously consumed by the mouth of a pure and clean heart, will not only refresh you as you lie deathly ill from the disease of sin, but will also preserve you from eternal death. For just as little bees fashion honey from dew and flowers: so the honey of Divine Wisdom is prepared from the Celestial, Spiritual, and Divine Dew—namely, the **H O L Y S P I R I T**—and from the flower of your **Mind**, which is to say, from faith, love, hope, and prayer. Even the smallest taste of this, perceived by a pious and faithful soul, surpasses all the sweetness, delight, and pleasure of the entire world. Hence the Psalmist says, *Your words are sweeter to me than honey and the honeycomb: Psalm 19:11 and 119:103.* May your sweetness, O **L O R D**, make all the bitters of the World sweet to me. Eat, therefore, **H O N E Y  F R O M  T H E  R O C K,  C H R I S T**, so that by his most healthy Balsam <note>A fragrant, healing ointment; here used metaphorically for Christ’s grace.</note> you may be liberated—in body, Spirit, and Soul—from annihilating corruption: (*Deut. 32:13*) the lack of which will let you die. Within this most pleasant honey lies hidden the **S A L T O F W I S D O M** <note>original: "SAL SAPIENTIÆ"; salt was a symbol of permanence and spiritual insight in both alchemy and theology.</note>, wisely named so by the wise. It is surely a wondrous proof of Divine Kindness that this phrase has remained alive even to our own age, even among those who practice profane philosophy; though these wretched little men (by **G O D**) have not understood what they were saying. There is a secret power in this speech. Learn it, my son.

**[To go before the Sun]** To outrun the Sun; the eye (according to Hermes) <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary figure to whom many mystical and alchemical texts were attributed</note> which is not only that visible one, that is, the greater light in the Firmament, but also the **D I V I N E** one: and at the rising of its light within us, to proceed toward you, **J E H O V A H**, to meet you, to approach you, to come together with you, in supplications (1 Timothy 2:1-2) <note>original: "1. Timoth. 2, 2."</note>, in prayers, petitions, and thanksgivings (since thanksgiving is an invitation to give more) for the rays of your blessing to be kindly poured into our minds as well as our actions or labors, and to anticipate you at the opportune place and time; or, to consult you and act with you Theosophically <term>Theosophy: 'God-wisdom'; a method of gaining knowledge of divine things through direct spiritual intuition</term> regarding all business. # INTERPRETATIONS

<margin>So is the heart of the King, etc. <note>Refers to Proverbs 21:1: "The king's heart is in the hand of the Lord... he turns it wherever he will."</note></margin> Daily experience testifies that **GOD** promotes or annihilates the thoughts, actions, and labors of men according to His pleasure. Therefore, that saying is true:

->*Divine power plays a part in human affairs.*<-
<note>original: "Ludit in humanis Diuina potentia rebus," a quote from the Roman poet Ovid.</note>

**JEHOVAH** breathes both blessing and cursing into the work and the person, for whom and whenever He wills. **HE** establishes Kings and deposes them; He exalts, humbles, builds up, and destroys; He blesses and He curses; **ALL THINGS** are in His almighty hand. If, therefore, you have business to conduct before Princely persons, tending toward the honor of **GOD**, the benefit of your Neighbor, or yourself, "Pray and Work" <note>The famous Latin maxim "Ora et Labora."</note> Theosophically, so that you may remain in the Love of **GOD**—O, this <term>Divine Art of Divine Love</term> <note>Khunrath refers here to a spiritual-alchemical practice where aligning one's will with God's love grants influence over the natural and social world.</note>, which this *Amphitheater* of ours teaches—and be a friend of **GOD**. Then the Prince will also be a friend (if what you seek is pleasing to **GOD**), merciful, gracious, and kind. For the **LORD** will turn them wherever He wishes. One must always add: *Thy will, O LORD, be done.* 

Well known is the story of Alexander the Great: when he was besieging Tyre and marching with his army toward Jerusalem because they had denied him supplies, Jaddus the High Priest turned his mind by coming out to meet him in his priestly robes. The same is read concerning Attila the Hun when he sought to attack Rome <note>According to tradition, Pope Leo I met Attila in 452 AD and persuaded him to turn back from invading Italy.</note>. Ahasuerus was swayed by Esther so that he would not destroy the Jews in a single day. 

Look, therefore, learn, and judge: just as the Wise man rules over the stars <note>A reference to the popular astrological maxim "Sapiens dominabitur astris," meaning a person of wisdom can overcome their celestial fate.</note>, can he not also rule over the souls and minds of men? Even **GOD** is swayed from His anger by a praying voice; why not man? But how, by what art, what industry, what Ray? By the Ray of Divine Wisdom. Do not be so simple-minded as to think it happened without art and without singular Divine Wisdom that Laban heard that voice in his dreams: *Take care that you do not speak to Jacob otherwise than kindly.* <note>Genesis 31:24.</note> Or do you think it happened by chance that Alexander the Great saw the High Priest in a dream, dressed in his robes, coming toward him? Prick up your ears and seek after this Wisdom. For if Christians have received power from **GOD** over all the force of our most bitter enemy, the devil; why not over the minds of men who are ruled by the devil?

### FOURTH STEP

presents and manifests in the Light before the face of **GOD**. For even if our actions, when viewed by the Light of human reason, seem good, legitimate, and just; nevertheless, when noted by the Light of Divine Wisdom, they appear most inept, false, and unjust.

->**L O T S** are cast into the lap, but they are governed by the **L O R D**.<-
<margin>Prov. 16 Verse 33.</margin>
*The* **L O T** *is thrown into the lap, and from* **J E H O V A H** *is its every judgment.*
<margin>180</margin>

**Lots are cast into the lap, etc.**] If lots are cast concerning secret, abstruse matters that are hidden from us—things doubtful and mysterious yet nonetheless useful, salutary, and (in times of extreme distress and necessity) most necessary—then, far from being illicit or prohibited in the sacred pages, they are actually governed by the **LORD**. That is, they are ruled by Divine Providence and are true Divine answers. Of this matter, we have almost innumerable mandates, testimonies, and examples clearly expressed in the book of sacred letters. These are the testimonies: Isaiah 34:17. **HE** (**THE LORD**) sent the *lot* for it (in dividing the land of Canaan for the people of Israel), *and His hand divided it for them by measure*. And, in Proverbs 18:18, the Wise Man says: *The lot suppresses contradictions, and it decides even between the powerful.* Rightly, therefore, does that Divine Prophet commend his lots to the Lord, saying: **O LORD**, *my lots* <note>original: "sortes meæ"; usually translated in modern bibles as "my times" (Psalm 31:15/16), but here interpreted literally as the "lots" of one's destiny.</note> are in your hand, Psalm 31:16. 

Examples are found everywhere in the sacred texts: Aaron, the brother of Moses, is commanded by **GOD** to cast lots over two goats before the Lord at the door of the tabernacle of testimony—one for the **LORD**, and the other for the scapegoat <note>original: "capro emissario," the goat sent into the wilderness bearing the sins of the people.</note>. The one whose lot comes up for the **LORD**, he shall offer as a sin offering; etc. Leviticus 16:8. When Israel had transgressed the covenant of **GOD** and had taken from the <term>anathema</term> <note>Referring to the "devoted things" or accursed loot from Jericho that Achan stole, causing God's displeasure.</note>, so that they were struck down by their enemies, the men of the city of Ai, and forced to turn their backs: Joshua searched out the sin of the anathema by lot. He investigated first by tribe, then by clan within the tribe, then by house within the clan, and finally by the man himself, the author of the anathema. Joshua 7:14 and following. 

When the Prophet Samuel was occupied in choosing and designating a King for the Israelites by lot, he brought forward all the tribes of Israel, and the lot fell upon the Tribe of Benjamin. He brought forward the Tribe of Benjamin and its clans, and it fell upon the clan of Matri, and finally it reached Saul, the son of Kish. 1 Samuel 10:20. And a little later in verse 24, Samuel says to all the people: *Surely you see whom the* **LORD** *has chosen (BY LOT), since there is no one like him among all the people.* You yourself may read in 1 Chronicles 24 how the Royal Prophet David divided the Levites by lots (how they should enter the house of the Lord according to their ministries). So too was Jonah discovered by lot to be the cause of such a great storm that even the ship was in peril. Jonah 1:7. The lot cast into the urn before Haman revealed that in the twelfth month, which is called *Adar*, the nation of the Jews ought to be killed. Esther 3:7. And truly, unless the Jews—clothed in sackcloth, sprinkling ashes on their heads, crying out to **GOD** with a loud voice, and praying to Him fervently with fasting, wailing, and weeping in repentance (as seen in chapter 4, verses 1 & 2)—had obtained grace and mercy from **GOD**, without any doubt the sentence (of killing the Jews) of the lot (the interpreter of the Divine will) would never have been changed or retracted.

# INTERPRETATIONS

If one also wishes to look at examples from the New Testament: was not the place of ministry and Apostleship (which Judas forfeited to go to his own place) determined by lot? Acts 1, last verse. Looking toward this end, **GOD** commanded the land of Canaan to be distributed to the Israelites by lot. For thus He says in Numbers 26, verse 56: *Whatever falls by lot, let it be received by many or by few.* And in chapter 33, verse 54: *You shall divide the land among yourselves (which I gave to you as a possession) by lot: to the more numerous you shall give a wider portion, and to the fewer a narrower one; to each, as the lot falls, so shall the inheritance be granted; the possession shall be divided by tribes and families.* And this ritual of casting lots has always been in use. For in this way the Romans of old elected their Dictators, Consuls, Senators, and Tribunes of the people through the luck of the tokens <note>original: "tesserarum sortes"; refers to small tablets or dice used for voting or drawing lots.</note>. Even today, in most places and almost everywhere, offices in any state, gifts, inheritances, etc., are distributed by lot. Whence it is said in Ecclesiasticus 14, verse 15: *Will you not leave your sorrows and labors to others in the division of the lot?* But let it suffice to have said these things. For it is not our purpose to bring forward here everything that serves to confirm and establish this divine art of divine <term>Geomancy</term> <note>Geomancy: literally "earth-divination," but here used broadly to describe any divinatory practice involving the casting of signs or lots to discern God's will.</note>. Therefore, from these things which have now been said by us, it emerges clearer than the midday light that **GOD** Himself is the Moderator, Ruler, Author, Favorer, Defender, and Promoter of lots.

<header>THE FOURTH STEP.</header>

I have established and completed the work. In the **Oratory** <note>Oratory: A private room or chapel dedicated to prayer.</note> therefore, one must sweat **Theosophically** <note>Theosophically: Referring to "Theosophy," which in this period meant a direct, mystical knowledge of God and the hidden secrets of nature.</note>, so that **GOD** may inform us; that He may not take His Holy Spirit from us; that He may bless us and our labors; and that He may guard our mind, senses, and reason, lest they be seduced by diabolical mockeries and phantasms; and guard our hands and feet, lest they destroy the work. Cicero, a prudent Heathen, was frustrated partly by many of his own counsels and reasons, and partly paid the heaviest penalties for his own confidence in his own wisdom and industry. What he achieved with worldly prudence is testified by many sad and tragic cries sent back from his exile, which are found in the letters of the third book to Atticus, and in his final letter to Octavius. Therefore, as he was about to be killed, he exclaimed: "O, that I was never Wise!" Rightly, therefore, says **Psalm 33:17**: *A horse is a vain hope for safety.* **And Psalm 127**: *Unless the LORD guards the city, etc.* **Ecclesiastes 11:5**: *As you do not know what is the way of the Spirit, or how the bones are joined together in the womb of a pregnant woman: so you do not know the works of GOD, who is the maker of all.* Therefore, let not our reason or the rashness of our talent claim such great prudence for itself, as to think (comparing itself only to itself) that it can govern its life, actions, and labors without a singular and specific Divine Blessing, or that it can manufacture its own fortune and success, or that it is within its own will and power to achieve anything good. Instead, let a person Christianly place and establish **EVERYTHING** in the hand of **God Almighty** and Merciful, and have (as the Wise Man wisely advises) his confidence in the **LORD** with his whole heart, from the beginning even to the end of his ways—that is, of all his actions and labors, in the **Oratory** and the **Laboratory** <note>Oratory and Laboratory: A famous alchemical pairing, emphasizing that spiritual prayer and physical experimentation must go hand-in-hand.</note>. If the **Theosoph** must not fail in this, much less should the sophist in his Labyrinth. The will of **JEHOVAH** is a surer guide than the thread of Ariadne <note>Ariadne’s thread: In Greek mythology, the string used by Theseus to find his way out of the Minotaur's labyrinth.</note> for us as we tremble in the great labyrinth of this world. Therefore, study **Cabala, Magic, and Alchemy** <note>The author views these as legitimate "divine arts" for understanding the universe.</note> diligently, and examine yourself against this **Touchstone** <term>Lydian Stone</term> <note>Lydian Stone: A dark stone used to test the purity of gold and silver; here used as a metaphor for a standard of truth.</note>: if your trust is in the **LORD**, you will draw the safety of His will from the **LORD**, and all things will succeed prosperously for you; you will be three and four times happy in both practice and theory; nor will you be confounded for eternity (as Experience itself testifies along with <term>Holy Scripture</term>). Hence, in **2 Maccabees 8:36**, Nicanor proclaimed that the Jews had **GOD** as a protector, and because of Him they were **INVULNERABLE**, because they followed the Laws established by Him. The following verse means the same thing, written on an old tapestry in a certain French castle, in which a woman was depicted drawing threads, about the meaning of which **King Francis of France** often debated:

->*As the threads are woven, **GOD** joins the mind to Heaven.*<-

That is, **GOD** assists the labor of one's calling, <gloss>He joins the thread for the weaver</gloss> / And that help also, which He commands us to seek while we labor, joins the mind to Heaven, <gloss>He commands us to think on heaven and pray.</gloss> Not in vain did I cite the passage of Hermes <note>Hermes: Referring to Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of alchemy and Hermetic philosophy.</note>, verse 317: *He who did not spare his own soul, etc.* A secret lies hidden there regarding the **CONJUNCTION & UNION** in his **Universal Physico-Chemical Stone**, a divine matter of which it is not at all advisable to speak more openly. See verse 132.

# FOURTH GRADE

[*To speak according to one's thought*] This means the ease and faculty of speech, by which the concepts and thoughts of the mind are most easily expressed. This power of speech is called **Eloquence** or **Oratory**. [*To presume, etc.*] To think worthily of those things which are given by God. For it is a singular gift of **GOD** to hear, see, and observe what **GOD** wisely suggests to the lover of **WISDOM**, and responds to the faithful, beloved seeker. **GOD** speaks to many, who nevertheless neither understand nor observe Him speaking or responding: indeed (alas!) being warned of perverse precepts and seduced by their own malice, they are unwilling to observe and understand in a Theosophical way <term>Theo-Sophicè|A method of understanding that combines divine revelation with philosophical reasoning</term> and they reject it. **GOD** speaks to us in every place and at all times; in the Heaven, the Air, the Earth, indeed He places clear mirrors within ourselves to remind us. But very few (sadly) hear the voice of **GOD** speaking Universally <note>original: "Catholicè"</note>. Nor is it for the multitude to hear the words of **GOD**: therefore they cried out to Moses: (Exodus 20, 19.) *speak you to us, and we will hear: let not the LORD speak to us, lest we die.* Hence also all things are full of fools. See verses 35, 37, & 190, & 197. Furthermore: not only to think, but also to speak: for there are some who think rightly, and yet they cannot speak what they think skillfully and distinctly. Whence we see even those things which are good in themselves, if they are not also handled well, lose the grace of the good. [**HE is the leader of WISDOM**] **HE**, **HIMSELF**, the **LORD** (verse 156.) granting to men **WISDOM**, eloquence, and the moderation of speech: He is the director, governor, prow, and stern of the Wise. For He immediately adds that both we and our words are in His hand.

[*All wisdom, and of works, etc.*] All Prudence; theory and practice: all our actions and labors, in the Oratory and Laboratory <note>The "Oratorium and Laboratorium" was a central tenet of alchemy, signifying that spiritual prayer and physical experimentation must go hand-in-hand.</note>, indeed in the whole of life, established in a Theosophical way for the attainment of true **WISDOM** and its fruits: Therefore also the **Philosophers' Stone** <note>original: "Lapis Philm."</note>, the Supreme **GOOD** of Nature and Art, is the **GIFT** of the Most High **GOD**. <margin>190 MAIDSERVANTS.</margin>
**She has sent her maidservants.**] The maidservants of true **WISDOM** are all the good **SCIENCES** and Arts, known through practice and proven by experience, toward an honest and useful end for human life. For Antiquity rightly and learnedly judged that a good reputation concerning **GOD** and His **WISDOM** was scattered throughout the good Arts; for through them He deals with us regarding His mysteries, secrets, and hidden things (see verses 74 and 261). However, beyond the most common ones known and vulgarized everywhere, there are still others to be numbered among the maidservants of true **WISDOM**—those more secret ones, like certain chamber-maids (although, alas! just as the image of **GOD** in man was defiled by original sin, these have been splashed and greatly fouled by the most filthy mud of sophistry by the devil and his instruments). These are, namely: <term>CABALA|Kabbalah</term> (not that literal, common kind used by the Jews, such as <term>Notarieken|Notarikon; a method of forming words from the initials of others</term>, <term>Gimetria|Gematria; the calculation of the numerical value of letters</term>, and <term>Teuofrasiche|likely Temurah; the permutation of letters</term>, which are inferior; but that more recondite and far superior kind, known only to **Theosophers** by the Influence, Light, and Motion of the Divine alone); **MAGIC**; and its relatives, **PHYSIOGNOMY** <note>the study of character through facial features</note>, **METOPOSCOPY** <note>divination through the lines of the forehead</note>, **CHIROMANCY** <note>palm reading</note>, and the entire Doctrine of the Natural **SIGNATURE** of Things <note>the belief that plants or minerals bear physical marks indicating their medicinal use</note>; **ALCHEMY**; **ASTROLOGY** also with her daughter **GEOMANCY** <note>divination by means of earth or geographic features</note>, and several **OTHERS**, which wonderfully and almost miraculously narrate and serve their wondrous **LADY**. 

Beware, however, I pray you my brother, that you do not falsely attribute the lies of the prince of this unclean World, and the vices or errors of false craftsmen, to the Sciences and Arts themselves (which are not unclean in themselves). These errors freely prostrate themselves as **TRUTH** (as a just and worthy punishment) before mundane seekers of **TRUTH** who have not yet been **Theosophically** washed and purged—that is, before the foolish—at the command and will of true **WISDOM**. For in this way, virtue has often borne the blame for vice. It is truly said that sacred things are profaned because they are used profanely by the profane. Even a good thing, when turned to abuse, becomes evil. *But to the pure all things are pure* (Titus 1:15; Romans 14:20). *And we know that for those who love GOD, all things work together for good* (Romans 8:28; see verse 261). All things are good and evil...

<margin>194</margin>

[*He shall draw grace, etc.*] Just as the Grace of GOD makes men good, so does that same grace nourish those who are the dwellings of piety and divine fear, adorning them with many gifts of grace. For there are various degrees of these Gifts. Just as the rays of the sun illuminate dark glass only dimly; yet if the glass is a little clearer, they illuminate it more; and if it is most clear and transparent, they illuminate it most brightly: so too is the human soul. If it is in some way purged, it is indeed illuminated by a ray of eternal Wisdom, but somewhat obscurely; if it is purged more thoroughly of its vices, it is illuminated more clearly; and if it is most perfectly purged, having forgotten almost all worldly things, it is illuminated most clearly of all by a certain intimate vision <note>original: "visione quadam intima"</note> of GOD, as our Savior testifies in Matthew 5, verse 8: *Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see GOD.* And in Hebrews 12:14: *Follow after holiness, without which no one shall see GOD.* But what is the nature of this vision? It is, specifically, the knowledge of Divine mysteries, which the Psalmist <note>original: "Psaltes"; referring to King David as the author of the Psalms.</note> calls the secret Wisdom of GOD in Psalm 51:8. No man of evil thoughts shall draw this from GOD; rather, he shall be filled with interior and exterior darkness: which is true condemnation.

<header>OF THE FOURTH GRADE. 95</header>

*They do not understand judgment]* Many things happen in our common life that are truly the judgments of the **L o r d**: yet the impious do not understand these things, but think they happen by some chance, not noticing the admirable Prudence of **G o d**. However, those who are endowed with the Spirit of Divine Wisdom can judge even those things which portend either the salvation or the ruin of men; indeed, they judge all the actions of men entirely, discerning what outcome or end they shall have. <note>original: "Iudicia Dei abyssus multa"</note> **The judgments of God are a great deep.** *But those seeking* **J e h o v a h**, *etc.*] Great (alas!) is the darkness of human reason, which without Divine Revelations can perceive the reason, cause, and end of no work of **G o d**. But by what means, and by what path one must arrive at revelations of this sort, our Wise man clearly teaches with a golden axiom: **Those seeking the Lord shall understand all things.** The Patriarch Joseph, the Prophet Daniel, and many others serve as examples. Most memorable is that passage from Job chapter 32, verses 7 and 8: *I hoped that greater age would speak, and a multitude of years would teach Wisdom. But as I see, there is a Spirit in men, and the Inspiration of the Almighty gives Understanding.*

| Blessings are upon the head of the righteous: but the mouth of the wicked covers iniquity. | <margin>Prov. 10 Verse 6.</margin> | ☞ *The blessing of the* **L o r d** *is upon the head of the righteous: but iniquity covers the mouth of the wicked:* |

[*The blessing of the Lord, etc.*] In ancient times, Kings, High Priests, and beloved guests were anointed with <term>Balsam</term> <note>Fragrant resins or oils used in sacred rituals to signify consecration or favor.</note>; hands were also placed upon the head when blessing. In the same way, Divine Wisdom anoints her worshippers with the Balsam of the Spirit, adorns her guests with gifts, and places her healing hands upon the heads of the righteous. For just as the head is the ornament and glory of a man, so Divine **W i s d o m** (which is the most noble crown of the head) adds an ornament to man that is by far the most beautiful. Stand, therefore, at the throne of **W i s d o m** with bended knees, and with a humble mouth and mind, incessantly and constantly plead for a Spiritual Blessing; and the blessing shall descend upon your head, like dripping Balsam. But the mouth of the wicked, which foams with nothing but arrogance, pride, insults, and uncleanness, shall be covered in confusion.

Those people mock **Wisdom**; in turn, they are mocked by **Her**. This law of **Incarnate Wisdom** <note>original: "SAPIENTIAE incarnatæ," often referring to Christ as the embodiment of Divine Wisdom.</note> is most just: *With the same measure you use, it will be measured back to you.* With the holy, **Jehovah** is holy; and with the blameless man, He is innocent; with the chosen, He is chosen; and with the perverse, He is perverse, as stated in Psalm 18:25. *To the gentle*] To the humble: for He exalts these, while He casts down the proud. Humility or gentleness, and the casting down of oneself in the **Fear of God** (before God), is the glorious discovery, exaltation, and sublimation <note>The author uses "sublimation" here both in the spiritual sense of refinement and the alchemical sense of a solid turning into vapor to be purified.</note> of oneself within God, along with the fruits of **Wisdom**. For God exalts those who are humble in heart and makes them sublime. See verse 202.

# INTERPRETATIONS

**WISDOM** <note>The Latin text begins with "PIENTIA," likely due to a decorative drop-cap "SA" being omitted in the OCR.</note> is not sold for money; nor does it pass to children by inheritance: it is necessary that we ask and obtain it from the Benevolence of the Benevolent [God] (asking that He might kindly send it) through prayers poured out from the whole heart to **JEHOVAH**. **SUMMARY**: One must Pray for Her in Spirit and Truth: and for the sake of successfully attaining Her treasures, one must wisely Labor. The **ORATORY** <term>Oratorium: a place of prayer</term> and the **LABORATORY** <term>Laboratorium: a place of work, specifically alchemical or chemical labor</term> are, therefore, to be entered wisely, according to the Laws and Teaching of this Amphitheater <note>The "Amphitheater" refers to the title of this book, *The Amphitheater of Eternal Wisdom*.</note>. See verse 87. Note: the "fool" in this place can also be understood as the profanely learned: And "riches" as the gifts of talent without the Fear of **GOD**: *A linguistically learned Fool / A foolish linguistic scholar / a lettered fool, not a truly learned one.* <note>original: "Ein Sprachgelehrter Narr / Ein närrischer Sprachgelehrter / literatus stultus, non doctus."</note>

<margin>204</margin>
*In the heart.*] In the soul: because it is the <term>hagiastherion</term> <note>Greek: "holy place" or "shrine"</note> or Sanctuary of WISDOM; the Microcosmic temple of Minerva <note>Minerva was the Roman goddess of wisdom; the "Microcosmic temple" refers to the human being as a "little world" that mirrors the universe</note>. So Proverbs 17 verse 24 says: *Wisdom shines in the face of the prudent.* And, Ecclesiastes 8 verse 1: *The wisdom of a man shines in his countenance*: namely, through physiognomy <term>Physiognomy: the practice of judging character from facial features</term> and metoposcopy <term>Metoposcopy: the art of reading a person's character or destiny from the lines of the forehead</term>.

| ☛ **He who walks with the wise shall be wise: ☛ a friend of fools shall become like them.** | <margin>Proverbs 13 verse 20.</margin> | *He who walks with the wise shall be wise: but he who is a friend to fools shall be destroyed.* |

<margin>205</margin>
*He who walks with the wise, etc.*] This means with those who follow the teaching of the Books of Nature, the Sacred Scripture, and the testimony of their own conscience: he who does this, by faithfully Praying and wisely Working, ascends by a straight and most certain way to the highest knowledge of things Divine and human, and is truly wise. All things must be according to their laws and testimonies: without which we seekers of TRUTH are ashamed to speak. 

But if your soul, O son, has been thus Cabalistically <term>Cabalistically: referring to the Cabala, a mystical Jewish tradition of interpreting scripture and the universe</term> illuminated by a ray of Eternal WISDOM; (for, according to Hermes Trismegistus <note>A legendary figure representing the combination of the Greek god Hermes and the Egyptian Thoth, regarded as the author of sacred hermetic texts</note>, GOD HIMSELF is the eye of our Mind, without whose light (I say) the mind remains blind in things Physical as well as hyperphysical and Divine; nor shall we ever see the light of the knowledge of Sacred Scripture, or of Nature, or of our own selves); then, led by this ineffable light, you will walk safely through all the shadows of error. 

Then, without harm, you will be able to penetrate freely and fruitfully all kinds of disciplines, both good and bad (in their own way). Then, like Ulysses (I shall use the words of Heinrich Cornelius Agrippa <note>A 16th-century polymath and occultist; Khunrath here defends him as a "philosophical evangelist" rather than a sorcerer</note>, whom I know from his genuine writings to be a good and philosophical evangelist, because his words presuppose a Theo-Sophical <term>Theo-Sophical: relating to divine wisdom or "God-knowledge"</term> mind, not a necromantic <term>Nigromantica: black magic or communication with the dead</term> one): if you enter the cave of the Cyclops, and descend to the underworld, you shall return unharmed; if you approach the Lotus-eaters or the Syrtes, you shall return safe; if you drink Circe’s cup, you shall not be transformed; if you sail past Scylla, you shall not be in danger; if you hear the Sirens, you shall not fall asleep, but you shall be judging all things, as the Apostle says, and judged by no one. 

*A friend of fools.*] The filth gathered from every kind of vice is called "folly" by our Sage and the Stoics, those most serious defenders of virtue; in the Sacred Scriptures it is called Malice and Folly: likewise, just as Integrity, perfect in all its parts, is called WISDOM by both. Flee the company of fools—that is, the vicious or the evil (as in verse 201; of whom, alas, almost all states, sciences, and arts are full): for no poison, no plague, causes as much harm as the familiarity of such diabolical fools. In the study of Cabala and Magic, avoid necromancers (as you would the Devil himself, whose instruments they are); in Alchemy, [avoid] sophists...

...differing and struggling: because they are fools. Do not say "Greetings" to them; much less let them be familiar to you. A neighbor catches the plague from a neighbor.

->Trust G O D faithfully, but trust a mortal cautiously;<-
->And look well beforehand, whether he be worthy of trust.<-

For to trust much, and to have seen little, prepares the greatest losses. *A grape*, says Juvenal, *takes on a dark hue from the sight of another grape.* <note>original: "Uva... conspecta livorem ducit ab uva." This is a Latin proverb suggesting that one bad person can corrupt those around them through proximity.</note> Great is the power of habit or conversation in either direction. One must walk with a few, and those being good. Everyone is such as the company in which he delights. For *he is known by his companion, who is not known by himself.* A companion is the shadow of a companion. But WISDOM (Wisdom of Solomon 7, verse 30) overcomes malice: therefore, in the WISDOM of G O D made flesh, we may report a triumph over malice, provided only that we have been wise in her, in whom we shall also conquer. Therefore, be ONE with yourself, but not alone; because you are in the ONE: the Triune <note>The Trinity: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit</note> in the TRIUNE. Incarnate WISDOM says: *where two or three are gathered in my name, I AM in the midst of them.* Male and female are TWO; Body, Spirit, and Soul are THREE distinct in essence; gathered together in the person of the student of <term>Divine-Wisdom</term> <note>original: "Theo-Sophiæ"</note> in the name of I H S V H <note>The "Pentagrammaton," a Kabbalistic/Esoteric spelling of the name of Jesus used to represent the Word made flesh.</note> C H R I S T crucified—the incarnate WISDOM of the Father—they are ONE. In the midst of this and of these is HE WHO WAS, WHO IS, and WHO SHALL BE, GOD; the WISDOM of GOD; the SPIRIT of DIVINE WISDOM. Then you shall say more rightly and truly than Scipio <note>Scipio Africanus the Elder, famously quoted by Cicero as saying he was "never less idle than when idle."</note>, that you are never less idle than when idle; nor less alone than when alone. And: that while at leisure, you do more. O blessed leisure, not at all lazy! which the unclean world does not grasp. Only the friend of G O D enjoys this leisure, not the friend of fools, who are wise in a worldly and profane way. A man with a "rubbed forehead" <note>An idiom for someone shameless or hardened, who has lost the ability to blush.</note> will not grasp these things.

Following the previous page's warning about choosing the right companions, it now focuses on the ethics of sharing knowledge—balancing the duty to be generous with the need to protect sacred "mysteries" from the unworthy—and concludes with a warning against drunkenness as an obstacle to wisdom.</meta>

<page-num>101</page-num>
<header>THE FIFTH STEP.</header>

*Nor with wasting envy, etc.* <note>original: "Neque cum inuidia tabeſcente." A quote from the primary text being commented upon.</note>] I will not communicate; I will have nothing in common; I will not associate with the envious man. For it is the custom of Philosophers not to be envious. For this reason, pious antiquity willed that the doors of the Muses should be open. Yet, not indiscriminately to everyone: but to whom? To the sons of Learning and Discipline alone. For the gifts of <term>GOD</term> <note>The capitalization of DEI reflects the original emphasis on the Divine source of knowledge.</note> are to be shared honestly and liberally, but only with honest and liberal minds (lest pearls be cast before swine possessed by the devil, as in verse 344). The most learned <term>Zwinger</term> <note>Theodor Zwinger (1533–1588), a Swiss physician and scholar known for his encyclopedic "Theatrum Humanae Vitae."</note> rightly says in his Hippocratic tables, page 37: "This," he says, "was the ancient majesty of the arts: that they were not communicated except to the initiated, either by word of mouth—whom they called <term>listeners</term> <note>original: "ἀκροατὰς" (akroatas)</note>, from which the <term>Kabbalah</term> <note>The Jewish mystical tradition, here used to mean received oral tradition.</note> of the Hebrews takes its name—or by writing, but in a dark style, by which the profane commoners might be kept away, and the secret might be communicated only to those who understand (verse 43)." Truly, the very prostitution of the Arts seems to steal away both their authority and their effectiveness due to the resulting contempt. Just as those who rashly reveal the secrets of the arts to outsiders are worthy of the whip, so too are those who, out of envy, refuse to share even with the initiated. These are his words. The quoted words of our Wise Man, and those in verse 147, must be interpreted prudently in this sense. You might perhaps, oh sharp-nosed critic, object to the envy of those who philosophize <term>Physico-Chemically</term> <note>Refers to Alchemical philosophy, combining natural physics with chemical experimentation.</note> regarding the "Supreme Good" in Nature and Art. Hear the philosopher <term>Rosinus</term> <note>Zosimos of Panopolis, an early alchemist often called "Rosinus" in Latin translations.</note>: "It is the judgment of <term>GOD</term> that those who know this matter find envy—not because of worldly greed, but lest the evil, perceiving this, become more ready to perform profane acts, and the Philosophers be forced to give an account for their sins." Behold, you also have a sufficiently honorable, sufficient, just, and fair answer in the words of <term>Zwinger</term> just cited.

| Wine makes a mocker, strong drink makes a brawler: and everyone who delights in it will not be wise. | <insert>Proverbs 20 Verse 1.</insert> | *WINE is a luxurious thing, and drunkenness is tumultuous: whoever delights in these will not be wise:* |

*WINE is a luxurious thing, etc.*] <term>Heraclitus</term> said: *it is difficult to hide folly; but in wine, it is impossible.* <term>Cato</term>: *With one exception, no one has ever approached the overturning of the Republic while sober.* <term>Plato</term>: *In a life that is not sober, no one ever becomes Wise, and much less becomes moderate.* <term>Seneca</term>: *Vices conceived through wine, when the insanity is hardened by habit, remain powerful even without the wine.* Wisdom, therefore, is not to be drawn from drinking cups. But you will greatly desire that you might be permitted to drink from the silver cup of the <term>Patriarch Joseph</term> (Genesis 44, verse 5), in which he prophesied and divined the future. Truly, who will deny that this cup was cast astronomically from <term>Philosophical Electrum</term> <note>An alchemical alloy of the seven metals, believed to be sensitive to planetary influences and capable of magical effects.</note> by the highest Divine-Magical craftsmanship? There exist writings which <term>Aureolus ab Hohenheim</term> <note>Paracelsus (1493–1541), the famous physician and alchemist. "Aureolus" was part of his self-given name.</note>, the Master of Mysteries, left to posterity concerning that Electrum. Wisdom pours out such a cup to her lovers in the Song of Solomon (Chapter 8, 2), and intoxicates them with Heavenly Nectar. Those Heavenly influences and starry treasures, which are the guardians of all natural Wisdom, most willingly flow into and lower themselves into sober souls who thirst for wisdom. *But the drunken and mad fools heaven leaves as unsteady and clumsy louts.* <note>original German: "Die vollen vnd tollen Narren aber leſſet der himmel vnſleter vnd Tölpel bleiben."</note>

**You shall have in the end]** Because you dwell in the help of the Most High, and abide under the protection of the **GOD** of Heaven. *Who do not test him*] Not in vain does the Divine Law warn: *You shall not test the* **LORD your GOD**, Deuteronomy 6:16; Matthew 4:7; Luke 4:12. **JEHOVAH**, who is a Jealous God <note>original: *Zelotes*</note>, cannot endure a joke. Refer here to the tenth canon, of the fourth part of this Amphitheater, regarding the restorative and renewing reformation of <term>Magic</term> <note>original: *Mageia*; here referring to "high magic" or the divine wisdom of the Magi, which the author seeks to "reform" or restore to its holy origins.</note>; and on the other hand, the eradicating extirpation of <term>Necromancy</term> <note>original: *Nigromantia*; literally "black divination," which the author views as a corrupt and forbidden practice to be uprooted.</note>. Thus Eternal **WISDOM**, manifested in the flesh, **JESUS CHRIST**, says in John 14:21: *I will manifest and declare myself* <note>original Greek: ἐμφανίσω ἐμαυτὸν (emphanisō emauton)</note>. See verses 142 and 195. And be understanding. *Who have faith, etc.*] The Wise Man teaches that unbelief <note>original Greek: τὴν ἀπιστίαν (tēn apistian)</note> is an obstacle by which the truth is less known, and we are prevented from obtaining the **Gifts of GOD**. Unbelief (I constantly affirm, having been taught by experience) is like a left hand, with which we perversely strike away the **GIFTS OF GOD** that He kindly offers us of His own accord. For just as the hand that is the door of miracles and for obtaining Goods and wonderful Gifts from the **LORD** is Faith; so distrust or unbelief is the loss or expulsion of miracles, and an obstacle to obtaining the great and wonderful things of **JEHOVAH**, and to performing them through us (for a Theosopher <note>original: *Theo-Sophus*</note> is to **GOD** what his own hand is to a man). Rightly, therefore, the man who can never be praised enough, <term>Capnio</term> <note>The Greek-derived nickname (meaning "Smoke") for the famous Renaissance Hebraist and humanist Johann Reuchlin.</note>, in his book *On the Wonder-Working Word*, book 2, chapter 6, says: *God strikes a covenant with man, not with just anyone, but with him who, in Holiness, Piety, and Religion...*

<meta>This page continues the "Interpretations" section, concluding a thought on the spiritual transformation of the individual into a "truly universal" or "catholic" being who is united with God. -># I N T E R P R E T A T I O N S<-

...one, reborn, truly universal <note>Latin: *catholico*. Khunrath uses this in the sense of "whole" or "universal" spiritual rebirth rather than referring to the Roman Catholic Church.</note>, as is shown in the second figure of this Amphitheatre. By the washing of repentance, as in Isaiah 1:16 <note>"Wash yourselves, make yourselves clean; put away the evil of your doings from before My eyes."</note>, having been changed for the better, you will be joined and united to **GOD**: you will be illuminated by the ray of the super-celestial Sun. And you, being pure in heart, will see **GOD** in you, and yourself in **GOD**; **ALL IN ALL**. The earthly man suffers earthly things; the mundane man suffers worldly things from the Prince of the unclean world; the Spiritual man suffers spiritual things from good Spirits, by way of the administration delegated by **GOD**, both Macro- and Micro-Cosmically <note>The Macrocosm is the great world/universe; the Microcosm is the little world/man. Khunrath views them as reflections of each other.</note>; the Divine man suffers divine things from **GOD** Himself. He who is less than pure, how does he dare to touch the Pure? As for spiritual and divine matters, you who are earthly and mundane, abstain from passing judgment. You judge those things whose sweetness you have never tasted, like a blind man judging colors. See verses 46 and 157. You have judged me and this book as mundane and unclean; see that you do not do so too mundanely yourself. Seek verse 46. *Subject to sins*] Do not sin, therefore, O son of **WISDOM**, for **GOD** himself sees (for in every place the eyes of the **LORD** behold the good and the bad, Proverbs 15:3); why would He not see? # THE FIFTH STEP #

...they choose her] For GOD draws the one who is running. See verses 145 and 160. *She is found*] Therefore Solomon, groaning in Ecclesiastes 7:24 <note>Original: "Eccles. 7, 25." WISDOM is found: because she flows in from the Divine more than she is acquired by human means (that is, by human prudence, reasoning, imagination, or speculation). To those who apply their hands Theo-Sophically, the Gods (Elohim <note>original: "Dii (Elohim)." Khunrath uses the Hebrew plural name for God.</note>) give aid, verse 92, and several following. Yet the splendor of such a venerable Divinity and Light does not shine upon us through our own merits or our own holiness, but by the GIFT of a Merciful GOD. To this, refer the whole last chapter of Jesus Sirach <note>also known as the Book of Ecclesiasticus or the Wisdom of Sirach.</note>, which I recommend to you as being of the best quality.

| To bring a word before **GOD**: because **GOD** is in Heaven and you are upon the Earth, therefore let your words be few. | *A speech is to be brought before* **GOD**: *for* **GOD** *is in Heaven, and You are upon the Earth; therefore let your speeches be few.* |

*Lest you speak anything rashly*] The searcher of hearts loves the speech of a pure, inward, and sincere heart, as it is in Psalm 19:14. <note>The text cites verse 15, following the numbering in some Latin Bibles.</note> *Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be always pleasing in your sight, O Lord, my helper and my redeemer.* Therefore, let your speech, by which you address **GOD**, be born in the deepest heart, not on the lips; and it is better for you to speak with **GOD** using sighs coming from the deep heart than with rash words. For the sighs of the godly proceed from the Holy Spirit, when He groans within us; words, for the most part, come from human imagination—and there is a great difference between the words of the Spirit and the words of the mouth.

<margin>Verse 3.</margin>

| **When you have vowed a vow to GOD, do not delay to pay it: because there is no pleasure for GOD in fools: therefore pay what you have vowed.** | <margin>238 **THE VOW.** Deuteronomy 23, Verse 21.</margin> *(And) If you have vowed anything to* **GOD**, *do not delay to pay it; for an unfaithful and foolish promise displeases Him: but whatever you have vowed, pay.* |

*If you have vowed anything to* **GOD**, *etc.*] The Wise Man speaks in the manner of the Old Testament. For the godly, when placed in distress, were accustomed to promise "thank-offerings" <note>original: "χαριστικὰ" (charistika) — sacrifices of gratitude or thanksgiving</note> to **GOD**. Just as Hannah in 1 Samuel 1:11, when she asked for a son from **GOD**, vows and promises that she would return him to the Lord; as also Jephthah in Judges 11:30. *Vow and pay to the Lord your* **GOD**, says the Writer of the Psalms in Psalm 76:11. And, *that which has once gone out of your lips, you shall observe*, Deuteronomy 23:23. Such vows proceed from the highest love of **GOD**, most holy desire, and sincere gratitude of the soul; and they must be paid to **GOD** without delay. 

In this way the Patriarch Jacob, when he had seen the celestial ladder in his dreams, upon waking vows to **GOD** that he would build a House of **GOD** in that place—that is, that he would spread the knowledge and true worship of **GOD** and the doctrine of the Messiah there. Genesis 28:20. We in the New Testament have vowed to **GOD** a vow of filial obedience in Baptism, and we return this vow to **GOD** in holiness and justice, faith, patience, and humility. We therefore define the vow of the New Testament thus: A vow is an obligation to perform the worship of the First Table <note>The "First Table" refers to the first segment of the Ten Commandments, which details a person's direct duties toward God.</note>, which are the Fear of **GOD**, faith, love, patience, invocation, thanksgiving, confession, and the preaching of the Divine Name. These vows must absolutely be paid to **GOD** by all Christians. 

Special vows, however, are when—besides the usual generosity toward the poor—we bind ourselves to some particular and singular good work by which either the honor of **GOD** or the salvation of men is promoted; and this without any hypocrisy or rashness, but out of deep and sincere gratitude of soul for this purpose: that the benefit received from **GOD**, which we obtained through prayers, might also overflow to our neighbor.

**[He who indeed turns away, etc.]** Let him who has ears to hear, hear what the **SPIRIT OF TRUTH** says to the sons of men: let him turn away from evil and do good; let him fear **GOD** and perform justice; and let him obey the one who counsels him well, otherwise he will obtain or achieve nothing good, whether in the **ORATORY** <note>The "Oratory" refers to a place of prayer and meditation.</note> or in the **LABORATORY** <note>The "Laboratory" refers to the place of physical work or alchemical practice; the author emphasizes that both spiritual and physical labor must be conducted with a pure heart.</note>. For if the tree is displeasing, how could the fruit be pleasing? Indeed, a holy and immaculate life is entirely a prayer before **GOD**, an acceptable sacrifice, and a most pleasing worship to **GOD**. You must speak before **GOD** by your work itself, not just by words: if it is otherwise, our prayer becomes a sin, as in Psalm 109, verse 7.

# OF THE FIFTH STEP.

**[They who work evil.]** The fruit cannot be more excellent than its seed: whatever a man sows, that he shall also reap. Archelaus, King of Macedonia <note>Archelaus I (reigned c. 413–399 BC), who was notorious for the violent and treacherous methods he used to secure his throne.</note>, when he had killed three legitimate heirs and seized the kingdom, was finally killed by a youth who plunged a sword into his liver; therefore a verse was written about him: *Constructing evil for another, he constructs evil for his own liver.* Mercy and truth are two handmaidens and faithful companions to all who cultivate piety and the Fear of **GOD**.

It is not the mark of a Wise Man to say at any time, *I did not think*. <note>A common Stoic proverb—the wise man is never caught off guard.</note> Do not be ashamed of coals. The world is judged **Physico-Chemically** <note>Through the laws of physical alchemy</note> today by philosophers, and it will be judged **Theosophically** <note>Through divine wisdom</note> by the final fire, by God himself.

Secondly, the **Above**—not mixed with the Elements or their superfluities, but through and in itself (yet animated by Nature)—He congealed, solidified, and constituted into a hard and solid body; that is, He strengthened it. For by the Word of the Lord the heavens were made firm, and by the Spirit of His mouth (<term>Ruach Elohim</term> <note>original Hebrew: "The Spirit of God"</note>, the Divine Emanation, verse 13) all their power, Psalm 33:6. His Spirit adorned the Heavens, Job 26:13. For God said, Genesis 1:6: Let there be a <term>Rachia</term> <note>original Hebrew: "expanse" or "firmament"</note> (that is, a solid extension or expansion, firm and compact). From this, the Latins rightly said *Firmamentum* <note>Firmament</note>, and the Germans *eine Veste* <note>a stronghold or firmament</note>: for it is harder and more durable than any brass or adamant; the most solid Heavens are cast, as if from brass, Job 37:18. Therefore, it suffers no lessening by the heat of its own Light or fire, nor by the swiftness of its motion, let alone being consumed before the final day of the Lord. Jehovah alone stretched out the Heavens, Isaiah 44:24 and 45:12.

## OF THE FIFTH DEGREE.

On this matter, even *Hermolaus Barbarus* <note>An Italian scholar (1454–1493) famous for his commentaries on ancient science.</note> in his supplement to *Dioscorides*, where he treats "Waters" in general, says: "There is also a Celestial water, or rather the Divine water of the Chemists, which both *Democritus* and *Hermes Trismegistus* <note>The legendary founder of alchemy.</note> knew, calling it now 'Divine water,' now 'Scythian liquor,' now <term>pneuma</term> <note>original Greek: πνεῦμα, meaning 'breath' or 'spirit'</note>, that is, Spirit from the nature of the aether, and the Fifth Essence of things." From this comes Potable Gold <note>Liquid gold intended as a universal medicine.</note> and that celebrated, yet-to-be-found Philosopher's Stone (sought by the alchemical-sophists, I mean, with whom—alas—nearly everywhere is full, nor will it ever be found by them; the contrary has been sufficiently demonstrated regarding the Theo-Sophists in this *Amphitheater* <note>Khunrath refers here to his own book, the *Amphitheatrum Sapientiae Aeternae*.</note>) and fable. "This kind of liquor, I believe," says the same author, "is signified by the inscription found very recently in the Paduan fields near the little town of Este, in a brickwork and therefore fragile structure, which was broken by the clumsy hand of a farmer plowing the earth there." Thus he speaks. *Conrad Gessner, the physician of Zurich*, on page 5 of his work on *Moonworts and things that shine by night*, records the aforementioned epigram, which smacks of the most ancient paganism, as follows:

> *Lest the value of so great a liquor should perish.*

Inside this urn another small urn was found, with the inscription of these verses; about which see also the preface to the *Book of Secret Remedies* by *Euonymus Gessner, the lover of medicine* <note>Euonymus Philiatrus was a pseudonym for Conrad Gessner.</note>:

Thus it is written there. The truth of this water is gravely confirmed by an ancient author in the *Revelation of the Secret Spirit of the World*, solemnly affirming among other things that this ethereal spirit (<term>Schamaim</term> <note>original Hebrew: "Heavens"</note>, Heaven), existing in a watery body more than perfectly glorified, burns perceptibly in a clever lamp without diminution or consumption of itself, forever. We also know from the testimony of histories and trustworthy men that in our own age, such lamps—burning perpetually without the addition of new fuel and filled with a most fragrant ethereal liquor—have been found in the most ancient tombs and caves of Lower Germany and Greece. So great and so wonderful, indeed almost supernatural, is the condition of the Fire of this super-Celestial liquor, that it burns in a vessel most tightly closed, but its flame is extinguished by and in our air when the vessel is opened. <note>original German: "Es ist gar ein ander wasser vnd fewer / als vnsere gemeine wasser vnd fewer."</note> *It is quite another water and fire than our common water and fire.* Hence the Physico-Chemical Philosophers say: *Our water is fire*; (for it is <term>Schamaim</term>, from the fiery water of the super-Celestial) burning bodies more than the fire of the common people. # INTERPRETATIONS

**GOD** did not only set apart and wisely reserve Heaven, but also Earth and Water—namely the *hyle* <note>original: "hylin," a Greek term for the "first matter" or raw substance of the universe</note> or seeds of this whole World, which exist even today in their primordial, universal state, animated by the universal spark of the **WORLD SOUL** (see Figure 3, Question 7 of this *Amphitheater*). This was done so that from these things, as if in and from a macrocosmic, universally summarized subject—to be prepared physico-chemically as well as treated Christian-Cabalistically—one might universally track down and extract the knowledge of the Creator and of the crucified **JESUS CHRIST** whom He sent. This includes the knowledge of Nature and every creature, and consequently (for it is consistent with truth) also those things which are above the Heavens (namely the first and second); that is, the *Schamaim* <note>original Hebrew: שמים (Heavens). Alchemists often read this as a compound of "Esch" (fire) and "Maim" (water), signifying "Fiery-Water."</note> or "Waters Above the Heavens," the fiery waters of the Third Heaven, the tabernacle of **GOD** and the Sanctuary of the Angels, as well as the knowledge of oneself. Thus, from the universally summarized Book of Nature, the Theo-Sophist <note>A "God-wise" person who seeks understanding through both scripture and nature.</note> might recognize what a wondrous Wisdom, Power, and Goodness the Creator possesses.

I could very easily show sufficient causes for the **DIVINE USE** of the Philosopher’s Stone in a Christian-Cabalistic manner (see Figure 4 of this *Amphitheater*, where it treats the **URIM & THUMMIM** <note>Sacred objects used by ancient Hebrew high priests for seeking oracles; Khunrath equates them with alchemical mysteries.</note>) from these very things, if it were lawful to break the celestial seal of hidden revelation and divulge the mysteries of **GOD**. Let those things which this *Amphitheater* provides here and there suffice for the present for the son of doctrine (to whose Theo-Sophic meditation I have decided to leave something to be tracked down). For it is fitting for a Theo-Sophist to philosophize not only about the use of the Heavens, but also about their substance, essence, and nature. I have shown that the **WATERS ABOVE THE HEAVENS** are (and are found by the Wise in the nature of inferior things) most pure, most subtle, fiery, most bright, more than perfect, and therefore incorruptible. They are perpetually fixed in themselves—that is, permanent—yet liquid and fluid, flammable, and not at all combustible. They serve this **USE**: that they may exist in the highest region and constitute the *Schamaim*, or the Third Heaven, which on its nearest surface is watery, and on its outermost is fiery: a flaming fire, a burning water. 

What then? Here, in these pure inferior things (though only in the macrocosmic universal), there exists a Water so noble, or a watery fire so marvelous, contrary to common style and reason, which is of a super-celestial substance and nature, and is found wisely only by the Wise. How much more so in the highest region, that is, above the Firmament, in the world called "hyper-physical" because of its Divine use? If this were not so, the Mineral of **WISDOM** would not represent the universal Macrocosm in a real form. Far be it from those who are wise in Physico-Chemistry to think the contrary, let alone to establish or speak it.

**I PROCEED: IN THE FIRMAMENT**, by the power of the **WORD OF JEHOVAH**, as if by a certain grasping and a screw-like lifting upward; by the constitution (as was said) of the **FIRMAMENT**, immediately and on the spot, there simultaneously appeared a certain great space or high interval between Heaven and Earth, which is and is called **PLACE**. For just as there is no mountain without a valley, or just as hands first joined and then separated and set apart cannot be without a middle space between them; so too Heaven and Earth, once this sublimation of separation, drawing away, and secreting from one another was made, could not exist without an intervening space and distance. Ezekiel 8:3: *The Spirit lifted me up between Earth and Heaven.* It was necessary that a **VACUUM** exist first, but afterward it was filled with watery humors, continuous vapors and exhalations (the materials of various meteors) daily evaporating from the lower region and tending upward, as well as innumerable earthly bodies, so that they might be there, and might grow in length and breadth...

<summary>Khunrath explains that the "Waters Above the Heavens" (Schamaim) are a fiery, alchemical substance that can be found in nature by the wise. He further describes the creation of the Firmament as a physical separation that created the concept of "Place" and "Vacuum" between the celestial and terrestrial realms.</summary>

->### THE FIFTH STEP.<-

...should grow, breathe, and move. The Wondrous Macrocosmic Laboratory of the Wondrous **GOD**, with Nature presiding or Laboring, is perpetual and Universal. **GOD** said furthermore: *Let there be Lights in the Firmament of Heaven* (that is, <term>Rachia Schamaim</term> <note>original Hebrew: רקיע השמים. Alchemists interpreted this "expanse" not just as space, but as the stabilizing or "firming" of spiritual, watery essences into celestial bodies.</note>, in the expansion of Heaven, or the ethereal watery spirits made firm) *and let them divide the day and the night: and let them be for signs and Seasons, and days and Years: That they may shine in the Firmament of Heaven, and illuminate the Earth. And it was so done. And **GOD** made two great lights: the greater light, to rule the day: and the lesser light, to rule the night, and the stars.* And He placed them in the **FIRMAMENT OF HEAVEN** (*that is, in the Rachia, the extension or expansion of the firmed Schamaim*) so that they might shine upon the Earth, rule over day and night, and divide the light from the darkness. **NOTE**: In what way the **STARS** are for signs (Hebrew: *A O T* <note>original: אות (Oth), meaning a sign, signal, or monument.</note>), that is, indicating signs, and as it were an Alphabet in the volume of the Book of the Greater Celestial World, through which **GOD** (paternally caring for us) speaks with us concerning various and great matters; He shows, foretells, and predicts things that are to come and are imminent before they happen; I shall declare this more widely elsewhere (**GOD** granting). See verses 35 and 353. **THIS** is the **SECOND HEAVEN**; sublime; a purely ethereal Region. This holds the Sun, Moon, and Stars; indeed, even the **FIRST** and Lower Heaven has (in its own way) its own stars: a thing which the Sages know and testify. Both are moved by a harmonic or sympathetic motion (toward one another): that which is below is as that which is above, and vice versa. This motion confirms the certainty (of which I spoke) of the signs. **GOD** is Wondrous in His works. The Sum: **ALL THINGS** of the Micro- and Macro-Cosmos are flowing together, breathing together, and in agreement. Finally, the Firmament of Heaven—as Isaiah 51:6 witnesses—(once the bonds of its coagulations are dissolved by **FIRE**) shall melt away like smoke. For it shall be reduced back into that which it was before its freezing, solidification, and firming; that is, it becomes a free **SPIRIT**.

Thirdly, and **MOST HIGHLY**, above the <term>RACHIA SCHAMAIM</term> (that is, the Firmament of Heaven), He did not mix the <term>SCHAMAIM</term> with the Elements (as He did with the First Heaven), much less did He pollute it with the waste-like surpluses of those elements; nor did He congeal and firm it into a solid and hard body (as He did with the Second); but (by His Omnipotent virtue) by and in itself, making it more than perfect, He established the <term>SUPER-CELESTIAL WATERS</term> as such things as we taught a little while ago, **REMAINING** in perpetuity; and by manifesting their fire, they are always burning upon the outermost surface without consuming themselves, and they shine with a most white light without smoke. **THIS** is the <term>Empyrean Heaven</term> <note>The "Empyrean" is the highest heaven, traditionally thought to be composed of pure fire or light.</note>, most lucid; indeed, it is **LIGHT**, which **GOD** inhabits as a thing consistent with Divinity, inaccessible (1 Timothy 6:16). Therefore, Plato learned from the Brahmins of India <note>A common Renaissance belief that Greek philosophy originated from ancient Eastern or "Gymnosophist" wisdom.</note> that **GOD** exists in a fiery Essence, and he established the Fifth Essence <note>The "Quintessence," the purest element that makes up the celestial bodies.</note> as the dwelling place of Divinity. In the same sense, perhaps, Thomas Aquinas—although the Author of the *Aurora of the Philosophers* <note>A famous alchemical text often attributed to Paracelsus or Pseudo-Aquinas.</note> thinks the opposite in chapter 19—said without blasphemy that **GOD** and His Angels cannot be without the fire of burning water <note>original: "ignis aquae ardentis." In alchemy, "burning water" often refers to alcohol or acids, but here it signifies a spiritual, paradoxical substance.</note>, but use it daily. He cannot be without it because He willed it so; He willed most highly to use these things—Above, Below, and in the Middle—for the seat and throne of His Majesty, and for various fitting uses. Thus it pleased the **LORD**; let the same please you. **THIS** is the **HEAVEN** or the **HEAVEN OF HEAVENS** (Schamaim) mentioned in Deuteronomy 10:14, 1 Kings 8:27, Psalm 115:16, and Nehemiah 9:6. In respect to the two—the lower and the lowest—this is the **THIRD**, to which Paul was drawn (2 Corinthians 12:2) by the pull of a Magnet...

## INTERPRETATIONS

Caught up by the Divine Mind, in which he heard secret words that a man is not permitted to speak: *The immense, the highest, the final* <note>original: "Immenſum, ſummum, Vltimum"</note> (Deuteronomy 4:32); for Holy Scripture mentions nothing further or higher. This is the <term>Sanctuary</term> <note>original Greek: Ἁγιαστήριον</note>, that is, the Sanctuary of our Angels, who always behold the face of <term>GOD THE FATHER</term> (Matthew 18:10). It is the Paradise of highest happiness; the seat and Throne of blessed minds. O glorious day (to use the words of Cicero from *On Old Age* in a Christian sense) when I shall set out for that council and assembly of souls! What else? <term>THE LORD GOD HIMSELF</term> <note>original Hebrew: HV (Hu), often used as a Divine name meaning "He"</note> is in Heaven above (Deuteronomy 4:39). To which and above which our Lord Jesus Christ, having been crucified, ascended on the fortieth day after his Resurrection, <term>made higher than the heavens</term> <note>original Greek: ὑψηλότερος τῶν οὐρανῶν</note> (Hebrews 7:26). *Ascending above all Heavens* (Ephesians 4:10). *Sitting at the right hand of God the Father, from whence He shall come* (Acts 1:10, Matthew 26:64) *to judge the living and the dead* (Matthew 25:31, Acts 10:42) and the Age by <term>FIRE</term> (Isaiah 66:15, 2 Peter 3:7). Concerning these <term>HOLY HEAVENS</term> (Psalm 102:20), in which <term>THE LORD GOD HIMSELF</term> is above (Deuteronomy 4:39, Joshua 2:11, Ecclesiastes 5:1); concerning this Sanctuary of His, this high dwelling place of the Heavens (Deuteronomy 26:15, 2 Chronicles 30:27); the Holy Place, the Throne of His glory (Isaiah 63:15); His holy House (Baruch 2:16); the holy Temple of His glory; the Throne of His kingdom (Daniel 3:53)—from here, our Royal Theosophist <note>Likely referring to King Solomon, traditionally viewed as the master of divine wisdom.</note> asks for <term>WISDOM</term> to be sent to him from <term>JEHOVAH</term>. Let us also ask of Him, in our <term>THEOSOPHICAL ORATORY</term> <note>A place of both prayer and study/experimentation.</note>, in Spirit and in Truth, and it shall truly be sent, in a theosophical manner, even to us.

<term>COROLLARY</term>: The word <term>SCHAMAIM</term> <note>original Hebrew: שמים (Heavens)</note>, that is, <term>HEAVEN</term>, when truly explained by this doctrine of ours, will most healthfully teach you the source and nature of <term>LIGHT</term> (in Hebrew, <term>A O R</term> <note>original: אור</note>) (Genesis 1:3). Light is the author of splendor and illumination, as well as (by its arrangement) of the <term>DAY</term> (verse 139). You will learn how it shone out from the <term>DARKNESS</term> (2 Corinthians 4:6)—for the *Schamaim*, or Heaven, and consequently the entire <term>CHAOS</term>, was dark and not visible because its internal fiery Light was not yet divinely manifested—by the force of the Divine command, established and firm (just as fire is manifested from "spirit of wine" <note>An early term for concentrated alcohol or ethanol.</note> in a dark place), and the Day arose. Without the presence or lack of this <term>LIGHT</term>, the immense and universal work of <term>GOD</term> would have remained unknown and obscure to us. 

You will also learn how <term>UR</term> <note>A play on the Hebrew word for light/fire.</note> or <term>FIRE</term> is naturally made and artificially manifested every day. Since fire cannot exist without heat, it always exhibits and demonstrates its effect: <term>HEAT</term>. This heat, certainly, exists in all things (for an animated *Schamaim* exists in all things as <term>NATURE</term>). It is the guardian of every form and species, the stimulus for natural actions and for the carrying out and production of things. It is the <term>instrumental</term> <note>original Greek: ὀργανικόν</note> principle (both externally and internally), both natural and artificial, and the impulsive, <term>motive</term> <note>original Greek: κινητικόν</note>, or <term>active</term> <note>original Greek: ἐνεργητικόν</note> force established by <term>GOD</term>. It is attributed to the <term>SOUL</term>, which (by means of the Heaven/Schamaim) grants its gifts in many forms to things so they may exist within them—acting like a most faithful midwife to both the Microcosm [man] and Macrocosm [universe]. 

We must ask why, or in what respect, <term>HEAT</term> is called Divine; Celestial; Elemental; Natural; or implanted and innate, corresponding by a certain proportion to the heat of the sun and the stars. We must ask from whence the actions of these things (and of <term>GOD HIMSELF</term>) are so diverse; and in what sense (not a common one, but by giving each its due) these phrases of the Philosophers are to be interpreted: "The <term>HEAVEN</term> is alive"; "It acts upon lower things through Influence, Light, and Motion"; "Heaven is the primary cause why the Elements, though contrary by their own Nature, are mixed together and..."

### OF THE FIFTH STEP

<margin>R 3</margin>

...and they are joined to one another. Toward the **First Matter** <note>original: "primam materiam" — the formless primal substance from which all things are created</note>, the Heaven holds the same relationship as a husband to his beloved wife; it loves lower things; it pours its seed into the Earth just as a male into a female; it begets lower bodies. It is the parent of all. It is the instrument by which **GOD** acts with us. It is the cause of all things that are born; it bestows Form and Species, sending them into the prepared matter. It rules everything contained here in the World; it makes the seeds fruitful; all fertility is scattered from **HEAVEN**. And other things similar to these: **THEN YOU WILL BE ABLE TO PHILOSOPHIZE RIGHTLY CONCERNING THE SECRETS OF NATURE.** He teaches and learns well who distinguishes well.

*From the seat of your greatness* <note>original: "A sede magnitudinis tuæ"</note>] The **LORD** says in Isaiah 66:1: *Heaven is my throne.* Psalm 103:19: *The LORD has prepared his throne in Heaven.* Psalm 123:1: *To you I lift up my eyes, who dwell in the heavens.* Psalm 110:4: *The LORD, his throne is in Heaven.* Matthew 6:9: *Our Father who art in heaven.* It must be noted: From the throne of Divine loftiness, nothing comes but what is Divine and eternal. **WISDOM** <note>An emanation of the Divine; see verse 137</note> is therefore not created, not formed, not originated or made like creatures, but begotten from the Eternal Divine Father, Divine and Eternal; provided we grasp this with a faithful mind as Christians, rather than trying to comprehend it with a fanatical imagination.

*May she be with me, etc.*] That there may be present for me a <term>FAMILIAR SPIRIT</term> <note>original: "SPIRITVS FAMILIARIS" — in this context, a tutelary angel or guiding genius, not a "witch's familiar"</note>; see verse 223. Pray to **GOD, THE BEST AND GREATEST**, so that you—who desire to reach the longed-for end of your Physico-Chemical work—may be assisted by a good <term>ASSISTING SPIRIT</term> <note>original: "SPIRITVS ASSISTENTIÆ"</note>, who may most faithfully guard the work not only from that most hateful enemy the devil (the author of all confusion), but also encourage you to labor wisely. And, lest you fail in anything from which harm might come to the work, he may discourage you from error.

Certainly, it should not be considered a trivial thing to preside over the **Laboratory of the Wise**; rather, it should be entered reverently, as a <term>place of purification</term> <note>original Greek: ἁγνεῖον — a holy sanctuary or place for ritual cleansing</note>, and in it one must labor in such a way that you do not offend your good genius who guards you and your Work. The "swine of this world" <note>original: "Sues mundani" — the uninitiated or those focused only on material gain</note> understand nothing of this; Philosophers alone will perceive my mind and meaning, and they will follow it.

May the **ASSISTING SPIRIT** also be with me to Pray with me, and Labor with me: may he wisely instruct, direct, arrange, help, promote, prosper, and bless my Mind, Understanding, Reason, Thoughts and senses, and all my Actions and Labors (see verses 28, 145, 158, 181, and 292). This is a great Mystery, observed by very few, without which you—though you profess yourself a Christian—will never bring the <term>Philosopher’s Stone</term> <note>original: "Lapidem Philosophorum"</note> to its desired end (even if you proceed correctly and artificially in and from Natural Principles, according to the method of Nature). See verse 132. Be, in life and deeds, the one you wish to be seen, said to be, and truly are: a **Christian Philosopher**.

It is a gift of **GOD**, the secret of which **Hermes** <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of alchemy</note> and others held by Divine inspiration. In the <term>Macrocosm</term> <note>The "Great World" or the universe</note>, it consists of Body, Spirit, and Soul. Regarding this, we also, in the <term>Microcosm</term> <note>The "Small World," i.e., the human being</note>, according to the laws and teaching of this *Amphitheater*, must pray <term>Theosophically</term> <note>through divine wisdom</note> and sweat or labor <term>Cabalistically</term>, <term>Magically</term>, and <term>Physico-Chemically</term> in Body, Spirit, and Soul. So that the Triune **JEHOVAH**, by cooperating with the trinity of you and your labors, may deign to inspire, give, and bestow the will, the knowledge, the being, and the power to achieve the triune universal Physico-Chemical Work. Remember to work Theosophically. He who can grasp it, let him grasp it; I have said enough.

**Observe:** Certain sciences and arts are good, yet they are sometimes called **UNCERTAIN**, not because they are uncertain in and of themselves, or because those who presume to handle them might sometimes treat them poorly; but because there is **LACKING**...

# INTERPRETATIONS

For the working craftsman, <term>T H E  W I L L  O F  G O D</term>. **Everything depends on God's blessing. One must also have good fortune from God.** <note>original German: "An Gottes Segen iſts alles gelegen. Man muß auch das Glück von Gott haben." This reflects the contemporary proverb that skill alone is insufficient without divine favor.</note> For why, I beseech you, Almighty <term>J E H O V A H</term>, if He wished to punish you with His divine curse, or to take away (on account of sins) that gift of His, or to deprive you of the treasures and fruits of Wisdom—why, I say, could He not do so? He who created All things, who also inverts the order of Nature when He wills; just as, according to the will of Joshua, the Sun stood still in the midst of Heaven and did not hasten to set for the space of a whole day (Joshua 10:13). At the petition of Hezekiah, <term>G O D</term> brought back the shadow by the lines it had already descended on the sundial of Ahaz, backward by ten degrees (4 Kings 20:11) <note>This refers to 2 Kings in modern Bibles; the Vulgate uses the 4 Kings numbering.</note>. The three Hebrew men—Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego—cast into the midst of the furnace of burning fire (in Babylon), were not touched by the fire (Daniel 3:21 and following). And these things are done through the Omnipotence of <term>G O D</term>, who holds Nature in His omnipotent hand and rules it as He wills. Therefore, the <term>W I L L I N G</term> of <term>G O D</term> must be obtained by us. The great Count Pico della Mirandola <note>Giovanni Pico della Mirandola (1463–1494), a famous Renaissance philosopher who sought to harmonize Platonism, Neoplatonism, and the Kabbalah with Christianity.</note> meant this same thing (although he was unfairly criticized for this statement by a man of great authority) when he said: *He approaches Nature in vain who has not drawn to himself <term>P A N</term> (that is, the <term>G O D</term> of all Nature)* <note>Pico used the Greek name "Pan," meaning "All," as a code for the Divine Source of the natural world.</note>. This, according to the Laws and Doctrine of this Amphitheater <note>The "Amphitheater" refers to Khunrath's own book, the *Amphitheatrum Sapientiae Aeternae*.</note>, with <term>G O D</term>'s assent, can be done <term>Theo-Sophi-cally</term> in the Oratory, verse 190. <term>T H E  S U M</term>: The sciences and more secret arts are and remain uncertain, unless they are sub-delegated by the <term>H I G H E S T</term>, joined with the virtue of a nobler operation; unless, I say, they are animated or strengthened by <term>D I V I N E  V I R T U E</term>. This is the same thing that Solomon said (v. 329): *to draw the will from the <term>L O R D</term> and to dwell with <term>W I S D O M</term>* (verse 300).

The <term>Binary</term> <note>The 'Binary' or number two symbolizes duality, conflict, and the separation from the 'One' (God). In this philosophical system, it represents the fallen material world which must be overcome to reach spiritual unity.</note> is therefore to be rejected. See the second figure of this Amphitheater <note>Likely a reference to the "Amphitheater of Eternal Wisdom," a famous alchemical work by Heinrich Khunrath.</note>. *The earthly dwelling weighs down, etc.*] Our mind, dwelling in a body that is corruptible and mortal because of sin, is held shut away as if in a dark prison, so that man cannot rightly recognize **GOD**, nor know Nature and himself, by and through himself. For this reason, **GOD** must be prayed to, so that through <term>Theo-Sophic</term> <note>Divine Wisdom; a spiritual practice aimed at gaining direct knowledge of the divine through meditation and prayer.</note> exercise in the love of **GOD** (having conquered and overcome the passions of the flesh through repentance), the mind may be snatched up to the contemplation and handling of Divine, Spiritual, and Natural things. It is as if the mind were Divinely drawn upward out of the depths of the prison and placed at the very top of the dwelling; from here, it may begin to discern what it previously could not see while placed at the bottom, and in its own way, it may secretly enjoy the sweetest conversation with **JEHOVAH** and the good spirits delegated by **GOD**. It may be intoxicated by Divine Nectar, and thus arrive at the knowledge and enjoyment of the whole **UNIVERSE**. See verse 145. No one understands this except the faithful student of Divine Love.
