**TWO things I have asked of YOU.]** Considering both the inner and outer man and life, the wisest King <note>Solomon, traditionally credited with the wisdom in Proverbs</note> seeks the governance of both from GOD. For a man left to himself alone falls into darkness and errors of the mind, and also loses external happiness and success. From this, a man becomes like that tree which is planted by the streams of water, which will give its fruit in its season, whose leaf shall not fall off, and all things whatsoever he shall do shall prosper (Psalm 1:3). **Vanity.** What is vanity, if not the worldly, impure wisdom, which is foolish, blind, reckless, proud, ignorant of GOD, superstitious, idolatrous, a despiser of GOD, seditious, cruel, bloody, bold, inhuman, <term>epichaerecaca</term> <note>from the Greek "epichairekakia": finding pleasure in the misfortunes of others, similar to the modern "schadenfreude"</note>, restless, hypocritical, <term>philonic</term> <note>contentious or argumentative</note>, impudent, incontinent, ferocious, greedy, slandering, lying, deceptive, false, arrogant, double-tongued, deceitful; and in short, nothing but that serpent-like cunning and malice innate to natural man: and that deplorable fall of the <term>protoplast</term> <note>the "first-formed" man, Adam</note>, and a horrible ruin always tending and proceeding toward eternal destruction. **Lying words.** He opposes lying to the true Knowledge and Invocation of GOD: for the Knowledge and Invocation of GOD are the fountains of eternal blessing and happiness; but lying—that is, ignorance...

# INTERPRETATIONS

Of GOD, idolatry, superstition, contempt for GOD and for prayer; this is an abyss of curse, both temporal and eternal. The wise man desires neither riches nor poverty: for

->*Prosperity often causes minds to grow excessive:*<-
->*The shining light of the World was the poor Jesus.*<-
<note>original: "Luxuriant animi rebus plerunque secundis: Fulgida lux Mundi pauper Iesus erat." This couplet contrasts worldly arrogance with the humility of Christ.</note>

<margin>273</margin>
| | | |
| :--- | :---: | :--- |
| ☞ Lest by chance, being full, I be enticed to deny [You], and say: Who is the LORD? Or compelled by want, I steal, and swear falsely by the NAME of my GOD. | <margin>Verse 9.</margin> | *Lest by chance I be full, and deny, and say: Who is JEHOVAH? And lest by chance I be made poor, and steal, and take the name of my GOD in vain.* |
<margin>273</margin>

**Lest by chance, being full, etc.]** The moderate comforts of life are what should be desired by a Wise man. A Poet calls riches and wealth *the incentives for evils*. <note>original: "irritamenta malorum," a reference to the Roman poet Ovid.</note> Pharaoh, in his great abundance and power, imprudently and arrogantly uttered this voice: *Who is JEHOVAH?* Therefore, excessive riches brought him to ruin; for he encountered a superior and more powerful Lord in the Red Sea, whom he—hardened in his mind—refused to revere, fear, or acknowledge despite so many supernatural and clearly divine wonders. Therefore, those who seek only mountains of gold in our more secret philosophy are wandering; this is the mark of a Fool, not a Wise man. For Wisdom is the worshiper and lover of GOD, not of gold. This **Heavenly Bride** is free from all greed, luxury, pride, and haughtiness; she walks in a simple and humble habit, yet one that is honorable and clean. She uses favorable things modestly and prepares herself to endure adversity: indeed, so that she may gather a treasure of Divine and Natural Mysteries, she sustains poverty, burdens, and labors, and does not easily yield to misfortunes:

->*For neither do pleasant things puff up the good, nor do harsh things break them;*<-
->*But the true joys of an invincible faith sustain them.*<-

<margin>274</margin>
# But ☞ Wisdom is the excellence of rectification.
<margin>Ecclesiastes 10, Verse 10.</margin> ->*After INDUSTRY (this truly being so) follows WISDOM!*<-
<margin>274</margin>

**The excellence of rectification, etc.]** How distorted and depraved human Nature is, our daily weaknesses, hallucinations, darkness, and errors sufficiently testify: therefore, the <term>rectification</term> <note>the process of refining or "straightening" a substance or the soul</note> and improvement of our perverse nature must be established at every moment. Wisdom is the goal of this <term>ἐπανόρθωσις</term> <note>Greek: epanorthosis; meaning correction, or setting right what is crooked</note> and of our rectification. The greatest of all evils is born with us, which everyone forgives and for which no one desires a remedy; namely, <term>philautia</term> <note>Greek: self-love or excessive ego</note> and self-love, by which everyone is by nature a friend to themselves and delighted by their own opinions. But in truth, this disease, by which individuals please themselves too much, is the fountain of all errors and offenses in life. Accordingly, the rebuilding of nature and of self-love is highly necessary if you, a follower of Wisdom, desire to breathe in the LIGHT of true WISDOM.

->But you, son of the DOCTRINE, who by the grace of JEHOVAH,<-
->have thus obtained His WISDOM or certain<-
->singular GIFTS.<-

<margin>The Mark of the Wise.</margin>
**And he will hasten to receive.**] Even with great thanksgiving and the proper payment for the labors performed. These are the MARKS <note>original: "SIGNATVRÆ," referring to the outward signs or characteristics that identify a person's nature</note> of the faithful and beloved heirs of WISDOM. However, those who forget their benefactors, or sons who foolishly wish to be before the father—*that the egg wants to be wiser than the hen* <note>original: "daß das Ey will klüger seyn denn die henne," a German proverb about youthful arrogance</note>—these are the ungrateful, from whose house evil shall not depart.

<margin>Where and why the Wise man should not speak.</margin>
**In the ears of the foolish, etc.**] I warn you as a brother: do not forget this precept. For it is not fitting or right, nor entirely safe, to speak and philosophize with everyone, or at all times, or about everything concerning the Mysteries, arcana, and secrets of **GOD**, Man, Spirits, and Nature; rather, there is (as has already been said quite often) a *to whom*, a *when*, and a *how much*. One must sometimes speak like the many, but decide like the few. One must serve the time, the place, and the persons. Beware also—as a certain Religious man well warned—lest some Saturn <note>In this context, "Saturn" refers to a stern, cold, or restrictive critic or authority figure who might suppress secret knowledge.</note> look upon your books, the witnesses of your secrets; lest you be ignominiously subjected to and trampled by the hooves of oxen—which has happened to many who were unmindful of this precept. Would that I myself were always mindful of this! Do not cast pearls before swine possessed by the devil. It has often been beneficial to have remained silent in the right time and place.

<page-num>140</page-num>

-> # INTERPRETATIONS <-

Through the Book of Holy Scripture, of Nature, and of itself, the human heart is freed from corruption, diabolical filth, and ignorance. For **GOD** adorns and rewards the study of wisdom in this life with greater light, understanding, science, and a spiritual and natural knowledge of things, as well as with counsel, the strength of faith, consolation, and success in both public and domestic governance; and after this life, with immortal prizes.

| He who neglects Discipline, despises his own soul: but he who hears reproof, possesses a heart. | <margin>Verse 32.</margin> | *He who casts away* <insert>❦</insert> **DISCIPLINE**, *despises his own Soul: but he who yields to reproofs is the possessor of a heart.* | |

*Discipline, etc.*] Just as one who neglects medicine hates and despises the health of the body, and is an enemy to this bodily life; so too he who neglects discipline, which is the medicine of the soul, is the enemy and murderer of his own soul. And just as there is "health to the navel and watering to the bones" <note>original: "sanitas vmbilico, & irrigatio oſſium," quoting Proverbs 3:8</note> for those who fear the Lord and turn away from evil (Proverbs 3:8), so on the contrary, there is decay, weakness, and the like—the gnawing worm of conscience—for those who despise the Fear of the Lord and discipline (Psalm 32:3). *Possessor of a heart.*] This means he is the master of his own passions: anger, hatred, joy, sadness, fear, and pleasure. If a person learns to rightly rule and moderate these passions, he will surely act more prudently in all matters, and along with the possession and moderation of his own heart, he will possess glory and honor.

*Poverty and shame, etc.*] Wisdom herself unceasingly corrects the "natural man" <note>A term often used in the 17th century to describe a person living by instinct and ego, without spiritual enlightenment.</note>—who has clearly strayed from the paths of true Wisdom—in order to lead him back to the way and free him from innate and inborn foolishness. If the Wise man admits this correction, he is adorned by his corrector, Wisdom, with many rewards, among which are honest and legitimate wealth, as well as honors. If, however, the foolish man rejects Discipline, Wisdom departs from him, and poverty and shame—the daughters of impiety—take her place.

## THE FIFTH DEGREE.

<margin>282 The Signature of the Wise Man.</margin>

| **Do not rebuke a mocker, lest he hate you; rebuke a Wise man, and he will love you.** | *Therefore, do not reprove a mocker, lest he perhaps hold you in hatred: reprove a Wise man, and he will love you.* |

*Do not rebuke a mocker, etc.*] For you would be "washing a brick" or "washing an Ethiopian." <note>original: "Laterem enim vel Æthiopem lauabis." These were common Latin idioms for attempting an impossible or futile task—one cannot wash the color out of a brick or the skin of an Ethiopian.</note> Consider that German saying: **The Devil has truly showered me with fools. One would have much to do indeed if he were to make all fools clever.** <note>original: "Hat mich dē der Teuffel mit Narren beschiffen. Es müste auch einer viel zuthun haben / der alle Narren solte klug machen."</note> Avoid these people. *Do not give what is holy to the dogs.* <note>A reference to Matthew 7:6.</note> Epicureans <note>Here used to mean those devoted only to pleasure.</note> and atheists become more furious when rebuked; but the pious, being teachable and fearing **GOD**, make progress in Wisdom and many other excellent gifts.

<margin>283</margin>
<margin>Prov. 14 Verse 6.</margin>
<margin>283</margin>

| | |
|----------|----------|
| **A mocker seeks Wisdom, and finds it not: but knowledge is easy for him who understands.** | *A mocker seeks (indeed) WISDOM, and finds it not: the learning of the prudent is easy.* |

*A mocker seeks, etc.*] A skeptical and arrogant <note>original: "nasutulum," literally "large-nosed," a Latin metaphor for one who is critical or prone to mocking.</note> mind is by no means capable of true Wisdom. For WISDOM loves a simple soul that is eager to learn; she feeds it with honeycomb and honey, and intoxicates it with the nectar of Wisdom. A soul suited for knowledge, says Ptolemy <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the ancient astronomer and geographer.</note>, attains more of the truth than one who exercises himself in science in a supreme manner. Indeed, this fitness of the mind is a heavenly gift, and is acquired through Prayer.

<margin>284</margin>
<margin>Prov. 17 Verse 24.</margin>
<margin>284</margin>

| | |
|----------|----------|
| **WISDOM appears in the sight of the understanding: and the eyes of a fool are in the ends of the earth.** | *WISDOM shines in the face of the prudent; the eyes of fools are at the ends of the Earth.* |

*In the face of the prudent, etc.*] That is, the countenance of the Wise man is modest, but the eyes of fools wander about inconsistently and are indicators of lightness; for the face is the picture of the soul. Just as the face of those looking in mirrors reflects in the water, so the hearts of men are manifest to the prudent, Proverbs 27:19. And, *diligently know the face of your cattle, and consider your flocks.* Ibid. verse 23. *A man's wisdom shines in his face, and the Most Powerful will change his countenance,* Ecclesiastes 8:1. Therefore, explore men and disciples through <term>Metoposcopy</term> <note>The art of reading a person's character from the lines on their forehead.</note>, <term>Physiognomy</term> <note>The practice of judging character from facial features.</note>, and <term>Chiromancy</term> <note>Palm reading.</note>, just as Pythagoras did for several days. For just as all created things are painted and adorned by Nature with certain marks and signs, and distinguished by the divine characteristics of Nature—namely, by a certain proportion, figure, and habit—so judgment can be made concerning the internal and hidden spirit and the secret properties of things. Indeed, the secret property of things and the latent spirit betrays itself by certain external marks and signs, and according to its nature and character, it fashions such a <gloss>signature</gloss>, figure, proportion, and habit as it wishes to be known by the Wise. This is the <term>Signature of Natural Magic</term>, the beginning, and as it were the alphabet and first element of the art. Thus, this "painting" is especially to be recognized in the face and habit of man. For the signature of all Nature converges in the <term>Microcosm</term> <note>The "Little World"—the idea that a human being is a miniature map of the entire universe.</note>. Here the characters of Nature, and the hieroglyphic marks, are certain...

...as will be clear from what follows. But how? you will ask again. Immediately, I answer, and mediately, according to the most free will of **GOD**; and indeed: Theosophically; Physically; Physico-Medically; Physico-Chemically; Physico-Magically; Hyperphysico-Magically; Cabalistically; by the Law and Doctrine of this entire Amphitheater. The terms I have listed are few, yet their meaning spreads very widely. You ask for definitions: rightly so: I provide them. <term>**THEOSOPHY**</term> *is Catholic <note>Here, "Catholic" is used in its original sense of "universal" rather than referring to the Roman Catholic Church.</note> Theology, in a triad (that is, Biblically, Macro-cosmically, and Micro-cosmically)*, *the wondrous and miraculous knowledge of* <term>**JEHOVAH**</term>, *(verse 157. The Voice of* <term>**GOD**</term> *in All things, through All things, concerning All things, to All people. (verse 35.)* <term>**PHYSICS**</term> <note>In this context, "Physics" refers to Natural Philosophy—the study of the physical universe and its spiritual underpinnings.</note> *is the knowledge and treatment of both Worlds—that is, of the entire Greater World and the Lesser World (according to the Body and Spirit which it holds from the Macrocosm)—through Tradition, Nature, and Art, Universally, from and within the sacrosanct Scripture, the Philosopher's Stone, and ourselves; and Particularly from and within the parts of both.* <term>**PHYSICO-MEDICINE**</term> *is the art of knowing the great* **Book of Nature** *(Macro- and Micro-cosmically): so that you may read (as much universally as particularly) Yourself in the larger World; and* 
<margin>To this belongs the Doctrine of Signatures. <note>The "Doctrine of Signatures" was the belief that plants or minerals that resemble parts of the body can be used to treat those parts.</note></margin>
*conversely, the larger World in Yourself: for the sake of protecting the health of the human body and putting diseases to flight (v. 297.)* <term>**PHYSICO-CHEMISTRY**</term> *is the art, by the method of Nature, of Chemically dissolving, purifying, and rightly reuniting Physical things; both the Universal (Macro-cosmically, the Philosopher's Stone; Micro-cosmically, the parts of the human body: though let there be no slander about restoring the original form) and* **ALL** *the particular things of the lower globe.* <term>**MAGIC**</term> <note>original: "Mageia"</note> *of the most ancient Sages (who were called Magi by the Persians, Philosophers by the Greeks, Wise Men by the Latins, Gymnosophists and Brahmans by the Indians, Priests and Kabbalists <note>original: "Mekubales"</note> by the Egyptians, Prophets and Cabalists by the Hebrews, **Chaldeans** by the Babylonians and Assyrians, and Druids, Bards, and Semnothei by the Celtic Gauls)* **UNIVERSALLY** *taken, is the same as the study of the Cabala among the Hebrews, most highly perfected and absolute, since it consists piously and wisely in the worship of Divine things, the handling of Spiritual things and conversation with them, and the investigation of Natural things:* Although these [the Hebrews], in one and the same course, under a more kindly Guide, ran far ahead of those others. But, <term>**PHYSICO-MAGIC**</term> (a work only concerning <term>the Beginning</term> <note>original: "Beresith", the Hebrew word for "In the beginning," referring here to the secrets of Creation and natural wisdom.</note>, that is, the Wisdom of Nature, verse 162.) is a miraculous method of practicing by Natural artifice (Macro- and Micro-cosmically). <term>**HYPERPHYSICO-MAGIC**</term> (so called in respect to the Natural and for the sake of Teaching) is a pious and useful conversation with good Angels, the flaming ministers of **GOD**, under the manner of an administration delegated by **GOD**, as much while waking as while sleeping, mediately and immediately. <margin>The Divine study of Cabala.</margin> <term>**CABALA**</term> is the symbolic **RECEPTION**, allotted Theosophically (both Universally and Particularly, by which we may perceive Divine things in a human way, either immediately or through a suitable medium), of Divine revelation for the soul-saving recognition of **GOD** and the <term>Messiah</term> <note>original: "Maschiah"</note>; for the knowledge, union, and enjoyment of separate Forms, of Nature (in the Macro- and Microcosm) and of ourselves; and also for the true understanding of Holy Scripture. There you have it. This Amphitheater of ours, explained Philosophically, exhibits necessary and sufficient expositions in abundance to the sons of Doctrine in its own time (**GOD** willing). Be content with these for the present: and do not slander what you do not know. Concerning Magic, Alchemy, and Cabala, a man otherwise sufficiently learned in the more common Disciplines (I withhold his name to consult his honor) judged quite meagerly in his poems. *Every person judges a thing according to how they understand it.* <note>original: "Ein jeder iudicirt von einem dinge wie er es verstehet."</note> Such people deserve mercy rather than reproach. ### INTERPRETATIONS

...their taunts <note>original: "scommata"</note> detract from the truth; since they concern the abuse of a thing (which does not take away from its actual substance) rather than its legitimate and true use, as if a defect in the craftsman should imply the unworthiness of the art itself. In the same way, one might—though by what right?—brand Holy Scripture with the mark of heresy. **I add this:** Someone may ask: "From where do you get these things which you propose to us in this <term>Amphitheater</term> <note>The "Amphitheater of Eternal Wisdom," Khunrath's primary work, which he envisions as a structured space for divine and natural learning.</note> of yours?" With our Wise Man <note>Likely referring to Solomon or the personification of Wisdom.</note> I answer candidly (and indeed all the more gladly to satisfy certain harsh critics, and I declare it in the most solemn legal form): **To me**, (the least of all Philosophers) **God gave: I received from the Lord:** as much immediately <note>Through direct revelation or inspiration.</note> as mediately <note>Through study and the natural world.</note>. And how, I ask, will you inquire again? I shall tell you. You heard it before, namely, <term>Theosophically</term>, <term>Physically</term>, <term>Physico-Medically</term>, and so on, as mentioned above. 

For I, inflamed with a massive fire and Divine heat to examine the highest matters, have sought out and surveyed the monuments of philosophers from various nations—the most ancient, the old, and the modern—whether they were sculpted, painted, or written (at home and abroad), myself and through others (by purchase or exchange), as time and occasion allowed. I have studied them whether they were expressed symbolically or mystically, hieroglyphically, figuratively, enigmatically, parabolically, allegorically, secretly, or openly. I have unrolled, reread, and read again the books of <term>Theosophers</term>, <term>Cabalists</term>, <term>Magi</term>, and <term>Physico-Chemists</term>—that is, of the Wise—as well as the works of non-illuminated ethnic philosophers or Sophists. With sighs and vows permitted and granted to a Christian, I wished, I invoked, and I prayed; and He opened them (the matter speaks for itself), He who alone is worthy: **JESUS, the Wisdom of the Father**. He opened not only those books I mentioned, but also the **Book of God** in the <term>universal triad</term> <note>original: "ternario Catholico." This refers to the three ways God reveals Himself: through Holy Scripture, the Macrocosm (the universe), and the Microcosm (man).</note>, which is Holy Scripture and both Worlds (the Greater and the Lesser), and He removed its seals (as in verse 223 and the second figure of this Amphitheater), so that book explains and interprets book still from day to day. 

In the <term>workshop of Vulcan</term> <note>A common alchemical metaphor for the laboratory, as Vulcan was the god of fire and smithing.</note>, from my fifteenth year of age onward, I have labored untiringly, at costs (certainly) not small, yet (thanks be to **God**) my own; alone and with companions, both those faithful to me and the unfaithful, sometimes skillfully, sometimes clumsily. For how can one do well who has never done poorly? Things that harmed me taught me. I observed what Nature taught (with Art acting as the midwife): O, most fruitful <term>Physico-Chemical Cabala</term> <note>A term Khunrath uses to describe the intersection of spiritual revelation (Cabala) and experimental science (Physics/Chemistry).</note>! I diligently noted down the discourses and labors, both my own and those of others, and the concepts of my foreboding mind. 

When you lazy fathers were snoring, I was awake and working. Let their way be dark and slippery, with the Angel of the Lord pursuing them.* And Psalm 91, verse 10 and following: *No evil shall befall you, nor shall any plague come near your dwelling. For he has given his Angels charge over you, to keep you in all your ways. In their hands they shall bear you up, lest you dash your foot against a stone.* With these counsels, I approach GOD by praying, observing GOD responding to me.

<margin>300</margin>
| | | |
|:---|:---:|:---|
| For **GOD** loves no one, except him who has intimacy with Wisdom. | Verse 28 <note>Wisdom of Solomon 7:28.</note> | For **GOD** loves no one, except him who dwells with **WISDOM**. |
<margin>300 In order that GOD might love us, let us seek WISDOM.</margin>

"GOD loves no one, except..." etc.] This voice of the Wise Man (I call GOD to witness) struck my soul as I was reading. Good **GOD**, what is this? That GOD loves no one except him who dwells with WISDOM? Now, no one dwells with WISDOM except he who walks in her ways; who loves GOD with all his heart and his Neighbor as himself; who seeks first and before all things the kingdom of GOD; who fears GOD and works righteousness—that is, a <term>THEOSOPHER</term> <note>original: "TEOSOPHVS." A practitioner of "Theosophy," which Khunrath defines as the practical, divinely-inspired wisdom that combines religious piety with the study of nature (alchemy/physics).</note>, who alone is an inhabitant of true WISDOM, obedient to his wonderful mistress, and entirely dedicated to and serving her alone (in Body, Spirit, and Soul); or at least striving to do so. Verse 1: It requires the whole man. No one can serve two masters: Eternal WISDOM and the unclean world. It is said in this study—so pious, so holy, so honorably fruitful for both neighbor and ourselves: The world's **friend** <note>original: "Freund"</note> / is **GOD's enemy** <note>original: "DEVS Feind"</note> / and vice versa. James 4:4.

# INTERPRETATIONS

| | | |
|:---|:---:|:---|
| When a man’s ways please the LORD, he will turn even his enemies to peace. | Verse 7. | When the ways of a man please the Lord, he will make even his enemies peaceful toward him. |

*Since they please, etc.* To please the LORD, walk in the ways of WISDOM (verse 7). For GOD loves no one except those with whom WISDOM dwells (verse 300). And then the LORD will compel your enemies to enter into peace with you, or he will scatter them by the Spirit of his power, as written in the Wisdom of Solomon, chapter 11, verse 21. For this reason Achior, the leader of the children of Ammon, says in Judith 5:17 and 19: *There was no one to insult this people, except when they departed from the worship* of the LORD their God. But as often as they repented for having departed from the worship of their God, GOD gave them the power to resist.

<margin>302</margin>

*Teacher, etc.* Teacher, selector, and inventor of the Knowledge <note>original: "Scientiæ"</note> of the works of GOD, and like a certain Priestess and most skillful Mistress, both for investigating and finding the mysteries of Holy Scripture and the secrets of Nature, as well as DISCIPLINE—that is, the FEAR OF GOD (verses 14, 5, and 158).

<margin>303</margin>

*If riches are sought, etc.* Yet not so that you might become proud from them, or make them a worldly thing for the sake of the world; but so that you may live honorably and be the Almoner of GOD <note>A person who distributes alms or charity on behalf of a religious house or personage.</note> in this great hospital, coming to the aid of your needy Neighbor. If you desire riches for this end, go wisely to true WISDOM: she will give to the Wise from the labors of your hands in the LABORATORY <note>original: "LABORATORIO"; in this context, it refers to both a place of physical chemical work and spiritual labor</note>, from which you also may be able to give in the place of GOD. See verses 291, 317, and 319. Riches, through the labors of WISDOM, are a Gift of GOD (verse 326). *Which works ALL THINGS.* Because she is ALL in All, and in All things (verse 299). The sense of these few words is very broad—indeed, infinite. Practice the labors of the mind here Theo-Sophically <note>original: "Theo-Sophicè"; a term used by Khunrath to describe a blend of divine wisdom, philosophy, and alchemy</note>, according to the teaching of this Amphitheater <note>Referring to the author’s work, *The Amphitheatre of Eternal Wisdom*</note>; you will experience wonders. See verse 137. From the knowledge, possession, and enjoyment of these things, true Philosophers have despised the unclean world. Hence the saying of Morienus the Roman <note>A famous, possibly legendary, alchemist of the 7th century</note>: *All those who have ALL THINGS with them do not need outside help.* And of Philip Theophrastus Paracelsus <note>The influential 16th-century Swiss-German physician and alchemist</note>: *Let no man belong to another who can be his own.* Golden liberty!

# THE SIXTH STEP.

V 3
<meta>image quality: clear; catchword: ENTIA (referring to Sapientia/Wisdom)</meta>

| | | |
|:---|:---:|:---|
| Is anyone more of a ☞ craftswoman than She? | | What in the nature of things is more skillfully made? |

---

**But if sense, etc.]** If anything can be performed or achieved through sense, reason, prudence, intellect, or art, what in the nature of things is more skillful than SHE (who gives, knows, understands, and works ALL things), or what more skillful can be found? **The Craftswoman <note>original: "Artifex"</note>.]** For she is (as Experience proves) the maker of all things that are and become Good, whether in Nature or in life. Therefore, set Her over yourself, as well as over your Oratory and your Laboratory <note>The "Oratorio ac Laboratorio" is a central concept in this work, representing the balance between prayer (oratory) and practical work or alchemy (laboratory).</note>: so that a familiar Spirit may be present to you, to teach, lead, and guard you, and grant that you may know, will, be, and be able to act well in ALL things.

---

| | | |
|:---|:---:|:---|
| <margin>305</margin> And if someone loves Justice: her labors are virtues: for she teaches Temperance, and Prudence, Justice and Fortitude, than which nothing is more useful to men in life. | Verse 7. | <margin>305</margin> And ☞ if someone loves JUSTICE; her labors have great virtues: ☞ for she teaches ☞ SOBRIETY, ☞ PRUDENCE, ☞ JUSTICE, and ☞ VIRTUE <note>The text uses "Virtutem" here as a synonym for "Fortitudinem" or Fortitude</note>; ☞ than which nothing is more useful in life for men. |

---

**If someone loves Justice, etc.]** If someone loves that which is just and equitable (verse 81), they shall possess it through the mediation of WISDOM; as is taught in verse 39 and several following. For SHE is also occupied in shaping the morals of men and acquiring virtues, making those who strive to live in conformity with the Decalogue <note>The Ten Commandments</note>. **Sobriety.]** Which is the gateway to all virtues. *A dry soul is the most prudent* <note>original: "Anima sicca, prudentissima." An ancient philosophical maxim suggesting that a mind unclouded by the "moistness" of intoxication or excess is sharpest.</note>. A fat mind tends downward, not upward. Excess <note>original: "Crapula," referring to the distress caused by over-drinking</note> (which the Devil defecates into the little brains of drunkards) is something more foul than all latrines (verse 79). Hear Paul to the Ephesians 5:18. *Do not,* he says, *be drunk with wine, in which is debauchery, but be filled with the Holy Spirit, speaking to yourselves in psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs in your hearts to the* LORD: *giving thanks always for all things in the name of our Lord JESUS CHRIST, to GOD and the Father.* These are his words. A fast <note>original: "Ieiunium"</note> instituted in a Christian manner—with abstinence from excessive food and drink and unlawful pleasures, with mourning and humility of soul, and the confession of sins and prayer simply surrounding Divine Mercy—is like a broom. With it, we are swept and purged for the arrival of the Most Holy guest, entering into his Universal <note>original: "Catholicon"</note> temple—triune, Microcosmic, and renewed (the second figure of this Amphitheater, and verse 218). For FASTING tames the flesh; it gives birth to humility, driving away rashness; it lights the lamp of Chastity; it sharpens the Intellect; it elevates the Mind; it provides healthy counsels; it drives away diseases; and it obtains (by grace) Divine favor. **Justice.]** That virtue which encompasses all virtues within itself. **Than which nothing is more useful, etc.]** For by living in this way, we are established as friends of GOD; otherwise, not at all: because WISDOM will not enter into a malevolent soul (verse 218): Nor does GOD love anyone, except the one who [dwells] with WIS[DOM]...

<summary>This page discusses the transition to the Sixth Step of Wisdom, defining Wisdom as the supreme artisan of nature and life. It emphasizes the necessity of the four cardinal virtues, particularly Sobriety and Fasting, as prerequisites for housing the Divine within the "Microcosmic temple" of the human self.</summary>

### INTERPRETATIONS

<margin>306</margin>

| | | | |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Furthermore, if anyone desires the use of many things, she knows the things of old, and conjectures what is to come; she understands the subtleties of speech and the interpretations of riddles; she foreknows signs and wonders, and the outcomes of seasons and times. | **Verse 8.** | *And* ❦ *if anyone desires a multitude of KNOWLEDGE: she knows the past, and judges concerning the future: she knows the subtleties of speech, and* ❦ *the unraveling of arguments:* ❦ *she knows signs and wonders before they happen, and* ❦ *the outcomes of seasons and ages.* | <margin>306</margin> |

*If a multitude of Knowledge, etc.*] If anyone should desire even the hidden Sciences, secret Arts, and the Experience of many things, <term>SHE</term> <note>original: "ILLA," referring to Wisdom/Sapientia</note> knows the past, present, and future. Not only does she wish to know such things herself, but she is also able—and most willingly and kindly rejoices—to reveal, communicate, give, and inspire her student and brother (that is, her faithful beloved) with successful labors. She does this "theosophically" <note>Theosophically: through divine or mystical insight rather than just human logic.</note> through her more faithful handmaidens or virgins, who are like her chamber-maids (as mentioned in verses 74 and 270), namely the good secret Sciences and Arts, according to the Laws and Doctrine of this Amphitheater. *She knows the subtleties of speech*] The deceptions of oratory and the solutions to riddles; these are obscure and complicated sentences, such as the Queen of the South (or Sheba) proposed to Solomon (see 1 Kings 10:1 and 2 Chronicles 9:1). Likewise, she knows the meaning of Parables, Allegories, Metaphors, and other figures of speech (verse 5). *The unraveling of arguments*] Because she is <term>TRUTH</term>; which is supported by Experience, refuting every sophisticated or fallacious logical argument. *Signs and wonders, etc.*] She does not only know them herself, but (as already said) she opens them to men. How? By the announcement of her "chamber-maid" virgins, who—if I may speak the truth—are sometimes familiar even to me: a Christian speaking to a Christian. *The outcomes of seasons and ages*] For this reason, she can and does establish Prophets (verse 305).

<margin>307</margin>

| | | | |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ☞ Therefore I proposed <term>HER</term> <br>☞ to be brought to me to live with me; ❦ knowing that ❦ she will communicate with me concerning good things, and will be a conversation for my weariness. | **Verse 9.** | *Therefore I decided to join her to myself for the use of life and companionship, knowing for certain that she would be a counselor of good things for me, and a consoler of cares and distress.* | <margin>307</margin> |

*I proposed, etc.*] This is a divine purpose, and supremely blessed. You, O <term>Hhochmahel</term> <note>original: "Hhochmahel," a name derived from the Hebrew 'Chokmah' (Wisdom) combined with 'El' (God), meaning the Wisdom of God.</note>, have proposed the same in me for my sake; oh, keep me firm and fixed in this purpose. Amen. *To be brought to me to live with me*] To take her to myself as a Sister, a Friend (verse 106), or a Bride (verse 146): to associate her with me, so that her familiar Spirit may enter into me (verse 223), into the garden of delights or the Paradise of my mind. *Knowing*] Knowing for certain, not merely opining or guessing. Lack of confidence regarding the assistance <term>WISDOM</term> provides should never fall upon the student of <term>WISDOM</term>; otherwise, he will be frustrated in the goal of his proposal.

-> ### THE SIXTH STEP <-

Having set before me the desired good. Verses 1 & 216. *She will communicate with me concerning good things, etc.*] Knowing that <term>WISDOM</term> <note>original: "SAPIENTIAM"</note>, who sits beside the throne of GOD (Verse 255), has now become my Friend, she will be with me (as a Friend of GOD) in my meditations and soliloquies (Verses 28, 158, 162, 170, 336, etc.) regarding the labors of <term>WISDOM</term> to be established wisely and fruitfully. She is the wisest Counselor, and at once a consoler of cares and troubles: most faithful. For she is "rest in labor, coolness in heat, solace in weeping, a sweet refreshment," <note>This is a reference to the "Veni Sancte Spiritus," a famous medieval hymn to the Holy Spirit often sung at Pentecost.</note> just as the Church rightly sings. Knowing that in times of doubt she will give good counsel, and a welcome solace in cares and troubles. None shall understand these things except the faithful and the experienced; those for whom—once the unruly passions of the senses and purely human reason have been stilled—the <term>LIGHT OF THE MIND</term> <note>original: "LVMEN MENTIS"</note>, ignited by the Divine, falls upon the Intellect, moving the free will to believe: which is the **MOST NOBLE WAY OF KNOWLEDGE**.

What Marcus Tullius <note>Referencing Marcus Tullius Cicero, the Roman statesman and philosopher.</note> wrote so excellently concerning letters in his *Oration for Archia*, ought to and can be transferred with far greater reason to the study of true <term>WISDOM</term>, where he says: *These studies nourish youth, delight old age, adorn prosperity, provide a refuge and solace in adversity; they delight us at home, do not hinder us abroad, stay through the night with us, travel with us, and go with us to the countryside. Even if we ourselves could neither attain these things nor taste them with our own senses, yet we ought to admire them, even when we see them in others.* Thus spoke he. Most happy, therefore, is he who dwells with <term>WISDOM</term>, and with whom SHE dwells.

|----------|----------|----------|
| **Because of HER I shall have brilliance before the crowds, and honor among the elders though I am young.** | Verse 10. | *I shall obtain glory among the common people because of her, and honor among the elders though I am young.* |

*I shall have because of this brilliance, etc.*] The reason is that ignorance is the mother of wonder; and wonder gives birth to brilliance, glory, and honor. For they are ignorant of what you know. Furthermore: since <term>WISDOM</term> herself is bright (Verse 142), she also makes the children of Doctrine and Discipline her faithful and beloved heirs (whose beginnings are in this life, and completion in the future), whether they be young or old in age (Verses 21 & 25); both among the common people and the elders of the people, because of the Gifts and Goods of <term>WISDOM</term> kindly granted to them. For these people are in GOD HIMSELF, WHO WAS, IS, and SHALL BE ALL in All, our true GLORY and victory.

Then all is well with them <note>original German: "Alsdann stehet es wol vmb sie"</note>. For the Wise become Kings through the companionship of the Wise. (Verse 74).

# THE SIXTH STEP

| | | |
|:---|:---:|:---|
| In the multitude I shall be seen as good, and in war, brave. | | *In the multitude I shall appear good, and in war, vigorous.* |

**They will fear me, etc.]** I shall be formidable to my enemies and those who oppose me; and <term>WISDOM</term> <note>original: "SAPIENTIA"</note> (who is with me) will strike terror into them, having been granted to me by the LORD as a bride. **In the multitude, etc.]** Among the common people, I will appear good in times of peace because of <term>JUSTICE</term> <note>original: "IVSTITIAM"</note>, from which "good men" take their name; and I will appear brave in times of war because of <term>WISDOM</term>, which is better than mere strength. See verse 13.

---

<margin>314</margin>
<margin>The Fruits and Benefits of true WISDOM.</margin>
| | | |
|:---|:---:|:---|
| **Thinking these things within myself, and remembering them in my heart: that there is immortality in the thinking of WISDOM.** | Verse 14. | *Reflecting on these things within myself, and weighing them with the greatest care of the mind: that there is immortality in the kinship of Wisdom,* |

**Thinking these things within myself, etc.]** Not in passing, nor superficially, but studiously and anxiously weighing these things—that is, the treasures, labors, fruits, and benefits of <term>WISDOM</term>—in the balance of my heart. Our Wise Author has joined meditation and study with the labors undertaken for the sake of <term>WISDOM</term>; in this, he must be zealously imitated by us: by **Praying and Working** <note>original: "Orando & Laborando"</note> at the same time. One must not labor without study and meditation in the Place of Prayer. **Because it is immortal, etc.]** Here he provides a summary of the benefits of <term>WISDOM</term>, which were discussed at length in the preceding sections.

---

<margin>315</margin>
| | | |
|:---|:---:|:---|
| **And there is good delight in her friendship, and inexhaustible riches in the labors of her hands, and Prudence in the meeting and talking with her, and glory in the communication of her words.** | Verse 18. | *And in Her friendship is good delight, and in the works of her hands is integrity without fail, and WISDOM in the contest of Her speech, and excellence in the communication of HER words.* |

**And in her friendship, etc.]** Three things are here commended to the son of Wisdom. 1. The friendship of Eternal Wisdom; then her Labors; and finally, her conversation. Indeed, no one can become a participant in her labors and conversation unless they have first contracted a firm and inviolable friendship with her. This cannot happen unless unclean worldly wisdom is first abandoned and repudiated. Then, finally, a true, sincere, and <term>irrevocable</term> <note>original Greek: "ἀμεταμέλητος" (ametamelētos), meaning something not to be regretted or turned back from</note> delight can be drawn from the Friendship of Eternal Wisdom. From her labors come honorable riches; from her conversation, prudence and glory.

<margin>316</margin>
<margin>Praise of WISDOM.</margin>

# INTERPRETATIONS

[*The Tree of Life.* <note>original: "Lignum vitæ"</note>] According to the body, Spirit, and Soul: in this life and the future one. Here, the **Tree of Life** can also be understood as the knowledge of **GOD**, of oneself, and of Nature: for these three types of knowledge are the fruits of **WISDOM**. Therefore, one must judge and conclude from the effect and the consequence (as if by a <term>signature</term> <note>A "signature" in this context refers to the theory of signatures, where the outward appearance of something indicates its inner nature or divine purpose</note> pointing the way) that the <term>Theosophists</term> <note>In the 17th century, "Theosophists" were not members of the modern society, but seekers of "divine wisdom" who combined mystical insight with natural philosophy</note> who wisely practice the **Labors of WISDOM**—namely, the Christian-Cabalistic, Physico-Magical, and Physico-Chemical arts—are also enrolled in the register of the righteous. For they take hold of and keep **WISDOM** along with her fruits. *For the fruit of the righteous is a tree of life.* Proverbs 11:30. This applies both passively and actively. This is a great comfort to those applying themselves <term>theosophically</term> to **Cabala, Magic, and Alchemy**. It is a certification of their divine calling.

For where the things themselves are lacking—those things drawn from the true treasures of Wisdom, whether Spiritual, Divine, or Natural—there this poverty of substance either makes a man fall silent in difficult matters, or the mind pours itself out into inept, vain, and foolish chatter and empty talk, which is hateful to **GOD**, the Angels, and men. False eloquence is born from that serpentine cunning, and it has need of many seductive words, colors, and persuasions to deceive the minds of men.

*Then you shall walk confidently &c.*] If GOD, our life, is for us, who is against us? If He sustains us, who shall fail? You need only conceive a desire for victory with your whole Christian heart. You need only take care that you are a living member of the incarnate WISDOM OF GOD, imitating the Archetype <term>Archetype: the divine original pattern or blueprint of all things</term> Theosophically <term>Theosophically: through "God-Wisdom," a spiritual method of understanding the divine and natural worlds together</term> according to the Law and Doctrine of this Amphitheatre <note>referring to the book's title, the *Amphitheatre of Eternal Wisdom*</note>: and thus You, in the body, will be able to do all things through the head <note>referring to Christ as the head of the spiritual body</note>. In yourself indeed you are too weak, but in Him there is nothing you cannot do. This is our glory, this is our victory, this is the Theosophic way of obtaining the power to will well, to know, to be, and to be able, from JEHOVAH, in things Cabalistic, Magical, and Chemical: ALL IN ALL.

*Your sleep shall be sweet*] And while sleeping, in the mirror of a virgin Mind—that is, a mind cleansed from the filth of sins by the washing of repentance—you shall be divinely warned, taught, and instructed by Visions fully filled with life-giving doctrine. <margin>Proverbs 15, 15.</margin> A secure mind is *as if a continual (perpetual)* feast. Hence Augustine says: *A man rich in conscience sleeps more securely on the ground than a man rich in purple robes.* Concerning hypnotic Visions, or dream-like Revelations, whether in prophetic or Divine dreams, take this briefly: The SOUL, free from the mass of blameworthy cares, sober and healthy in a healthy body, Mistress of vices and Queen of affections, in control of itself and having Theosophically entered into itself, by right attempts to attain and explain the secrets of the entire created Universe (because it is a small spark of the DIVINE breath <note>original Latin: "particula aurae," a classical reference to the soul as a divine fragment</note> of the CREATOR of the Universe); to be joined to good Spirits; to review old things; to contemplate New things; to presage the future: finally, to represent the mysteries of the parent and of the parent <note>referring to God as the source/parent of the soul</note> (by the irradiation of the parent) as if in a mirror, by Divine means. In sum: our Mind, joined to the SPIRIT OF THE WISDOM OF GOD, washed and cleansed through repentance, Theosophically raised on wings and sublimated by the fire of Divine love into the *Sanctuary of good Spirits* <note>original Greek: "ἁγιαστήριον" (hagiastērion)</note>, or of the Angels of GOD (which can happen to a man whether waking or sleeping), undergoes spiritual things by receiving them Cabalistically; it contemplates super-celestial things; it sees many Physical things, from and within the hyper-physical (not only by itself, but also with the mediation of the senses and sensible things): moreover, with the lower powers lulled and absorbed—that is, in ecstasy, or an out-of-body experience or rapture into the highest GOD—it experiences the highest things, that is, Divine things; it sees and apprehends ALL things ineffably. It has pleased me to add here the beginning of the *Pymander* of Hermes Trismegistus <note>a legendary Hellenistic figure associated with a body of secret wisdom and alchemy</note> (who was inspired by the Divine Spirit), because of the excellence of its doctrine: *When,* he says, *I was thinking about the Nature of things, and raised the sharp edge of my Mind to higher things, the senses of my body being now lulled to sleep, just as usually happens to those who are heavy with sleep due to fullness or exhaustion: suddenly I seemed to see someone of immense body size, who called me by name, [saying...]*

...declaring in this manner, he cried out: *What is it, O Mercury, that you desire to learn and understand? I am Pymander, the Mind of Divine Power; see what you wish: for I will be with you everywhere. But I answered: I desire to learn the Nature of things, and to know GOD. To this Pymander replied: embrace me with your Mind, and I will instruct you in everything you have desired.* <note>This dialogue is from the *Poimandres*, a foundational text of Hermeticism attributed to Hermes Trismegistus (here called Mercury). The "Pymander" represents the Divine Mind or a revelatory spirit.</note> When he had said this, he changed his form, and suddenly revealed all things. Saint Cyprian in his book of Letters, Epistle 9: *I remember,* he says, *what was shown to me, and what the LORD deigned to reveal to me among other things; nor are those to be considered ridiculous or foolish visions, just as Joseph’s brothers said of him: "behold, the dreamer comes."* <note>original: "ecce, somniator venit" from Genesis 37:19</note> Thus he spoke. And is this the judgment of brothers concerning a brother? How very sarcastic! It is no wonder if worldly brothers pass the same perverted judgment on me. However it may be, it remains certain that those to whom GOD reveals things (whether mediately or immediately) are not to be counted among vain dreamers. Cicero says: *There is something in us that presages and divines. What is that? The Mind; a presage of good or evil.* Many examples, both from our own age and from antiquity, I defer to a more convenient place; I have carefully reserved many things for that more extensive deduction. In place of a concluding mark, I will add this from Julius Caesar Scaliger’s book *Epidorpides*, regarding the truth of dreams:

->*He who denies true dreams, speaks while dreaming:*<-
->*For we have found them not once, but all too frequently.*<-
->*And rarely does a night pass without some perception.*<-

I have brought these words of one most knowledgeable of the truth, not for my own sake, but for the sake of the Thomists <note>Followers of the medieval theologian Thomas Aquinas, who were often skeptical of contemporary mystical revelations.</note>. Oh, what is more blessed than a mind loosed from cares!

*Delivered from hardships]*: First, Wisdom imbues and adorns the mind with the knowledge of many divine and human things, from which the soul is refreshed with sweet joy. | Honor (therefore) the **LORD** with your substance, and with the firstfruits of all your crops. | <gloss>Proverbs 3, Verse 9.</gloss> | *Honor **JEHOVAH** with your riches, and with the firstfruits of all your produce.* | |

From this foundation is built the second Corollary of the third figure of this Amphitheater <note>The "Amphitheater" refers to Khunrath's famous book, *Amphitheatrum Sapientiae Aeternae* (Amphitheater of Eternal Wisdom).</note>, concerning the **TITHE** <term>Decima: the practice of giving a tenth of one's income or produce to God or for charitable works.</term>. ### THE SIXTH STEP.

*Your barns, etc.*] The **LORD** will cause the latter rain of Blessing and the morning dew to descend upon you, so that the floors of your barns may be filled, both Macro- and Micro-cosmically <note>Referring to the universe (macrocosm) and the individual human (microcosm); the author suggests that both physical and spiritual stores will be replenished.</note>; according to the body, Spirit, and Soul; Externally and Internally. And **GOD** will establish you, just like Israel, upon the high places of the earth: so that you may eat the fruits of the fields, that you may suck honey from the rock, and oil from the hardest stone. Butter from the herd, and milk from the sheep, with the fat of lambs and rams, and goats with the marrow of wheat, and that you may drink the purest blood of the grape. **Deuteronomy 32, 13 & 14.**

<margin>Proverbs 5, Verse 15.</margin>
<margin>342</margin>
<margin>He wishes us to live by our own labors and to impart them to others.</margin>
->**Drink water from your own cistern, and the flowing streams of your own well.** | *Drink water from your own cistern, and the flowing streams from the midst of your own well.*<-

*Drink water, etc.*] As if he were to say: use your own Goods and Gifts, not only the external ones, but also the internal ones, kindly granted to you by **GOD**. Do not be a slave or an ape <note>A "slave or ape" (mancipium aut simia) refers to someone who blindly copies others without understanding or freedom.</note> of the opinions of another, such that you are willing to swear by the words and sentences of any Master who deviates from the right path of truth—that is, a foolish man—whether he be a Theologian, Lawyer, Physician, Natural Philosopher, Chemist, Magus, Cabalist, etc.; even if he carries weight before the world due to his antiquity or authority. Believe me, great men commit great errors. *An unlearned man starts his own heresy; the evilly-learned ones are the perverse. Thus age also does not help against folly.* <note>original: "Ein ungelehrter Mann / richt seine ketzerey an / die bößgelehrten / die verkehrten. So hilfft auch Alter für Thorheit nicht." This German proverb emphasizes that neither a lack of education nor high learning guarantees truth, and age does not cure foolishness.</note> Since the power of philosophical liberty has been granted by Divine illumination to anyone, allowing them to philosophize Theo-Sophically <note>original: "Theo-Sophicè," meaning with the wisdom of God.</note>, let each person use and enjoy their own Genius and talent. Let everyone hear, see, and observe **JEHOVAH** speaking, teaching, and responding in the Holy Scripture, in the Book of Nature, and in oneself. Just as no one was ever truly a Pythagorean—as a certain most learned man testifies—who did not perceive the Gods <note>original: "Elohim," the Hebrew term for God/Gods.</note>: so, I say, no one is a follower of David who has not heard the **LORD** speaking within himself (**Psalm 85, 9**), and no one is truly a Christian who has not tasted within himself the anointing of the Holy Spirit of **WISDOM**. **GOD** is no respecter of persons, but (according to the doctrine of the Universal Religion, verses 184 and 304) from every nation, he who fears Him and works righteousness is accepted by Him. **Acts 10, 35.** Therefore, my son, do not lack confidence in the anointing of your own self—that is, of your own person—by the Holy Spirit, while Praying in spirit and truth and living Theo-Sophically. (Verse 10). Each of us, through the working, flowing, and giving of Divine Grace, ought to and can know the Doctrine of truth (provided he himself wills it in a Christian manner, verse 157), so that he may be able to admonish and teach himself and others from **GOD**, and not see only through the eyes of others or hear with the ears of others. And just as it is beneficial for everyone to have food stored at home for the sustenance of their body and family, so it is profitable for everyone to have the Doctrine of Truth ready in the storehouse of their own Divinely illuminated mind, from which they can provide counsel for themselves and others. Behold, my Genius <note>A guiding spirit or inner voice.</note> plucks my ear, warning me of the mangling and taunts of sharp-nosed fools <note>original: "stultorum nasutorum," literally "large-nosed fools," referring to haughty critics or scoffers.</note>. What shall I do? Ought I to keep the truth silent? Far be it: for I know that it is the condition of truth that it always has antagonists, stirred up by the devil, pressing upon the truth but not suppressing it. **Truth** <note>original: "Α'λήθεια" (Aletheia), Greek for Truth.</note> will only make the fools more infatuated.

*Have them for yourself alone.*] Every Good thing is indeed communicative <note>In medieval philosophy, "goodness" was seen as something that naturally spreads or shares itself.</note>, but it is not communicable to everyone without discrimination. This is because all things do not suit all people; there is a specific person, time, and amount, as we correctly and often cite from Nazianzen <note>Saint Gregory of Nazianzus, a 4th-century theologian known for his "Theological Orations" on the limits of speaking about God.</note>. This <term>Talmudic</term> <note>Though the author calls it "Talmudic," this sentiment is also found in the Book of Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 6:6.</note> saying must be observed: *Let your friends be many, but reveal your secret to scarcely one in a thousand.* Even from her who lies in your bosom, guard the doors of your mouth: lest you be saddened on the morrow, for you do not know what the day may bring. Imitate **CHRIST**, who said to his disciples (his disciples, I say!): *To you it is given to know the mystery of the kingdom of* **GOD**, *but to others in parables, so that seeing they might not see, and hearing they might not understand,* Luke 8:10. Mindful of this precept, Morienus the Roman <note>A legendary Christian alchemist said to have lived as a hermit near Jerusalem.</note>, a Christian Philosopher about to depart from King Calid <note>Khalid ibn Yazid, an Umayyad prince often cited in alchemical literature as the student of Morienus.</note>, indeed perfected the highest Good of Nature and Art and left it behind; yet he did not reveal the Science and the Art to him. Hence Alanus <note>Likely referring to Alain de Lille, a 12th-century scholar.</note> says: *Son, set a guard for your mouth before the lattice.* <note>original: "Sohn / setze dir einen hüter / deines mundes / für die Gitter."</note> Therefore, if I too speak secretly about certain more secret things, do not be angry with me: it is not becoming for a Philosopher to transgress the precepts of the Sages, lest the secrets become cheapened, or lest he provoke a Divine curse against himself.

*Of the good*] Of people, that is, those who strive with all their might to be led back to the simplicity of the <term>Monad</term> <note>The "Monad" represents the state of oneness or the primal unity of God; here, it refers to spiritual and alchemical perfection.</note> under the guidance and teaching of the **WISDOM OF JEHOVAH**. Into the actions and labors of these men (not of fools), the will, the knowledge, the being, and the power to do well are inspired by **GOD**. This was hinted at in a few words by the elder Zadith, son of Hamuel <note>Zadith ben Hamuel, or Ibn Umail, a 10th-century alchemist whose "Chemical Tables" were highly influential.</note>, when treating of the universal <term>Physical-Chemical</term> work; however, we have explained it somewhat more clearly throughout the exposition of this Prologue. He who can grasp it, let him grasp it. A great secret lies hidden here, observed by very few. I wish that the fools would become wise by my faithful admonition.

*The Light of the Morning Star.* That <term>Morning Star</term> <note>original: "Phosphorus." This is the Greek name for the morning star, literally meaning "light-bringer." In this context, it refers to the spiritual awakening in the believer's heart.</note> rising in the hearts of the pious is Christ Jesus, the true light illuminating every man coming into this world: he drives out the darkness of the mind; he kindles the light of faith, the flame of charity, the ray of hope, the star of humility, the glow of gentleness, the splendor of piety, the little spark of divine fear, the light of prayer, the radiance of unconquered patience, the star of mercy, the lightning of justice, until that dark night of the flesh vanishes, and the day or the light of the new Jerusalem shines forth in its entirety.

*The dark way of the wicked.* Just as light grows in the pious, so darkness and madness grow in the wicked. For the whole life of the wicked is a night full of ignorance of God and of lasting goods, and likewise of that whole new life by which a man becomes Light in Christ Jesus. From this darkness, then, and the errors and madness of the wicked, nothing can follow but perpetual ruin, and even unexpected ruin, until the final destruction.

->THE SEVENTH STEP. 175<-

## PRUDENCE & INTEGRITY OF LIFE, or purity.

Truly, youth itself does not prevent us from being able to discern just as well, or sometimes even a little better, than certain foolish elders. For understanding comes not from age, but from talent and Divine inspiration. It is not the number of years or the multitude of days that grant true knowledge, but Talent, infused from heaven by the Spirit of the **LORD**, which provides **WISDOM**, even to little ones; as Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite <note>A character from the Book of Job who speaks after the three older friends, arguing that wisdom is a gift from God's spirit regardless of age.</note> testifies with many reasons in the book of Job, chapter 32, verse 8. Samuel, when he was a small boy, received the Spirit of the **LORD**, 1 Samuel 3. Heroic Wisdom, virtue, and success in David were the effects of the special presence of the Spirit of **WISDOM**, the particular workings of the Holy Spirit. For these were not merely gifts of Nature; but in his mind was the Light of the Son of **GOD**, and in his will was kindled the burning motion of the Holy Spirit. He who was not yet twenty years old was anointed by Samuel at the command of **GOD** and filled with the Holy Spirit (1 Samuel 16:13). If all the "wise men" of this world's filth had stood by Samuel then, they would undoubtedly have judged that the older sons of Jesse were more suitable for governing, just as Samuel himself was initially deceived by external appearance. But **GOD**, taking no account of age, nature, or any other fleshly prerogative, handed the kingdom to the youth David; He elevated, fortified, guarded, and helped him, while setting aside the other brothers, whose jealousy David bore patiently. *Of himself he says in 2 Samuel 23:2, "The Spirit of the Lord has spoken through me, and his word is on my tongue."* And *Psalm 119, verses 99 and 100: "I have understood more than all my teachers: because your testimonies are my meditation. I have understood more than the elders, because I have sought your commandments. And verse 130: The declaration of your words gives light, and gives understanding to the little ones."* Solomon in his youth received **WISDOM**, 1 Kings 3:12 <note>original: "3. Reg. 3, 12." In older Latin Bibles, 1 and 2 Kings are titled 3 and 4 Kings.</note>. Daniel, a boy of twelve years, was filled with the Holy Spirit. To the four boys—Daniel, Ananias, Mishael, and Azariah (Daniel 1:17)—**GOD** gave Knowledge and Discipline in every book and Wisdom; to Daniel, however, he gave the understanding of all visions and dreams. And every word of Wisdom and understanding that the King asked of them, he found in them tenfold above all the diviners and magicians who were in his entire kingdom. Sirach <note>Referring to the Book of Sirach, also called Ecclesiasticus.</note> says: "While I was still young, before I went astray, I sought **WISDOM** openly in my prayer; from my youth I investigated her." Ecclesiasticus, last chapter, verse 18. The Apostle Paul does not want Timothy (because he is young) to be despised for his youth, 1 Corinthians 16:11 <note>Paul similarly instructs Timothy in 1 Timothy 4:12: "Let no one despise your youth."</note>. And Jeremiah heard from the **LORD**: "Do not say 'I am a boy': for to all places where I send you, you shall go; and everything I command you, you shall speak," Jeremiah 1:7. And in *Ecclesiastes 4:13* it is said: *"Better is a poor and wise youth than an old and foolish king who does not know how to look to the future."* And these examples indeed are sought from the fountain of the **HOLY** Scripture.

But if one were free to roam to other examples, good **GOD**, what a vast field for speaking would open up to us here! But let us bring only a few things forward. In Alexander the Great (great in deed and name), while still a youth, there was a wonderful power of Nature, by which he surpassed even the wisest elders in counsel, due to the sagacity of his talent, through which he could both best judge present affairs and foresee future events. When the Venetians had sent beardless <note>original: "imberbes." Meaning young men who have not yet grown beards, used here to emphasize their youth.</note> ambassadors to the Emperor of the East, and the Tyrant <note>A common Renaissance term for a powerful ruler or autocrat, often referring here to the Byzantine or Ottoman Emperor.</note> was indignant, as if they had been sent as an insult, one of them answered intrepidly: "Judgment of men and their learning should not be made from age alone; for if..."

# INTERPRETATIONS

...it would happen that the condition of goats would be better than that of men <note>original: "hircorum quàm hominum conditionem meliorem fore." A common Renaissance proverb suggesting that if a long beard (age) were the only mark of wisdom, a goat would be wiser than a man.</note>. However, he whom virtue exalts is not to be rejected simply because he is a youth. How many and how great were the deeds performed against old men by those great military leaders of our own times—**Maurice of Nassau, Sigismund of Transylvania, Don John of Austria, etc.**—who were born for this by a singular celestial influence while they were still young? This can be obscure to no one, unless they are entirely ignorant of historical knowledge. For the Supreme Monarch of the World, **GOD** the Best and Greatest, when He decides to either establish or transfer worldly kingdoms, raises up such instruments and adds authority to them—that is, Fear, Justice, Wisdom, counsel, and success in their endeavors. No mortal, however powerful, can hinder their efforts. For those heroes are clothed and armed with an invincible and supernatural strength. Moreover, the deeds and names of these heroes are inscribed only in the corruptible heaven <note>The physical stars or the astrological firmament.</note>; from which skilled astronomers (I do not mean those common street-calculators, but those who understand the art of the Magi from the East) are able to seek out all things truly and excellently performed and commit them to writing again with much greater reliability—even if all history books had perished—which may seem incredible to the ignorant. On the other hand, the Names and deeds of the Heroes of the Church, whose virtue powerfully exercised itself in their youth and physical bodies—such as Joseph, Samuel, David, Solomon, and Daniel—are written not in the corruptible heaven, but in the eternal one, where they can be read by all the elect. Therefore, a good natural disposition does not require a specific number of years; nor is age waited for in one who both shines with virtues and is powerful in action. The saying from Valerius Maximus (Book 3, Chapter 1) fits this appropriately: *It is unjust for honor not to seem timely for one who is already ripe in virtue.* And our own age is not entirely lacking in examples. For there are (praise be to **GOD**) and are still found today several people whose talent and practical prudence arrived swiftly before their first beard-hairs, as Persius sang in his 4th Satire: *Youths in body, but in mind, elders.* Conversely, the Germans say: **One finds old fools too;** <note>original: "Man findet alte Thoren auch."</note> especially since all places are full of fools. Likewise: **Age does not help against foolishness.** <note>original: "Alter hilfft für thorheit nicht."</note> And, *old men are twice children:* <note>original: "bis pueri senes."</note> why? Because delirium increases with old age, as the proverb says.

[*Gray hair, however, is the understanding, etc.*] <note>A reference to the Wisdom of Solomon 4:9: "But understanding is gray hair for men, and a blameless life is ripe old age."</note> These words are golden and worthy of note, and should be thrown in the faces of those foolish elders with long beards who scurrilously despise youth that is <term>TheoSophically</term> <note>Wise in the "Wisdom of God" (Theosophy), implying a mystical or divinely-inspired understanding rather than mere book learning.</note> Wise and Prudent. Those who are equipped with heroic gifts carry a manly mind and care before their years.

[*Old age is a crown of dignity, etc.*] <note>A reference to Proverbs 16:31.</note> This is most true, even among the Pagans; for as Ovid says in the 6th book of the *Fasti*:

->*Great was once the reverence for the gray head,*<-
->*And the wrinkles of age were held in high value.*<-

Whose age? The Wise Man answers: That which is found in the ways of justice. Those two elders found in the ways of injustice in the story of Daniel, although they were old, were worthily stoned. What advantage does old age bring unless it adds probity and a constant integrity of life—unless men grow old with honesty and Wisdom? I confess, indeed, that a truly wise youth is a "rare bird" <note>original: "rara auis."</note>; nevertheless, such a one has been found, is found today, and will be found in the future.

**A youth according to [his] way** <note>original: "Adolescens iuxta viam." A reference to Proverbs 22:6: "Train up a child in the way he should go."</note>] Spirits of wickedness, of craftiness, of deceit, of perversity, of lying, of pride, of lust, of anger, of blasphemy, of envy, of slander, and of cunning infest the minds of children from an early age. Unless they are brought up with good discipline, in piety and the fear of the Lord, those malignant spirits retain their command and their seat in the foolish mind. Indeed, through scandals and stumbling blocks, they migrate and pass into the minds of children. For just as certainly as malignant spirits are driven out of the possessed by the power of prayer—especially if the possessed person prays and sighs together with them from the bottom of their heart (for the spirit of darkness cannot long endure such power and a praying spirit)—so in truth, through the exercise of piety and divine fear, children are fortified against the hostile infestation of malignant spirits. Therefore, the deceptive and impure spirits strive with all their might to occupy the first seat in a human being. They seek to take root in the will—which is corrupted by natural vice and the stain of original sin—and in impure affections, before any higher, heavenly, and pious education can arrive. Furthermore, just as seeds in the fields grow and mature daily until they turn into flowers and fruit, so the seeds of natural vices, unless they are restrained, grow daily and become one with a person as they age. In the same way, if the seeds of piety and the fear of **GOD** are planted in the mind through a proper education, those also grow and blossom into flowers of piety and the fruits of good works.

# INTERPRETATIONS

*Answer a fool, etc.* <note>A reference to Proverbs 26:4-5, which famously gives seemingly contradictory advice on whether to answer a fool.</note>] When reasonable causes suggest that you should answer, a refutation may be modestly put forward, containing useful things that are beneficial for pious readers and listeners, so that some may be either strengthened or healed. However, one must not engage in a contest of insults with adversaries; in this way, do not answer a fool according to his foolishness, lest you seem like him yourself: for victory does not lie in slander, but in the truth.

*He who [obeys] one who corrects, etc.*] Livy <note>Titus Livius, a famous Roman historian</note> in book 2 of his third Decade writes: *“I have often heard it said that he is the first man who himself considers what is to his advantage; the second is he who obeys one who gives good advice; but he who neither knows how to consider for himself nor how to obey another is of the lowest character.”* <note>original: "Sapè ego audiui... eum extremi ingenii eſſe."</note> Since that first lot of spirit and talent has been denied to us, let us hold to the second and middle path; and while we are learning how to command, let us bring our minds to obey prudently.

...restoring the Image of **G O D**, it is faithful, not deceptive; because **G O D** stands by His promises: to the unlearned, the uninstructed, and according to the world, to fools (1 Corinthians 2), He provides Wisdom, and calms the conscience: He shows the true worship of **G O D**, the infallible promises, with His Sacraments, faith, hope, love, humility, patience, the calling upon and the glorification of the Divine Name.

Know this: Whenever I read, from my very earliest youth, the words of the aforementioned Prologue in the books of the Royal Sage <note>The "Royal Sage" refers to King Solomon, the traditional author of the Book of Proverbs and Ecclesiastes.</note>, this thought always entered my mind (doubtless by the prompting of the voice of **G O D** speaking within me): These things are indeed great and almost beyond belief, which you read here concerning the fruits and treasures of **W I S D O M**; yet they are not at all false, invented, or fabricated. Ah! how will you reach the knowledge of these things? **G O D** knows; I cannot say how greatly I thirsted for the truth. BECAUSE IT SHALL OVERCOME EVERY SUBTLE THING, AND PENETRATE EVERY SOLID THING. THUS THE WORLD

I AM CALLED HERMES TRISMEGISTUS <note>"Thrice-Greatest Hermes," a legendary sage said to possess the three parts of the wisdom of the whole world: alchemy, astrology, and theurgy.</note>, HAVING THREE PARTS OF THE PHILOSOPHY OF THE WHOLE WORLD.
COMPLETE IS WHAT I HAVE SAID CONCERNING THE OPERATION OF THE SUN.

## In German:

*It is the most true of all, this which is BELOW is like the ABOVE /
and this which is ABOVE is like the BELOW: so that one can obtain and perform the miracle or wonder-
work of ONE THING. Just as ALL THINGS were created from ONE THING alone,
by the will and counsel of HIM who thought it; so ALL THINGS spring and come from
this single thing, by ordainment and union. The SUN is its FATHER, and
the MOON its MOTHER: the WIND has carried it in its belly: its NOURISHER or nurse
is the EARTH. This is the FATHER OF PERFECTION of this whole world. ITS POWER
is perfect when it is transformed into EARTH. So shall you separate the earth from the FIRE, and
the subtle from the coarse / quite lovely with great modesty and understanding. It rises from the
EARTH into HEAVEN, and becomes EARTH again, and thus gains the power of the Above and
the Below. So you will have the GLORY of the WHOLE WORLD. Therefore all 
darkness shall depart from you. This is the power of all STRENGTH, the STRONGEST STRENGTH; with it one 
can overcome all subtle things and penetrate all firm ones. THUS IS THE WORLD CREATED. From this 
happen wonderful and VARIOUS WONDERS worked; the way of which,
to do them, is here. Therefore I am named HERMES TRISMEGISTUS, having three parts of the WIS-
DOM of the whole world. All that I have said of the WORK OF THE SUN.*

A Sketch of the **Theo-magical GYMNASIUM**, the macro-cosmic and universal [school], which is the public court of judgment for **NATURE**.
Sea, Waters, Stones, Vegetables, Animals, Minerals and Metals; indeed through all things which are made by the great finger of Almighty **GOD**, exuded either in the womb of the Sea or <unclear>in the bosom of the Earth</unclear>, the Divinity and the essential and real Light of **NATURE** <unclear>shine back.</unclear>
Those ancestors of **DOCTRINE**, the faithful sons of all the faithful, the Magi or Sages and ancient Philosophers—for whom the World is held as a book, as highly-deep and wide-learned admirers of the great World-book of Nature <note>original German: "als hoch - tieff und weit - gelerte des grossen Weltbuchs der Natur admiratores"</note>—do not blush to visit these things (and indeed not in vain) wisely and faithfully by various industries of frequency and example. So that, truly by the Grace of **GOD**, by Divinity and Light, they speak Kabbalistically with men, and are followers [of it], and explain [it]. Partly indeed, through the most sagacious Volcanic Anatomy <term>Volcanic Anatomy: Khunrath's term for alchemical laboratory work using fire and heat, named for Vulcan, the god of fire</term>, of **Physical WISDOM**, as well as **Physico-artificially** there, as if from the clearest fountain of Philosophy, **Praying and Working** <note>original: "Orantes & Laborantes," a reference to the Benedictine motto *Ora et Labora* (Pray and Work)</note>, in mind; they are made; they shall be made. For, by this orthodox and truly Theosophical method of philosophizing, from the Creature <note>Here referring to anything created in the natural world</note>, as if from an illustrious and <unclear>splendid mirror</unclear>, we learn **JESUS CHRIST**, **OURSELVES**, and the inexhaustible treasures of the Divinity and Light of **NATURE**, both physically and through the study of words. Which is impossible for the one-eyed Sophists <note>Khunrath's derogatory term for scholars who use only worldly reason and lack spiritual sight</note>! Here is the peak of Higher Philosophy! Fie upon the slanderer! Invented by **HEINRICH KHUNRATH**.
